When she saw that she supposed that he had not entered because of what he had seen; so she tore down the curtain and took the two bracelets off the boys and cut them, and the boys wept, and she divided it between them. They went off to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, weeping, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, took it from them and said: O Thawban, take this to the family of so-and-so, a household in Medina, and buy for Fatima a necklace of sinew and two bracelets of ivory; for these are the people of my house, and I do not love that they should consume their good things in the life of this world. [3]
45:3: The venerable shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari related in al-Dala'il, with his chain to Ibn Mas'ud, that a man came to Fatima, peace be upon her, and said: O daughter of the Messenger of God, did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, leave with you anything you might favour me with? She, peace be upon her, said: O
45:n1: Bihar, vol. 3, p. 87; Tafsir al-Burhan, vol. 2, p. 364.
46:0: servant girl, bring that palm-leaf sheet. She sought it and did not find it, and she, peace be upon her, said: Woe to you, seek it, for it is worth to me al-Hasan and al-Husayn. So she sought it, and found that she had swept it up among her sweepings; and in it was:
46:1: Muhammad the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said: He is not of the believers whose neighbour is not safe from his injuries. Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him not harm his neighbour; and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him say what is good or keep silent. God Most High loves the good, the forbearing, the self-restraining, and hates the obscene, the foul-mouthed, the importunate beggar. Modesty is of faith, and faith is in the Garden; and obscenity is of foulness, and foulness is in the Fire. [4]
47:0: Section. Al-Shaykh al-Saduq related from Ibn 'Abbas, in a long report concerning the Prophet's foretelling, may God bless him and his Family, of the wrong done to the People of the House. Among what he told was that he said: As for my daughter Fatima, she is the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds, of the first of them and of the last. She is a part of me, and she is the light of my eye, and she is the fruit of my heart, and she is my spirit which is between my two sides. She is the human houri. Whenever she stands in her prayer-niche before her Lord, majestic is His majesty, her light shines for the angels of heaven as the light of the stars shines for the people of the earth; and God, mighty and exalted, says to His angels: O My angels, look upon My handmaid Fatima, the mistress of My handmaids, standing before Me, her limbs trembling from awe of Me, having turned with her heart to My worship. I call you to witness that I have made her partisans safe from the Fire.
47:1: I say: then the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said: And when I saw her I remembered what would be done to her after me. It is as though I see her, and abasement has entered her house, and her sanctity has been violated, and her right usurped, and her inheritance withheld, and her side broken, and her unborn child miscarried, while she cries out “O Muhammad!” and is not answered, and calls for help and is not helped. She will not cease after me to be sorrowful, stricken, weeping — remembering at one time the cutting off of revelation from her house, and at another her parting from me; growing desolate when night falls upon her at the loss of my voice, which she used to listen to when I kept vigil with the Qur'an. Then she will see herself abased after she had been, in the days of her father, honoured. At that God, exalted be His remembrance, will comfort her with the angels; and they will call to her with what they called to Maryam bint 'Imran, saying: “O Fatima, truly God has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds. O Fatima, be devoutly obedient to your Lord, and prostrate, and bow with those who bow.”
48:0: Then the sickness will begin with her and she will fall ill; and God, mighty and exalted, will send to her Maryam bint 'Imran to nurse her and to comfort her in her illness. And she will say at that: My Lord, I have wearied of life and grown weary of the people of this world; join me to my father. So God, mighty and exalted, will join her to me, and she will be the first of the people of my house to join me. She will come to me sorrowful, stricken, grieved, despoiled, slain. And I shall say at that: O God, curse whoever wronged her, and punish whoever usurped from her, and abase whoever abased her, and make everlasting in Your Fire whoever struck her side so that she cast forth her child. And the angels will say at that: Amen. [1]
49:0: Section [the report of the marriage of Fatima to 'Ali, peace be upon him]. In the Bihar, from the Amali of the Shaykh, with his chain, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, married Fatima, peace be upon her, to 'Ali, peace be upon him, he came in to her and she was weeping. He said to her: What makes you weep? By God, had there been in my household one better than he, I would have married you to him; and it is not I who married you, but God who married you, and made the fifth part your dower, so long as the heavens and the earth endure.
49:1: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: Rise and sell the coat of mail. So I rose and sold it, and took the price and came in to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and poured the dirhams into his lap; and he did not ask me how many they were, nor did I tell him. Then he took a handful and called Bilal and gave it to him and said: Buy perfume for Fatima. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, took of the dirhams with both his hands and gave it to Abu Bakr and said: Buy for Fatima what she needs of clothing and household furnishing; and he sent with him 'Ammar b. Yasir and a number of his companions.
49:2: They came to the market, and they would look over a thing that was suitable and not buy it until they had shown it to Abu Bakr; and if he found it suitable, they bought it. Among what they bought was a shift for seven dirhams, a head-covering for four dirhams, a black Khaybari blanket, a bedstead wound [1] with plaited palm-leaf, two mattresses of Egyptian sackcloth — one stuffed with palm fibre and the other with the shearing of sheep — four cushions of Ta'if leather stuffed with sweet rush, a woollen curtain, a mat of Hajar [2], a hand-mill, and a washing-basin [3] of
49:n1: Muzammal: that is, wound about. Al-sharit is plaited palm-leaf with which the bedstead is bound. Al-khaysh: cloth thin in its weave and coarse in its threads. His words “from the shearing of sheep”: that is, of the wool sheared from sheep.
49:n2: Hajar, with the vowels, is a town in Yemen, and also a village that was near Medina; see the margin of the Bihar.
49:n3: Al-mikhdab, on the pattern of minbar: the wash-tub.
50:0: copper, and a waterskin of hide, and a wooden bowl [4] for milk, and a skin for water, and a pitch-lined vessel for purification, and a green jar, and cups of earthenware. When the purchasing was complete, Abu Bakr carried some of the goods, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, who were with him carried the rest. When the goods were shown to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, he began to turn them over with his hand, saying: God bless it for the People of the House.
50:1: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: After that I remained a month, praying with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and returning to my dwelling, and mentioning nothing of the matter of Fatima, peace be upon her. Then the wives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: Shall we not ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, for you, that Fatima, peace be upon her, may come in to you? I said: Do so. So they came in to him, may God bless him and his Family, and Umm Ayman said: O Messenger of God, were Khadija still living, her eye would have been gladdened by the wedding of Fatima.
50:2: And 'Ali desires his wife; so gladden the eye of Fatima with her husband, and gather her household together, and gladden our eyes by it. He said: What ails 'Ali, that he does not ask me for his wife? We have been expecting that of him. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: I said: Shyness prevents me, O Messenger of God.
50:3: So he turned to the women and said: Who is here? Umm Salama said: I am Umm Salama, and this is Zaynab, and this is such a one and such a one. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: Make ready for my daughter and the son of my uncle a room in my own quarters. Umm Salama said: In which chamber, O Messenger of God?
50:4: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: In your chamber. And he commanded his wives to adorn her and to set her affairs in order.
50:5: Umm Salama said: I asked Fatima: Have you any perfume that you have stored up for yourself?
50:6: She said: Yes. And she brought a flask and poured from it into my palm, and I smelled from it a scent the like of which I had never smelled. I said: What is this?
50:7: She said: Dihya al-Kalbi used to come in to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and he would say to me: O Fatima, bring the cushion and lay it down for your uncle. So I would lay the cushion for him, and he would sit upon it; and when he rose, something would fall from among his clothes, and he would order me to gather it. 'Ali, peace be upon him, asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, about that, and he said: It is ambergris that falls from the wings of Gabriel.
51:0: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to me: O 'Ali, prepare for your household an excellent meal. Then he said: From us is the meat and the bread, and upon you are the dates and the clarified butter. So I bought dates and butter, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, bared his forearm and began to crush [5] the dates into the butter until he made of it a hays [6]; and he sent us a fat ram, and it was slaughtered, and much bread was baked for us.
51:1: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to me: Invite whom you will. So I came to the mosque, and it was crowded with the companions; and I was ashamed to single out one people and leave another. Then I climbed upon a rise there and called out: Come to the wedding feast of Fatima! And the people came in throngs, and I was ashamed at the multitude of the people and the scantness of the food. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, knew what had entered me, and said: O 'Ali, I shall pray to God for blessing.
51:2: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: So the people ate of my food to the last of them and drank of my drink, and prayed for blessing upon me and departed — and they were more than four thousand men — and nothing of the food was diminished.
51:3: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, called for the bowls, and they were filled and sent to the dwellings of his wives. Then he took a bowl and put food in it and said: This is for Fatima and her husband. And when the sun had turned to setting, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: O Umm Salama, bring Fatima. So she went and brought her, and she was trailing her skirts, and had broken out in sweat from shyness before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and she stumbled. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: May God spare you stumbling in this world and the next. And when she stood before him he drew the cloak back from her face until 'Ali, peace be upon him, saw her; then he took her hand and placed it in the hand of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and said: God bless you in the daughter of the Messenger of God. O 'Ali, excellent is Fatima as a wife; and O Fatima, excellent is 'Ali as a husband. Go to your dwelling, and do not do anything until I come to you.
51:n5: Al-shadkh: the crushing of a thing.
51:n6: Al-hays is dates mixed with clarified butter and dried curd.
52:0: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: So I took the hand of Fatima, peace be upon her, and went with her until she sat at one side of the portico, and I sat at her side; and she was looking down at the ground out of shyness before me, and I was looking down at the ground out of shyness before her.
52:1: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, came and said: Who is here?
52:2: We said: Enter, O Messenger of God; welcome to you as a visitor and as one entering. So he entered and seated Fatima at his side, and then said: O Fatima, bring me water. She rose to a wooden bowl in the house and filled it with water, then brought it to him. He took a mouthful and rinsed his mouth with it, then returned it into the bowl; then he poured some of it upon her head, and said: Come forward. And when she came forward he sprinkled some of it between her breasts. Then he said: Turn about. And she turned, and he sprinkled some of it between her shoulders. Then he said: O God, this is my daughter and the dearest of creation to me; O God, and this is my brother and the dearest of creation to me. O God, make him a friend to You and devoted to You, and bless him in his household. Then he said: O 'Ali, go in to your household; may God Most High bless you, and the mercy of God and His blessings be upon you; truly He is Praiseworthy, Glorious. [7]
52:3: And in another narration, 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, stayed away three days after that, not coming in to us. Then on the morning of the fourth day he came to enter upon us, and he met in our chamber Asma' bint 'Umays al-Khath'amiyya. He said to her: What keeps you standing here, when there is a man in the chamber?
52:4: She said: May my father and my mother be your ransom, when a young woman is brought to her husband she has need of a woman to look after her and see to her needs; so I stayed here to see to the needs of Fatima, peace be upon her, [and to attend to her affairs. And the eyes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, brimmed with tears.] He said: O Asma', may God fulfil for you the needs of this world and the next.
52:5: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: It was a cold [8] morning, and Fatima and I were under the cloak. When we heard the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, to Asma', we made to rise; but he said: By my right over you both, do not part until I come in to you. So we returned to our state, and he, may God bless him and his Family, entered and sat at
52:n7: Amali al-Shaykh, vol. 1, p. 39; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 94.
52:n8: Yawm qurr: that is, a cold day. Al-qurr, with damma, is cold.
53:0: our heads, and put his feet in between us. And I took his right foot and drew it to my breast, and Fatima, peace be upon her, took his left foot and drew it to her breast, and we set about warming his feet [9] from the cold, until when they were warm he said: O 'Ali, bring me a jug of water. So I brought it to him, and he spat into it three times and recited over it verses from the Book of God; then he said: O 'Ali, drink it and leave a little of it. So I did that, and he sprinkled the remaining water upon my head and my breast, and said: God has removed uncleanness from you, O Abu al-Hasan, and purified you with a thorough purification.
53:1: And he, may God bless him and his Family, said: Bring me fresh water. So I brought it to him, and he did as he had done, and handed it to his daughter and said to her: Drink, and leave a little of it.
53:2: She did so, and he sprinkled it upon her head and her breast and said: God has removed uncleanness from you and purified you with a thorough purification.
53:3: Then he ordered me out of the house and was alone with his daughter, and said: How are you, my little daughter? And how do you find your husband?
53:4: She said to him: Father, he is the best of husbands — except that women of Quraysh came in to me and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has married you to a poor man with no wealth. He said to her: My little daughter, your father is no poor man, nor is your husband poor. The treasuries of the earth, of gold and of silver, were offered to me, and I chose what is with my Lord, mighty and exalted. My little daughter, if you knew what your father knows, the world would look ugly in your eyes [10]. By God, my little daughter, I have not fallen short in counselling you [11]: I have married you to the earliest of them in submission, the greatest of them in knowledge, and the most eminent of them in forbearance. My little daughter, God, mighty and exalted, looked upon the earth with a single look and chose from its people two men: He made one of them your father and the other your husband. My little daughter, excellent is your husband as a husband; disobey no command of his.
53:5: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, called out to me: O 'Ali! I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: Enter your house, and be gentle with your wife and kind to her; for Fatima is a part of me — what pains her pains me, and what gladdens her gladdens me. I entrust you both to God, and appoint Him over you.
53:6: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: By God, I never angered her, nor compelled her to any matter, until God, mighty and exalted, took her
53:n9: Udfi'uhu: that is, I warm it from the cold.
53:n10: Samuja: that is, it became ugly.
53:n11: That is, I did not stint you of counsel.
54:0: to Himself; nor did she ever anger me, nor disobey any command of mine. And I would look at her, and the cares and the sorrows would be lifted from me.
54:1: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, rose to depart, and Fatima, peace be upon her, said to him: Father, I have no strength for the service of the house; so give me a servant to serve me and help me with the affairs of the house. He said to her: O Fatima, would you not rather have something better than a servant?
54:2: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Say yes. She said: Father, something better than a servant!
54:3: He said: You shall glorify God, mighty and exalted, thirty-three times each day, and praise Him thirty-three times, and magnify Him thirty-four times; and that is a hundred upon the tongue and a thousand good deeds in the balance. O Fatima, if you say it every morning, God will suffice you in whatever troubles you of the affair of this world and the next. [12]
54:4: He said in al-Misbah: On the first day of Dhu al-Hijja the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, married Fatima, peace be upon her, to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; and it is related that it was on the sixth day. [13]
54:n12: Kashf al-Ghumma, vol. 1, p. 362; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 132.
55:0: Chapter Three: on the reports of the Saqifa, and what befell her, God's blessings be upon her, after the death of her father, of wrong and of injury. Section. The Shaykh said in Talkhis al-Shafi, and al-Tabrisi in al-Ihtijaj, and Ibn Abi al-Hadid in his commentary on the Nahj, from the Book of the Saqifa of Ahmad b. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Jawhari, what may be summarised thus: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, the Ansar gathered in the portico of Banu Sa'ida and brought out Sa'd b. 'Ubada to appoint him to the caliphate — and he was ill. He addressed them and called them to give him the leadership and the caliphate, and they answered him all together. Then they turned the talk back and forth and said: [If the emigrants of Quraysh refuse, and say] we are the Emigrants and the first companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, his clan and his friends, then on what ground do you dispute the matter with us after him?
55:1: A party of them said: Then we shall say: from us an emir and from you an emir; and we shall never be content with less than this.
55:2: Sa'd b. 'Ubada, when he heard it, said: This is the beginning of weakness.
55:3: 'Umar heard the news and sent to Abu Bakr: Come out to me. And he sent back to him: I am occupied.
55:4: So 'Umar sent to him a second time: A matter has arisen which you must attend. So he came out to him, and he said: Do you not know that the Ansar have gathered in the portico of Banu Sa'ida, wishing to give this affair to Sa'd b. 'Ubada, and the best of them in speech is the one who says: from us an emir and from you an emir? And Abu Bakr was seized with the utmost
56:0: alarm, and the two of them went out in haste to the portico, and with them Abu 'Ubayda b. al-Jarrah. They came, and in the portico was a great crowd. 'Umar b. al-Khattab said: We came to them, and I had prepared words which I intended to deliver among them; but when I moved towards them and went to begin speaking, Abu Bakr said to me: Gently, until I speak.
56:1: Then say afterwards what you please. So he spoke; and 'Umar said: There was nothing I had wished to say but that he had said it. So Abu Bakr began: he praised God and extolled Him, then said: God sent Muhammad as a messenger to His creation and a witness over his community, that they might worship God and profess His oneness — while they were worshipping, apart from Him, sundry gods, claiming that they intercede for whoever worships them and profit them!
56:2: Yet they are only carved stone and hewn wood. Then he recited: “They worship, apart from God, what neither harms them” — the verse. It weighed heavily upon the Arabs to leave the religion of their fathers; so God singled out the first Emigrants of his people for believing him and having faith in him, for standing with him and enduring with him the severity of their people's injury to them and their calling him a liar. They are the first who worshipped God in the earth and believed in God and in the Messenger; they are his friends and his clan, and the most deserving of people of this affair after him, and none disputes it with them but a wrongdoer.
56:3: And you, O assembly of Ansar, are those whose merit in the religion is not denied, nor their great precedence in Islam. God was pleased with you as helpers of His religion and His Messenger, and appointed your place for his migration, and among you are the chief of his wives and his companions. There is none, after the first Emigrants, of your standing with us. So we are the commanders and you are the ministers.
56:4: We shall not act apart from you [1] in counsel, nor decide matters without you.
56:5: Then al-Hubab b. al-Mundhir b. al-Jamuh rose and said: O assembly of Ansar, keep your affair in your own hands, for the people are in your shadow; no bold man will dare to differ from you, and none will proceed but according to your opinion. You are the people of might and of protection, of number and of multitude, of valour and of courage. The people are only watching what you will do; so do not differ, lest your affairs be spoiled for you. And if these refuse anything but what you have heard, then from us an emir and from them an emir. 'Umar said: Never — two swords do not come together in one scabbard. By God, the Arabs will not be content to make you commanders when their prophet is of other than you; nor will the Arabs refuse to appoint over their affair those among whom the prophethood
56:n1: Iqtata 'alayhi: when he acts alone in his own opinion apart from another in the disposal of a matter. From him, may God have mercy on him.
57:0: was. Who disputes with us the authority of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, when we are his friends and his clan?
57:1: Al-Hubab b. al-Mundhir said: O assembly of Ansar, hold your hands, and do not listen to the words of this man and his companions, lest they take away your share of this affair. If they refuse you, then drive them out of these lands; for you are more deserving of this affair than they, since it was by your swords that the people submitted to this religion. I am the rubbing-post and the propped palm; I am the father of the lion cub in the lair of the lion. By God, if you wish, we shall return it a young beast again. 'Umar said: Then may God kill you. He said: Rather may He kill you. (2)
57:2: Abu 'Ubayda said: O assembly of Ansar, you were the first to help; so do not be the first to alter or to change.
57:3: Then Bashir b. Sa'd, the father of al-Nu'man b. Bashir, rose and said: O assembly of Ansar, Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, was of Quraysh, and his people are more entitled to him. By God, God shall not see me disputing this affair with them.
57:4: Abu Bakr said: Here are 'Umar and Abu 'Ubayda; pledge allegiance to whichever of them you will. And the two said: By God, we shall not take charge of this affair over you, when you are the most excellent of the Emigrants and the deputy of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, in the prayer — and it is the most excellent part of the religion!
57:5: Stretch out your hand. And when he stretched out his hand for them to pledge to him, Bashir b. Sa'd got in before them and pledged to him. Al-Hubab b. al-Mundhir called out to him: O Bashir, may you be disowned! You begrudged your cousin the command. [3]
57:6: Usayd b. Hudayr, the chief of the Aws, said to his companions: By God, if you do not pledge allegiance, the Khazraj will have the precedence over you for ever. So they rose and pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr; and what Sa'd b. 'Ubada and the Khazraj had agreed upon was broken up. The people came pledging allegiance to Abu Bakr from every side, and they thronged upon — (2) Al-jidhl: a post set up for mangy camels to rub against and so find relief; and al-muhakkak: that which has been much rubbed against until it has become smooth.
57:7: And al-'idhq, with fatha: the palm tree; and al-murajjab: the one propped with a rajaba, which is a piece of wood with two forks, done when it has grown tall and its load is heavy.
57:8: The meaning is: I am a man of judgement whose light is much sought in such an event as this; and in the abundance of my experience and my knowledge of how affairs come out in such matters and the like of them, I am as a palm tree heavy with fruit.
57:9: The sum of the intent of these words is: I am the one whose opinion is to be taken. (Bihar.)
57:n3: “By God, nothing drove you to this but envy of your cousin” — a variant in Ibn Abi al-Hadid.
58:0: that, and pressed together, so that they began to tread upon Sa'd from the severity of the crush, while he was among them on his bed, ill. He said: You have killed me. 'Umar said: Kill Sa'd; may God kill him. Qays b. Sa'd sprang up and took 'Umar by the beard and said: By God, O son of Suhak — coward in war, fugitive, a lion in the assembly and in safety — had you disturbed a single hair of his, you would not have gone back with a tooth showing in your mouth. [4]
58:1: Abu Bakr said: Gently, 'Umar, for gentleness is more effective and better. Sa'd said: O son of Suhak — and 'Umar's grandmother was an Abyssinian — by God, had I strength to rise, you two would have heard from me in its lanes a roaring that would have driven you and your companions from it; and I would have joined you to a people among whom you were tails, abased, followers and not followed. You have made bold, O family of Khazraj — carry me from the place of sedition.
58:2: So they carried him and brought him into his dwelling. And after that, Abu Bakr sent to him: The people have pledged allegiance, so pledge. He said: By God, not until I shoot at you every arrow in my quiver, and dye the head of my spear, and strike you with my sword as long as my hand can hold it, and fight you with whoever follows me of my household and my clan. By God, were the jinn and mankind to gather against me, I would not pledge allegiance to you two, O disobedient usurpers, until I come before my Lord and know what my reckoning is. When his words reached them, 'Umar said: There is no help for it but his allegiance.
58:3: Bashir b. Sa'd said: He has refused and persisted, and he will not pledge allegiance unless he is killed; and he will not be killed until the Khazraj and the Aws are killed with him. So leave him; leaving him will do no harm. So they accepted his word and left Sa'd. And Sa'd would not pray with their prayer, nor judge by their judgement; and had he found helpers he would have set upon them and fought them. He remained thus throughout the rule of Abu Bakr until Abu Bakr perished; then 'Umar ruled, and he was the same. Sa'd feared the malice of 'Umar and went out to Syria, and died at Hawran [5] during the rule of 'Umar, having pledged allegiance to no one. The cause of his death was that he was shot with an arrow by night and killed; and it was claimed that the jinn had shot him. [6]
58:4: And from Ibn 'Abd al-Barr and Ibn Hajar al-'Asqalani, that they both said: Sa'd pledged allegiance to neither
58:n4: Al-wadiha: the teeth that show when one laughs.
58:n5: Hawran, with fatha: a broad district of the territory of Damascus, having many villages.
58:n6: The commentary of Ibn Abi al-Hadid, vol. 6, pp. 5-11; al-Ihtijaj of al-Tabrisi, vol. 1, pp. 89-112.
59:0: Abu Bakr nor 'Umar, and they were not able to compel him as they compelled others, because of the multitude of his people from the Khazraj; so they guarded against their sedition. And when the government of the people of Islam came to 'Umar, Sa'd passed one day through the market of Medina, and 'Umar's eye fell upon him and he said to him: Enter into our allegiance, O Sa'd, or leave this town.
59:1: Sa'd said: It is forbidden to me to be in a town of which you are the commander. Then he went out from Medina to Syria; and he had a large clan in the districts of Damascus, and he would live each week with a group of them. In those days he was going one day from one village to another, and they shot him from behind an orchard that lay on his road with an arrow, and he was killed. End.
59:2: And from al-Baladhuri: that 'Umar b. al-Khattab indicated to Khalid b. al-Walid and Muhammad b. Maslama al-Ansari that he should be killed; and each of them shot him with an arrow and he was killed. Then they cast into people's minds the notion that the jinn had killed him, and they put this verse upon their tongues: “We have slain the lord of the Khazraj, Sa'd b. 'Ubada; we shot him with two arrows and did not miss his heart.” And Ibn Abi al-Hadid related from Abu Bakr Ahmad b. 'Abd al-'Aziz, with his chain, from al-Qasim b. Muhammad, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, died, the Ansar gathered to Sa'd b. 'Ubada, and Abu Bakr, 'Umar and Abu 'Ubayda came to them. Al-Hubab b. al-Mundhir said: From us an emir and from you an emir. By God, I do not begrudge you this affair, O company; but we fear that after you it will be held by those whose sons and fathers and brothers we killed. — the report.
59:3: Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: I read this report to Abu Ja'far Yahya b. Ja'far al-'Alawi, and he said: The insight of al-Hubab b. al-Mundhir proved true, for what he feared came to pass on the Day of al-Harra, and the vengeance of the polytremendous of the Day of Badr was taken from the Ansar.
59:4: Then he said to me, may God have mercy on him: And it was of this that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, also feared for his progeny and his family. For he, may God bless him and his Family, had wounded the people, and knew that if he died and left his daughter and her children as common folk and subjects under the hands of the rulers, they would be exposed to great danger. So he never ceased establishing for the son of
60:0: his uncle the foundation of the command after him, in order to preserve his blood and the blood of the people of his house; for if they were the holders of authority, their blood would be nearer to protection and safety than if they were common folk under the hand of a ruler from other than themselves. But the decree and the destiny did not aid him, and of the affair there came what came; and then the affair of his progeny thereafter came to what you know. [7]
60:n7: The commentary of Ibn Abi al-Hadid, vol. 2, p. 53.
61:0: Section [on part of what took place at the Saqifa]. Our shaykh al-Mufid said in the Irshad: The people seized the opportunity of 'Ali b. Abi Talib's being occupied, peace be upon him, with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and of the Banu Hashim's being cut off from them by their affliction in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. So they hastened to take charge of the affair; and there fell out for Abu Bakr what fell out, because of the disagreement of the Ansar among themselves, and the dislike of the freed men and those whose hearts were reconciled for the matter to be delayed until the Banu Hashim should be free, so that the affair might settle in its proper place. So they pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr because he was present on the spot. There were known causes by which what they aimed at was made easy for them, and this book is not the place to mention them, that we should set out the discussion of them in detail.
61:1: And the narration has come that when there was accomplished for Abu Bakr what was accomplished, and those who pledged allegiance had pledged, a man came to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, while he was levelling the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, with a spade in his hand. He said to him: The people have pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr; the Ansar were abandoned to failure through their disagreement, and the freed men hastened to conclude it for the man, fearing that you should attain the affair. So he, peace be upon him, set the edge of the spade upon the ground with his hand upon it, and then said: “In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Alif Lam Mim. Do people suppose that they will be left” — to His words, “what they judge.” [1] And Abu Sufyan had come to the door of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, while 'Ali, peace be upon him,
62:0: and al-'Abbas were wholly given to attending to his affair; and he called out: O Banu Hashim, do not make the people covetous towards you, and least of all Taym b. Murra or 'Adi; for the affair is only among you and to you, and none has a claim to it but Abu Hasan. — O 'Ali, Abu Hasan, grasp it with a resolute hand; for you are equal to the affair that is hoped for. — Then he called out at the top of his voice: O Banu Hashim, O Banu 'Abd Manaf, are you content that there should rule over you the father of a camel-calf, the base son of the base?
62:1: By God, had you wished, I would have filled it against them with horse and foot. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, called out to him: Turn back, Abu Sufyan. By God, you do not intend God by what you say; you have never ceased plotting against Islam and its people. We are occupied with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and upon every man is what he has earned, and he is the master of what he has gathered to himself. [2]
62:2: So Abu Sufyan turned away to the mosque and found the Banu Umayya gathered in it, and he incited them to the affair, but they did not rise to it. It was a sedition that spread wide and an affliction that encompassed all; evil causes coincided, by which Satan gained his foothold and the people of falsehood and enmity aided one another in it, so that the people of faith fell short in denouncing it. And that was the interpretation of the word of God, mighty and exalted: “And beware of a trial that will not afflict only those of you who do wrong.” [3] [4]
62:n2: Ihtaqaba: he gathered to himself, earned.
63:0: Section. The shaykh, the excellent imam, the most venerable and foremost scholar 'Ubayd Allah b. 'Abd Allah Asadabadi, may God have mercy on him, said in the book al-Muqni' fi al-Imama:
63:1: A section containing part of what took place in the affair of the Saqifa, that it may be known also how the people built their affair upon driving the holder of the command and the possessor of the right away from his right.
63:2: The authors of the biographies are agreed that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was occupied with washing him and preparing him; and the Emigrants and the Ansar and the rest of Quraysh were waiting to see what would come from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. Then Iblis, God curse him, appeared to them in the form of al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, the one-eyed man of Thaqif, and said to them: What are you waiting for?
63:3: They said: For what will come from the Banu Hashim. He said to them: Go on, and make it wide, and it will widen. By God, if you stand by until they are finished, it will come to be among them and will become a thing of Caesars and Chosroes. And before this a number of Quraysh had written a document of their agreement [among themselves] and deposited it with Abu 'Ubayda b. al-Jarrah, pledging in it that if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, were taken or slain, the imamate should be turned away from the Banu Hashim, so that prophethood and caliphate should not be gathered for them.
63:4: Then Iblis, God curse him, came and urged them on and made fair to them what they came to; and they went off to the portico of Banu Sa'ida. — And he carried his words on until he said: I shall set out, by the will of God Most High and His help, a part of what took place at the Saqifa which cannot be dispensed with and from which there is no escape, so that it may be known how they made light of the religion and how the master of the sacred law, God's blessings be upon him and his Family, was opposed.
64:0: Abu al-Hasan b. Zanji the lexicographer of Basra informed me, in the year four hundred and thirty-three, from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Numayri, from Ibn Durayd al-Azdi; and Abu al-Husayn 'Ali b. al-Muzaffar al-'Allama al-Bandanijini [1] informed me there, from Abu Ahmad b. 'Ubayd Allah b. Sa'id al-'Askari, from Ibn Durayd al-Azdi, from Abu Hatim al-Sijistani, from al-Asma'i, from Abu 'Amr b. al-'Ala',
64:1: that he said: Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali said: News reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was ill, and we felt dread at it and were filled with distress and grief. I passed a night whose stars stood still and whose hours were long, its darkness not lifting and its light not breaking; and I set myself to endure its length, never parted from its terror, until, when daybreak was near and dawn drew close, a caller called out and said: — A grave affair has broken in upon Islam, between the palm groves and the place where the idols were set. — The Prophet Muhammad has been taken, and our eyes pour their tears upon him in streams. [2] — Abu Dhu'ayb said: I leapt up from my sleep in terror and looked at the sky, and saw nothing but Sa'd the Slaughterer [3]. So I took an augury from it and said: Slaughtering and killing will fall among the Arabs. And I knew that the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, had been taken, or was being taken in that illness of his. So I mounted my she-camel and travelled; and when morning came I sought something from which to take an augury, and there appeared to me a porcupine [4] that had fastened upon a yellow snake [5]; and it was writhing while the porcupine gnawed at it until it devoured it. I took an augury from the two of them and said: The writhing of the snake is the turning away of the people from the truth to the one who rises up after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. Then I interpreted the porcupine's gnawing as his gnawing at the affair
64:n1: Al-Bandanijin is a well-known town at the edge of the Nahrawan on the side of the mountain, among the districts of Baghdad.
64:n2: Idhra': the shedding of tears. Isjam: the making of tears to flow.
64:n3: Sa'd al-Dhabih, “Sa'd the Slaughterer”: two bright stars with about a cubit between them, and in the throat of one of them a small star so near to it that it seems to be slaughtering it. It is one of the mansions of the moon. From him, may God have mercy on him.
64:n4: Shayham: the porcupine, the large-spined one.
65:0: and his drawing it to himself. So I urged my mount on until I came to Medina, and its people were clamouring with weeping like the clamour of the pilgrims when they raise the cry of consecration. I said: What is this?
65:1: It was said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has been taken. So I came to the mosque and found it empty; and I came to the house of the Messenger of God and found its door shut, and it was said: He is laid out, and his family are alone with him. I said: Where are the people?
65:2: It was said: They are in the portico of Banu Sa'ida; they have gone to the Ansar. So I came to the portico, and found Abu Bakr, 'Umar, al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, Abu 'Ubayda al-Jarrah and a company of Quraysh; and I saw the Ansar, and among them Sa'd b. Dalham [6], and with him their poets and their leader Hassan b. Thabit. So I joined myself to Quraysh. The Ansar spoke, and spoke long, and did not arrive at what was right; then the people pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr — in a long speech.
65:3: He said: Then Abu Dhu'ayb returned to his desert, and died in the days of 'Uthman b. 'Affan.
65:4: And by this same chain: that al-Nabigha al-Ja'di went out from his dwelling and asked after the state of the people. 'Imran b. Husayn and Qays b. Sirma met him, returning from the portico, and he said: What is behind you? 'Imran b. Husayn said: — If I know, then upon me be a sacrificial camel; from the abundance of the confusion, I do not know who I am. — Qays b. Sirma said: — The community has risen upon a wondrous affair, and rule among them has gone to whoever prevails. — I have spoken a word true and without falsehood: tomorrow the standards of the Arabs will perish. — Al-Nabigha said: And what has Abu Hasan, 'Ali, peace be upon him, done?
65:5: It was said: He is occupied with the preparation of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. So he said:
66:0: — Say to the bald one of Hashim, if the two of you should meet him: you have loosed her roots. — And when Quraysh vied together in glory, you were the one worthy of it, and you were their chief. — And upon you the morning greeting was given, as Commander of the Faithful; yet they did not keep that greeting. — Banu Taym b. Murra broke their covenant, and so took their place in its fires and its blaze. — And they disputed on the day of the Saqifa; and He in whose hand the dispute lies will tomorrow be their adversary. — And on this day al-Nu'man b. Zayd, the standard-bearer of the Ansar, said, weeping over Islam and over their opposing the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family:
66:1: — O you who announce the death of Islam, rise and announce it: the known has died and the unknown has come. — What ails Quraysh? Not upon their heel be it — those whom they have put forward today, and those whom they have put back. — One like 'Ali, whose affair is hidden from them — and the sun is not to be veiled; — nor is a dazzling and lofty knowledge to be folded away: the hand of God unfolds it for him — until they split open a solid mass; and the crack in the rock is not to be mended. — The ram of Quraysh in the clamour of her war, her discerner, her greatest truthful one;
67:0: — and the remover of distress, when its trouble has wearied the one who comes down to it and the one who draws from it. — He magnified God and prayed, when the people of wantonness neither prayed nor magnified. — Their contriving led them to what they came to; ruin upon them — how evil is what they contrived! — And al-'Abbas b. 'Abd al-Muttalib said: — I marvelled at a people who set other than Hashim in command over Hashim, the kin of the Prophet Muhammad; — they are no equals to them in any great matter, nor their peers in deed and in lordship. — And 'Utba b. Abi Sufyan b. 'Abd al-Muttalib said: — The holder of the command after Ahmad was 'Ali, and in every place his companion; — the legatee of the Messenger of God in truth, and of them [7]; the first who prayed, and the gentlest of side. — And 'Utba b. Abi Lahab b. 'Abd al-Muttalib said: — Banu Taym took charge over Hashim wrongfully, and they pushed 'Ali back from his command of old,
68:0: — and they did not keep the kinship of the Prophet, their near kinsman, nor did they begrudge knowledge to him who took charge of them. — And 'Ubada b. al-Samit said on the day of the Saqifa: — What ails the men, that they have put 'Ali back from a rank with which he was well pleasing? — Was he not, apart from them, the legatee? (in verses) — And 'Abd al-Rahman Hanbal, the confederate of Banu Jumah, said: — By my life, if you have pledged allegiance to a man of vigilance in the religion, known for chastity, granted success, — chaste from indecency, of white face, noble, truthful, and long since affirming the Almighty — — it is Abu Hasan: be content with him and pledge to him; for he is not as one in whom there is a passage for a fault. — 'Ali, the legatee of al-Mustafa and his minister, the first who prayed to the Lord of the Throne, and who feared Him. — You would have returned to the path of guidance after your swerving, and gathered of his scattering what had been torn apart. — And the Commander of the Faithful, of the house of Fatima, would have been to you, if a calamity fell, more dutiful and more gentle. — And Zafar b. al-Harith b. Hudhayfa al-Ansari said: — So guard 'Ali about and help him, for he is the legatee, and in Islam the first of the first;
69:0: — and if you abandon him, calamities being many, there will be for you no place of removal in the earth. — And Abu Sufyan Sakhr b. Harb b. Umayya said on the day of the Saqifa: — O Banu Hashim, what ails the inheritance of Ahmad, that it is carried away from you to a foundling and a rope-maker? [8] — O 'Abd Manaf, how can you be content with what I see, when among you are the foremost of the keen-edged blades? — May my mother be your ransom: stand firm, and trust in us and in the help that comes from us, before the deceiver has his way. — Since when have the lineages been passing through your minds? Since when has Taym been coupled with you in the assemblies? — Taym leads 'Adi alongside her, while you are the more entitled and the more deserving of the foremost affairs. — And he also said: — And Quraysh has become, after might and protection, submissive to Taym — and not by the striking of swords. — Alas for my soul, for that which she has won; and there has never ceased to be in her one who carries off the choicest spoils. — He said also: — O Banu Hashim, do not make the people covetous towards you, and least of all Taym b. Murra or 'Adi;
70:0: — for the affair is only among you and to you, and none has a claim to it but Abu Hasan. — O 'Ali, Abu Hasan, grasp it with a resolute hand; for you are equal to the affair that is hoped for. — And Khuzayma b. Thabit, he of the two testimonies, may God be pleased with him, said on the day of the Saqifa: — I never thought this affair would be moved away from Hashim, and then, from among them, away from Abu Hasan. — Was he not the first who prayed towards your qibla, and the most knowing of people in the Qur'an and the sunnas, — and the last of the people to be with the Prophet, and he whom Gabriel aided in the washing and the shrouding? — What is it that has turned you back from him, that we may know it? Truly your pledge of allegiance is the most cheating of cheats. — And these verses have been ascribed to 'Utba b. Abi Lahab b. 'Abd al-Muttalib.
70:1: And Khuzayma also said, addressing 'A'isha bint Abi Bakr: — O 'A'isha, leave off 'Ali and your reproach of him for what is not in him. — You are only the one who bore a parent; and he is the legatee of the Messenger of God, apart from his household — and you were a witness to what was of that. — And al-Nu'man b. 'Ajlan al-Ansari said on the day of the Saqifa, alluding to 'Amr b. al-'As: — You said that the setting up of Sa'd was forbidden — and your own setting up of 'Atiq the son of 'Amr, who was the intimate of Abu Bakr!
71:0: — So Abu Bakr was made fit for it, the best of those who stood; yet 'Ali was the worthier of the affair. — Our desire was in 'Ali, and he is fit for it, O 'Amr, from where you do not know. — He said: When the affair was made firm for Abu Bakr and he came down from the portico in the manner in which he came down, 'Amr b. al-'As spoke concerning the Ansar, disparaging them, belittling them and making little of their affair; and he showed what he had been concealing in himself and hiding from some of them during the life of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. That reached the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, so he entered the mosque and mounted the pulpit and mentioned the merit of the Ansar, and what God Most High had sent down concerning them in the Qur'an, and what the Muslims owe of honouring them and of knowing their rights. So they said to Hassan b. Thabit: You must mention the merit of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and his precedence — and they regretted what had come from them on the day of the Saqifa. So Hassan said: — May God reward with good — and the reward is in His hand — Abu Hasan on our behalf; and who is like Abu Hasan? — You outstripped Quraysh in that of which you are worthy; your breast is expanded and your heart is proved. — Men of Quraysh, mighty men, coveted your place — far from it! The lean is not as the fat. — And you are, in Islam, in every station, in the place of the full bucket upon the rope. — You were angry for us when 'Amr rose with a trait by which he killed piety and gave life to rancours. — And you were the one hoped for, of Lu'ayy b. Ghalib, for what was in him, and for what has not yet been.
72:0: — You kept the Messenger of God among us, and his covenant with you; and who is worthier of it than you — who, and who? — Are you not his brother in guidance, and his legatee, and by far the most knowing in the Book and in the sunnas? — Then the author of al-Muqni' carried his words on until he said: And the authors of the biographies related from Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali that he said: There related to me one who heard Umm Ayman, may God be pleased with her, say: On the night on which Abu Bakr was given allegiance, I heard a caller saying — and I did not see his person: — Truly Islam has been shaken by the loss of Ahmad, and every Muslim among you has wept for him; — and it has grieved him with a grief, that the company of the misguided should have conspired against 'Ali — the guide, the well-pleasing, the honoured, — the legatee of the Messenger of God, the first Muslim, and the most knowing of those who prayed and gave the alms of a dirham, — the brother of al-Mustafa, apart from those who took command over him, and who stripped from him the merit of precedence. — We have set forth, in verse and in prose, that from which the man of intellect may draw the proof that the people dealt with the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, as the Children of Israel dealt with Harun the brother of Musa — sandal matching sandal — so that the case of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and the case of Harun became one.
72:1: And how excellent is the word of Muhammad b. Nasr b. Bassam the secretary: — Truly 'Ali has never ceased to be a trial for the one who profits in religion and for the one who is cheated of it —
73:0: — al-Mustafa set him, of himself, in the station of a standard that followed (9) after the lesser; — he made him Harun among his people, for the sake of this world and of the religion. — So turn back to al-A'raf, that you may see what the people did to Harun. (1) “Lam taku” — a variant.
74:0: [Section] [on what Abu Bakr wrote to Usama b. Zayd, and his reply]. And among what indicates the soundness of the claim of him who says that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was deprived of his right to the imamate, is the letter of Abu Bakr to Usama b. Zayd when he came down from the portico: From the servant of God, Abu Bakr, the deputy of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, to Usama b. Zayd. To proceed: the Muslims took refuge with me, and made me their deputy, and set me in command over them after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family!
74:1: — in a long letter — and when you have read this letter of mine, enter into that which the Muslims have entered into, and give leave to 'Umar b. al-Khattab to remain behind from you, for I have no sufficiency without him; and set out to the destination to which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, directed you.
74:2: So Usama wrote to him: From Usama b. Zayd, the freedman of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, to Abu Bakr b. Abi Quhafa. To proceed: a letter has come to me from you whose end undoes its beginning. You mentioned at the beginning of your letter that you are the deputy of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; then you said that the Muslims made you their deputy, and took refuge with you, and set you in command over them. Had that been so, their pledge would have been in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and not in the portico of Banu Sa'ida!
74:3: And you asked that I give leave to 'Umar b. al-Khattab to remain behind from me, because of your need of him. He has already given leave to himself before I gave it to him — nor to anyone whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded to set out with me to him to whom he sent me. And your own case in remaining behind, and 'Umar's case in remaining behind, are one and the same; there is no difference between you and him
75:0: at all. And whoever disobeys the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, after his death is in the position of one who disobeyed him in his lifetime. You know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded you and commanded 'Umar to march with me; and his judgement for you two is better than your own judgement for yourselves, nor was your place hidden from him. He set me in authority over you two, and did not set you two in authority over me; and to disobey him is hypocrisy — in words which I have passed over here, and which I have set out in full in my book entitled 'Uyun al-Balagha fi uns al-hadir wa nuqlat al-musafir. End. [1]
75:n1: Its full text was transmitted by al-Sayyid Hibat al-Din in al-Majmu' al-Ra'iq, in the fifth chapter of it, pp. 104-107; the copy is in manuscript — see the library of Ayatollah al-Najafi, may God have mercy on him.
76:0: Section [on most of the people not being present at the burial of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family]. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said, as quoted from al-Isti'ab: Abu Bakr was given the pledge of the caliphate on the day on which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, in the portico of Banu Sa'ida; then he was given the general pledge on the Tuesday of the morrow of that day. And Sa'd b. 'Ubada held back from pledging to him, and a party of the Khazraj, and a group of Quraysh. End.
76:1: And our shaykh al-Mufid said in the Irshad: Most of the people were not present at the burial of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, because of the quarrelling that took place between the Emigrants and the Ansar over the affair of the caliphate; and most of them missed the prayer over him for that reason. And Fatima, peace be upon her, rose in the morning crying: Alas for the evil of this morning! Abu Bakr heard her and said to her: Truly your morning is a morning of evil. End. [1]
76:2: And al-Sayyid b. Tawus said in Kashf al-Mahajja, to his son: And among the most wondrous of what I have seen in the book of the opponents — and al-Tabari mentioned in his history what amounts to this: that the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, died on the Monday and was not buried until the night of Wednesday; and in a narration, that he remained three days until he was buried.
76:3: And Ibrahim al-Thaqafi mentioned in the book al-Ma'rifa, in the fourth part, as established, that the Prophet, may God bless
77:0: him and his Family, remained three days until he was buried, because of their being occupied with the rule of Abu Bakr and the disputes over it. And your father 'Ali, peace be upon him, was not able to part from him, nor to bury him before their prayer over him; nor was he safe from their killing him if he did so, or from their digging up the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and taking him out, and saying that he had buried him at other than the time of his burial, or in other than the place in which he should be buried. So may God, majestic is His majesty, put far from His mercy and His care those souls that left him upon the bed of his death and busied themselves with a rule whose very root was his own prophethood and his message — in order to take it out of the people of his house and his kindred. By God, my son, I do not know how their minds and their manliness and their souls and their companionship could allow, together with his tenderness towards them and his kindness to them, this making light of him.
77:1: And Zayd, the son of our master Zayn al-'Abidin, peace be upon him, said [2]: By God, had the people been able to seek the kingship without attaching themselves to the name of his message, they would have turned aside from his prophethood also. And God is the one whose help is sought.
77:2: And al-Sayyid said also: And among his rights, may God bless him and his Family, after his death — and especially on the day of his death — was that the Muslims should all have sat upon the dust, indeed upon ashes, and should have worn the best of what the people of mourning wear of black, and should have kept themselves that day above all from food and drink; and that men and women alike should have shared in the lamentation and the weeping and the afflictions; and that it should have been a day the like of which there had never been in the world, nor ever will be. End. [3]
77:n2: “And our master Zayn al-'Abidin, peace be upon him, said” — in the source.
78:0: Section [on the pledge of the people to Abu Bakr that 'Umar took]. Ibn Abi al-Hadid and Sulaym b. Qays related from al-Bara' b. 'Azib, who said: I never ceased to love the Banu Hashim. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, there seized me what seizes a bereaved and distracted woman, together with what was in my soul of grief at the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. I kept going back and forth to the Banu Hashim, who were with the Prophet in the chamber, and I would look out for the faces of Quraysh. And while I was thus, I missed Abu Bakr and 'Umar; and behold, one was saying: The people are in the portico of Banu Sa'ida. And behold, another was saying: Abu Bakr has already been given the pledge. I had not long to wait when there was Abu Bakr coming, and with him 'Umar and Abu 'Ubayda and a company of the men of the portico, girded with the wrappers of San'a', passing no one without setting upon him and bringing him forward, and stretching out his hand and wiping it upon the hand of Abu Bakr in pledge — whether he wished it or refused. And I did not know my own mind, and I went out running until I came to the Banu Hashim [1], and the door was shut upon them. So I beat upon the door violently and said: The people have pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr b. Abi Quhafa. Al-'Abbas said: May your hands be in the dust to the end of time. [2]
78:1: The author of al-Ihtijaj said, and Ibn Qutayba al-Dinawari in al-Imama wa'l-Siyasa, and others:
78:n1: “Until I reached the Banu Hashim” in another manuscript.
78:n2: The commentary of Ibn Abi al-Hadid, vol. 1, p. 219. Taribat aydikum: that is, may they be impoverished and attain no good.
79:0: When the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had finished with the affair of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, he sat in the mosque, grieving and downcast at the parting from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. The Banu Hashim gathered to him, and with him was al-Zubayr b. al-'Awwam; and the Banu Umayya gathered to 'Uthman b. 'Affan, and the Banu Zuhra to 'Abd al-Rahman b. 'Awf. They were gathered in the mosque when Abu Bakr and 'Umar and Abu 'Ubayda b. al-Jarrah came forward and said: What ails us, that we see you in separate circles? Rise and pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr, for the Ansar and the people have pledged to him. So 'Uthman rose, and 'Abd al-Rahman b. 'Awf and those with them, and they pledged. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, and the Banu Hashim went away to the dwelling of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and with them al-Zubayr. He said: 'Umar went to them with a company of those who had pledged, among them Usayd b. Hudayr and Salama b. Salama, and found them gathered, and said to them: Pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr, for the people have pledged to him. Al-Zubayr sprang to his sword, and 'Umar said: Take the biting dog, and spare us his harm. Salama b. Salama hastened forward and snatched the sword from his hand, and 'Umar took it and struck the ground with it and broke it. And they surrounded those of the Banu Hashim who were there, and went with their company to Abu Bakr. When they were present, they said: Pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr, for the people have pledged to him; and by God, if you refuse that, we shall judge between you and us with the sword. When the Banu Hashim saw that, man after man came forward and began to pledge — and so on. [3]
79:1: And the author of al-Ihtijaj related from 'Abd Allah b. 'Abd al-Rahman that he said: Then 'Umar girded himself with his wrapper and set about going round Medina calling out: Abu Bakr has been given the pledge, so come to the pledge. And the people poured out [4] and pledged. Then he learned that a company were hidden in their houses, so he would make for them with a body of men and fall upon them and bring them to the mosque, and they would pledge — until, when some days had passed, he came with a great company to the dwelling of 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and demanded that he come out; and he refused. So 'Umar called for firewood and fire,
79:2: and said: By Him in whose hand is 'Umar's soul, he shall come out, or I shall burn it down upon whoever is in it.
79:3: It was said to him: In it is Fatima the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and the children of the Messenger of God,
79:n4: Inthala al-nas: they poured forth and gathered.
80:0: may God bless him and his Family, and the relics of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, are in it. And the people found that saying of his abhorrent. When he perceived their abhorrence he said: What ails you? Do you think I would have done it? I only meant to strike terror. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, sent word to them: There is no means for me to come out, for I am engaged upon the collecting of the Book of God which you have cast away and from which the world has distracted you; and I have sworn that I shall not go out of my house, nor put my cloak upon my shoulder, until I have gathered the Qur'an.
80:1: He said: And Fatima the daughter of the Messenger of God, God's blessings be upon them both and upon their families, went out to them and stood at the door [5], and then said: I have no knowledge of a people of worse presence than you. You left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, a corpse before us, and you settled your affair among yourselves; you did not consult us [6], and you did not see any right as ours. [7]
80:2: It is as though you did not know what he said on the day of Ghadir Khumm. By God, he bound the allegiance to him that day, so as to cut off thereby your hope of it; but you severed the bonds between you and your prophet. And God is the reckoner between us and you in this world and the next. [8]
80:n5: “And she stood behind the door” in another manuscript.
80:n6: “And you did not set us in command” — a variant in the source.
80:n7: “And you did not see any right as ours” — in the source.
81:0: Section (on 'Ali's refusal, peace be upon him, of the pledge to Abu Bakr). Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah b. Muslim b. Qutayba al-Dinawari — and he is among the greatest of the scholars of the generality, and he lived in the Lesser Occultation and died in the year three hundred and twenty-two — said in the book al-Imama wa'l-Siyasa, and this is his wording: His refusal, 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, of the pledge to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both. Then 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, was brought to Abu Bakr, and he was saying: I am the servant of God and the brother of the Messenger of God. It was said to him: Pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr. He said: I am more entitled to this affair than you. I shall not pledge to you; rather you are the more bound to pledge to me. You took this affair from the Ansar and argued against them by kinship to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family — and you take it from us, the People of the House, by force. Did you not claim to the Ansar that you were more entitled to this affair than they, because Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, was of you? So they gave you the lead and surrendered the command to you. I argue against you with the like of what you argued with against the Ansar: we are more entitled to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, living and dead. So deal justly with us, if you are believers; and otherwise, take upon yourselves the wrong, knowing it. 'Umar said to him: You will not be let go until you pledge. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to him: Milk a milking of which the half is yours; bind it fast for him today, that he may return it to you tomorrow. Then he said: By God, 'Umar, I do not accept your word, nor shall I pledge to him. Abu Bakr said to him: If you will not pledge, I shall not compel you. Abu 'Ubayda b. al-Jarrah said to 'Ali, peace be upon him: O son of my uncle, you are young in years,
82:0: and these are the elders of your people; you have not the like of their experience and their knowledge of affairs. And I do not see Abu Bakr as other than stronger for this affair than you, and more able to bear it and to look into it [1]. So surrender this affair to Abu Bakr; for if you live and your remaining is long, you are fit for this affair and worthy of it, in your merit and your religion, your knowledge and your understanding, your precedence, your lineage and your marriage tie. 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, said: God, God, O assembly of Emigrants! Do not take the authority of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, among the Arabs out of his house and the inmost of his home to your houses and the inmost of your homes; and do not push away his family from his station among the people and from his right. [2]
82:1: By God, O assembly of Emigrants, we are the most entitled of people to him, for we are the People of the House; and we are more entitled to this affair than you. — And he carried the words on until he said: And 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, went out carrying Fatima the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, upon a mount by night, among the assemblies of the Ansar, and she was asking them for help. And they would say: O daughter of the Messenger of God, our pledge to this man has already passed; had your husband and the son of your uncle come to us before Abu Bakr, we would not have turned from him.
82:2: And 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, would say: Was I to leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, in his house unburied, and go out to dispute with the people over his authority? And Fatima said: Abu al-Hasan did nothing but what was fitting for him; and they have done what God is their reckoner and their claimant for.
82:3: Then Ibn Qutayba said: How the pledge of 'Ali b. Abi Talib, may God ennoble his face, came about. He said: Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, marked the absence of a people who had held back from pledging to him, with 'Ali, may God ennoble his face; so he sent 'Umar to them, and he came and called out to them while they were in the house of 'Ali, peace be upon him; and they refused to come out. So he called for the firewood
82:4: and said: By Him in whose hand is 'Umar's soul, you shall come out, or I shall burn it down upon whoever is in it. It was said to him: O Abu Hafs, Fatima is in it. He said: Even so. So they came out and pledged — except 'Ali; for he claimed that he had said: I have sworn that I shall not go out, nor put my garment upon my shoulder, until I have gathered the Qur'an. And Fatima stood
82:n1: “And more capable of bearing it” — a variant in the source.
82:n2: “And do not push away his family from his station among the people and from his right” — a variant in the source.
83:0: peace be upon her, at her door and said: I have no knowledge of a people present of worse presence than you. You left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, a corpse before us, and you settled your affair among yourselves; you did not consult us, and you did not restore to us any right. So 'Umar came to Abu Bakr and said to him: Will you not take this man who has held back from you to the pledge? Abu Bakr said to Qunfudh, a freedman of his: Go and call 'Ali to me. He said: So he went to 'Ali and said to him: What do you want?
83:1: He said: The deputy of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, summons you!
83:2: 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: How swiftly you have lied against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family! So he returned and delivered the message. He said: And Abu Bakr wept a long while.
83:3: Then 'Umar said a second time: Do not give this man who has held back from you any respite from the pledge. So Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said to Qunfudh: Go back to him and say to him: The Commander of the Faithful [3] summons you, that you may pledge. So Qunfudh came to him and delivered what he had been ordered. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, raised his voice and said: Glory be to God! He has claimed what is not his. So Qunfudh went back and delivered the message [4], and Abu Bakr wept a long while.
83:4: Then 'Umar rose and walked with a company until they came to the door of Fatima, and they knocked at the door. When she heard their voices she called out at the top of her voice: O my father, O Messenger of God! What have we met after you from the son of al-Khattab and the son of Abi Quhafa!
83:5: When the people heard her voice and her weeping, they turned away weeping, and their hearts were near to splitting and their livers to bursting. And 'Umar remained, and with him a company; and they brought 'Ali out and went with him to Abu Bakr, and said to him: Pledge. He said: And if I do not, what then? They said: Then, by God beside whom there is no god, we shall strike off your head. He said: Then you would be killing the servant of God and the brother of His Messenger. 'Umar said: As for the servant of God, yes;
83:6: but as for the brother of His Messenger, no. And Abu Bakr was silent and did not speak. 'Umar said: Will you not give your command concerning him?
83:7: He said: I will not compel him to anything so long as Fatima is at his side.
83:8: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, betook himself to the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, crying out and weeping and calling: “Son of my mother, the people held me weak and were near to killing me.” And 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: Go with us
83:n3: “The deputy of the Messenger of God” — a variant in the source.
83:n4: “And delivered the message” — a variant in the source.
84:0: to Fatima, for we have angered her. So they went together and sought leave of Fatima, peace be upon her, and she did not give them leave. So they came to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and spoke to him, and he brought them in to her. When they sat down with her, she turned her face to the wall; and they greeted her, and she did not return the greeting to them. Abu Bakr spoke and said: O beloved of the Messenger of God, by God, the kinship of the Messenger of God is dearer to me than my own kin, and you are dearer to me than 'A'isha my daughter; and I could have wished, on the day your father died, that I had died and not remained after him.
84:1: Do you think that I know you, and know your merit and your nobility, and would withhold from you your right and your inheritance from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family? Only I heard your father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: We are not inherited from; what we leave is alms.
84:2: She said: Tell me, if I relate to you both a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, will you acknowledge it and act by it?
84:3: They said: Yes. She said: I adjure you by God, did you not hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: The good pleasure of Fatima is of my good pleasure, and the anger of Fatima is of my anger; so whoever loves Fatima my daughter has loved me, and whoever pleases Fatima has pleased me, and whoever angers Fatima has angered me? They said: Yes, we heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. She said: Then I call God and His angels to witness that you two have angered me and have not pleased me; and if I meet the Prophet I shall complain of you to him. Abu Bakr said: I take refuge with God from His anger and from your anger, O Fatima. Then Abu Bakr sobbed and wept until his soul was near to departing.
84:4: And she was saying: By God, I shall supplicate God against you in every prayer that I pray. Then he went out weeping.
84:5: And the people gathered to him, and he said to them: Every man of you passes his night embracing his wife, rejoicing in his family, and you have left me and what I am in. I have no need of your pledge; release me from my pledge. They said: O deputy of the Messenger of God, this affair will not stand straight, and you are the most knowing of us in that!
84:6: For if this were so, no religion would stand for God. He said: By God, were it not for that, and for what I fear of the slackness of this bond, I would not have passed a night with the pledge of a Muslim upon my neck, after what I have heard and seen from Fatima. He said: And 'Ali, may God ennoble his face, did not pledge until Fatima, may God be pleased with her, died; and she did not remain after her father but seventy-five nights. End of what is needed
85:0: of the words of Ibn Qutayba. [5] And Abu 'Amr Ahmad b. Muhammad al-Qurtubi al-Marwani al-Maliki, known as Ibn 'Abd Rabbih al-Andalusi, who died in the year three hundred and twenty-eight — and he is among the greatest of the scholars of the Sunnis — said in the second volume of the book al-'Iqd al-Farid, which is among the delightful books, and this is his wording: Those who held back from the pledge to Abu Bakr. As for 'Ali and al-'Abbas and al-Zubayr, they sat in the house of Fatima, peace be upon her, until Abu Bakr sent 'Umar b. al-Khattab to them, to bring them out of the house of Fatima, peace be upon her; and he said to him: If they refuse, then fight them. So he came forward with a brand of fire, to set the house ablaze upon them; and Fatima, peace be upon her, met him and said: O son of al-Khattab, have you come to burn our house? He said: Yes, or else you enter into what the community has entered into. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, went out until he came in to Abu Bakr and pledged to him. End. [6]
85:1: And al-Mas'udi mentioned in Muruj al-Dhahab, in the reports of 'Abd Allah b. al-Zubayr, that he set upon those of the Banu Hashim who were in Mecca and besieged them in the ravine, and gathered for them a great quantity of firewood such that, had a spark of fire fallen into it, not one would have escaped death; and among the people was Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya. Then he mentioned the coming of Abu 'Abd Allah al-Jadali with four thousand from Kufa on the part of al-Mukhtar, and their bringing the Banu Hashim out of the ravine.
85:2: Al-Mas'udi said: And al-Nawfali related in his book of reports, from Ibn 'A'isha, from his father, from Hammad b. Salama, who said: 'Urwa b. al-Zubayr used to excuse his brother when the mention of the Banu Hashim came up, and his besieging them in the ravine and his gathering the firewood to burn them, and he would say: He only meant by that to terrify them, that they might enter into obedience to him — just as the Banu Hashim were terrified and firewood was gathered for them, to burn them, when they refused the pledge in time past. This is a report which does not bear mentioning here; and we have given an account of it in our book on the merits of the People of the House and their reports, entitled Hada'iq al-Adhhan. End. [7]
85:n7: Muruj al-Dhahab, vol. 2, p. 100, Egyptian edition.
86:0: Our master al-Murtada, 'Alam al-Huda, may his secret be sanctified, said in al-Shafi, in refuting the words of the Chief Judge concerning the report of the burning, and this is his wording, upon him be mercy: The report of the burning has been related by other than the Shi'a, by those who are not suspect in the eyes of the people; and to reject narrations without an argument avails nothing. [8]
86:1: For al-Baladhuri related — and his standing in trustworthiness among the generality, and his distance from any closeness to the Shi'a, and his exactness in what he relates, are well known — from al-Mada'ini, from Salama b. Muharib, from Salman al-Laythi [9], from Ibn 'Awn: that Abu Bakr sent to 'Ali, peace be upon him, seeking to compel him to the pledge; and he did not pledge. So 'Umar came, and with him a brand of fire; and Fatima met him at the door and said: O son of al-Khattab, do I see you about to burn my house down upon me?
86:2: He said: Yes; and that is stronger for what your father brought. And 'Ali came and pledged. [10]
86:3: And this report the Shi'a have related by many paths; but the remarkable thing is that the shaykhs of the traditionists of the generality should relate it.
86:4: And Ibrahim b. Sa'id al-Thaqafi related, with his chain, from Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said: By God, 'Ali, peace be upon him, did not pledge until he saw the smoke had entered his house. [11]
86:5: And al-Sayyid b. Tawus said in Kashf al-Mahajja, in the mention of Abu Bakr and his holding back from the army of Usama: And his usurping of the caliphate on the day of the Saqifa. And I say: that did not suffice him, until he sent 'Umar to the door of your father 'Ali and your mother Fatima, peace be upon them, and with them were al-'Abbas and a company of the Banu Hashim, and they were occupied with the death of your grandfather Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, and with the mourning and the great afflictions; and he commanded that they be burned with fire if they did not come out for the pledge — according to what the author of the book al-'Iqd al-Farid mentioned in the fourth part of it, and a company of those who are not suspect in their narration.
