And it is a thing which, so far as I know, none reached before him nor after him, of the prophets or the legatees, nor of the kings known for force and harshness, nor the kings of the unbelievers — that they should send men to burn those who held back from their pledge with the burning of fire, in addition to the threat of killing
86:n8: Al-Shafi, p. 240, old edition; new edition, vol. 4, p. 112.
87:0: and of beating. I say: Nor has it reached us that any of the kings had a prophet, or that any king had an authority who had enriched them after poverty and delivered them from abasement and harm and guided them to the happiness of this world and the next, and opened for them by his prophethood the lands of the tyrants; then he died and left among them one daughter of his loins, and said to them: She is the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds — and two little ones with her, of hers, under seven years of age or near to it; and that the recompense of that prophet or that king from his subjects should be that they bring fire to burn his two sons and the person of his daughter, while they stand in the place of his spirit and his heart's blood. End. [12]
87:1: The author of al-Ihtijaj related from Ahmad b. Hammam, who said: I came to 'Ubada b. al-Samit during the rule of Abu Bakr and said: O Abu 'Umara [13], were the people upon preferring Abu Bakr before he was made deputy?
87:2: He said: O Abu Tha'laba, when we keep silent about you, then keep silent, and do not probe [14]. For by God, 'Ali b. Abi Talib was more entitled to the caliphate than Abu Bakr, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was more entitled to prophethood than Abu Jahl. He said: And I shall tell you more. We were one day with the Messenger of God when 'Ali and Abu Bakr and 'Umar came to the door of the Messenger of God. Abu Bakr entered, then 'Umar entered, then 'Ali, peace be upon him, entered after them; and it was as though ashes had been blown [15] upon the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. Then he said: O 'Ali, do these two go before you, when God has set you in command over them? Abu Bakr said: I forgot, O Messenger of God. And 'Umar said: I was heedless, O Messenger of God.
87:3: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: You did not forget, nor were you heedless. It is as though I see you two having seized his rule and warred over it, and the enemies of God and the enemies of His Messenger having helped you in that; and it is as though I see you two having left the Emigrants and the Ansar, some of them striking the faces of others with the sword over this world;
87:4: and it is as though I see the people of my house, and they are the overpowered, scattered in its regions — and that is for a matter that has been decreed.
87:n14: “And do not probe us” in another manuscript.
87:n15: Safat al-rih al-turab: when it scatters it.
88:0: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, wept until his tears flowed, and then said: O 'Ali, patience, patience, until the command comes down; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. For you shall have of reward, on every day, what your two recording angels cannot number. And when the matter is within your power, then the sword, the sword; then the slaying, the slaying — until they return to the command of God and the command of His Messenger. For you are upon the truth, and whoever opposes you is upon falsehood; and so likewise your progeny after you, until the Day of Resurrection. (16) (1) Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, p. 291.
89:0: Section (on words that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, spoke to Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with him). Al-Shaykh al-Saduq related, with his chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The caliphate was mentioned before the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, and he said: By God, the brother of Taym put it on like a shirt — the sermon; and we give it here as it stands in the Nahj al-Balagha. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: By God, so-and-so put it on like a shirt, and he knew well that my place in relation to it is the place of the axle to the mill: the flood pours down away from me, and no bird rises to me. So I let a garment down before it and turned my flank away from it, and I set to considering whether I should strike with a severed hand, or endure a blinding darkness in which the old grow decrepit and the young grow grey and a believer toils until he meets his Lord.
89:1: And I saw that patience in this was the wiser course. So I was patient, and in the eye was a mote and in the throat a choking, seeing my inheritance plundered — until the first went his way and handed it on to so-and-so after him. [1] Then he recited the words of al-A'sha: — How far apart are my day upon her saddle and the day of Hayyan, the brother of Jabir. — And oh, the wonder of it! While he was asking to be released from it in his lifetime, he bound it for another after his death. How hard the two of them shared
89:n1: Thus in both copies of the book; but in the printed Nahj al-Balagha: “to the son of al-Khattab after him”.
90:0: its udders! So he set it in a rough enclosure, whose wounding is harsh and whose touch is rough, in which stumbling is frequent and the excusing of it frequent. Its companion is as the rider of a difficult mount: if he pulls her rein tight he tears her nose, and if he slackens it she plunges headlong. So the people were afflicted, by the life of God, with blundering and with restiveness, with fickleness and with turning aside. Yet I was patient through the length of the period and the severity of the trial,
90:1: until, when he had gone his way, he set it in a company, claiming that I was one of them. God! and what a council! When did doubt ever fall upon me concerning the first of them, that I should come to be reckoned among these peers? But I sank low when they sank low and flew when they flew. One of them inclined aside for his rancour, and the other bent for his kinship by marriage, together with this and that.
90:2: — until the third of the people rose, puffing out his two flanks between his dung-heap and his fodder; and the sons of his father rose with him, devouring the wealth of God as camels devour the herbage of spring, until his rope unravelled upon him, and his own deeds finished him, and his gluttony brought him down.
90:3: Then nothing startled me but the people, like the hyena's mane, pressing in upon me, pouring upon me from every side, until al-Hasan and al-Husayn were trodden underfoot and my two flanks were torn, gathered about me like a flock of sheep. Then when I rose with the affair, one party broke faith, another went out of it, and others deviated — as though they had not heard the word of God, glory be to Him, where He says: “That is the abode of the hereafter; We appoint it for those who desire neither exaltation in the earth nor corruption; and the outcome is for the God-fearing.” Nay, by God, they had heard it and grasped it; but the world was made sweet in their eyes and its ornament dazzled them.
90:4: But by Him who split the seed and created the soul, were it not for the presence of the one present, and the establishing of the proof by the existence of a helper, and what God has taken upon the scholars — that they should not acquiesce in the gluttony of a wrongdoer nor in the hunger of the wronged — I would have cast its rope upon its own withers, and watered its last with the cup of its first; and you would have found this world of yours of less worth to me than the sneeze of a goat.
90:5: They said: And a man of the people of the Sawad rose to him when he had reached this point in his sermon, and handed him a letter; and he began to look into it. When he had finished reading it, Ibn 'Abbas, may God have mercy on him, said to him: O
91:0: Commander of the Faithful, if only you would carry your words on from where you left off. He said: Far from it, Ibn 'Abbas. That was a froth of the camel's rage: it bubbled up, and then it subsided. Ibn 'Abbas said: By God, I have never grieved over any speech as I grieved over this speech, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, did not reach in it the point he intended. [2]
91:1: Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: As for Ibn 'Abbas's words, “I never grieved over any speech” — my shaykh Abu al-Khayr Musaddiq b. Shabib al-Wasiti related to me in the year six hundred and three, saying: I read this sermon to the shaykh Abu Muhammad 'Abd Allah b. Ahmad, known as Ibn al-Khashshab; and when I reached this place he said to me: Had I heard Ibn 'Abbas say this, I would have said to him: And did there remain in your cousin's soul any matter he did not reach in this sermon, that you should grieve he did not attain of his speech what he intended? By God, he spared neither the first of them nor the last. [3]
91:2: And in the Bihar, from Kashf al-Yaqin, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: I used to watch for the anger of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, when he mentioned something, or when a report stirred him. Then one day some of his partisans in Syria wrote to him, mentioning in his letter that Mu'awiya, 'Amr b. al-'As, 'Utba b. Abi Sufyan, al-Walid b. 'Uqba and Marwan had gathered before Mu'awiya and had mentioned the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and reviled him, and had put about among the people that he disparages the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and mentions each one of them with what he deserves.
91:3: And that was when he, peace be upon him, had ordered his companions to wait for him at al-Nukhayla, and they entered Kufa and left him; and that weighed heavily upon him.
91:4: And this report came; so I came to his door by night and said: O Qanbar, what is the news of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him? He said: He is asleep. But he, peace be upon him, heard my words and said: Who is this?
91:5: I said: Ibn 'Abbas, O Commander of the Faithful. He said: Enter. So I entered, and there he was, seated apart from his bed in a single garment, in the posture of one troubled. I said: What ails you this night, Commander of the Faithful? He said: Woe to you, Ibn 'Abbas; and how
91:n2: Nahj al-Balagha, vol. 1, pp. 37-44; Nahj al-Balagha (Subhi), p. 48.
91:n3: The commentary of Ibn Abi al-Hadid, p. 205.
92:0: should the eyes sleep of one whose heart is occupied? O Ibn 'Abbas, your heart is the king of your limbs; and when it is made afraid, sleep flies from it. Here I am, as you see, since the beginning of the night: thought and sleeplessness have seized me, for what has gone before of the breaking of the covenant of the first of this community, for whom the breaking of her covenant was decreed.
92:1: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded those whom he commanded of his companions to greet me in his lifetime as Commander of the Faithful; and I was made certain that I should be so after his death. O Ibn 'Abbas, I am the most entitled of people to the people after him; but matters combined upon the people's desire for this world, and its commanding and its forbidding, and the turning of the hearts of its people away from me.
92:2: I say: and he carried his words on, peace be upon him, in complaint of those who went before him, until he said, peace be upon him: And now, Ibn 'Abbas, I am coupled with the son of the eater of livers, and with 'Amr and 'Utba and al-Walid and Marwan and their followers. When did it ever stir in my breast, or fall into my mind, that the affair would be led away to a world in which these should be chiefs, obeyed? And here they are, at the remembrance of the friends of the Merciful, disparaging them [4] and casting at them enormities, of forged calumny and of rancour long preceding.
92:3: And those entrusted with its keeping, of those who remain of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, know well that the generality of my enemies are of those who answered Satan against me, and whom the people made to shine, and who obeyed his own desire in what harms him in his hereafter. And in God, mighty and exalted, is sufficiency; and He is the granter of right guidance and of soundness. O Ibn 'Abbas, woe to him who wronged me and pushed away my right and did away with the greatness of my station. Where were those men,
92:4: while I was praying with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, a small boy upon whom no prayer was yet enjoined — and they were worshippers of idols and rebels against the Merciful, and by them the fires are kindled?
92:5: Then, when the turning aside of cheeks [5] and the wretchedness of fortunes drew near, they submitted unwillingly and concealed other than what they showed, coveting to put out the light of God; and they waited for the ending of the Messenger's affair and the passing of his term, when
92:n5: Sa'ara khaddahu tas'iran, and sa'arahu, and as'arahu: he turned it away from looking at people out of disdain. Al-ta's: perdition. And al-judud is the plural of al-jadd, with fatha, meaning fortune.
93:0: they had made their souls covet his killing, and their counsel in their house of assembly. God, mighty and exalted, said: “And they schemed, and God schemed; and God is the best of schemers.” [6] And He said: “They wish to put out the light of God with their mouths, and God refuses aught but to complete His light, though the polytheists be averse.” [7]
93:1: O Ibn 'Abbas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, called them in his lifetime, by a revelation from God, commanding them to take me as their friend; and the people bore what they bore of what the accursed one bore of envy towards our father Adam — so that he went out from the spirit of God and His good pleasure, and the curse was fastened upon him, for his envy of the friend of God. And that will not harm me in anything, God willing. O Ibn 'Abbas, every man wished to be a head, obeyed, to whom the world and his kinsmen should incline; so his desire carried him, and the sweetness of his world, and the people's following after him, to be angry at what had been appointed for me. And were it not for my fear for the lesser of the two weighty things — that it should be cast away, and the tree of knowledge be cut off, and the flower of the world, and the firm rope of God, and His trusted stronghold, and the children of the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds — then the seeking of death and the going forth to God, mighty and exalted, would have been dearer to me than a draught to the thirsty and than sleep to the drowsy. But I was patient, and in the breast are troubles and in the soul are whisperings: “so a comely patience; and God is He whose help is sought against what you describe.”
93:2: And of old were the prophets wronged and the friends of God slain — until he said: “And the unbeliever shall know for whom is the final abode.” And the caller gave the call to prayer, and he said: The prayer, Ibn 'Abbas; let it not be missed. I ask God's forgiveness for myself and for you; and God suffices us and is the best trustee; and there is no power and no strength save in God, the High, the Mighty. Ibn 'Abbas said: And the ending of the night grieved me, and I was filled with regret at its going. [8]
93:n8: Bihar al-Anwar, the Book of Trials and Tribulations, old edition, p. 162 (the conversation of Ibn 'Abbas with the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him).
94:0: Section [the objection of twelve men of the Emigrants and the Ansar to Abu Bakr over what took place after him]. A number of our companions related in their compilations that when the affair was complete for Abu Bakr, and he mounted the pulpit and sat in the seat of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, twelve men objected to that against Abu Bakr: six of the Emigrants — and they are Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As, who was of the Banu Umayya; Salman the Persian; Abu Dharr al-Ghifari; al-Miqdad b. al-Aswad; 'Ammar b. Yasir; and Burayda al-Aslami — and six of the Ansar — and they are Abu al-Haytham b. al-Tayyihan; Sahl and 'Uthman the sons of Hunayf; Khuzayma b. Thabit, he of the two testimonies; Ubayy b. Ka'b; and Abu Ayyub al-Ansari.
94:1: He said: When Abu Bakr mounted the pulpit they took counsel among themselves, and some of them said to others: By God, we shall go to him and bring him down from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And others of them said: By God, if you do that you will have helped against your own selves; and God, mighty and exalted, has said: “And do not cast yourselves by your own hands into destruction.” [1] So come with us to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, that we may consult him and learn his opinion. So the people went, all together, to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said: O Commander of the Faithful, you have left a right of which you are the more entitled and the more deserving; for we heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say:
95:0: 'Ali is with the truth and the truth is with 'Ali; he inclines with the truth wherever it inclines. And we had resolved to go to him and bring him down from the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; so we have come to you to consult you and to learn your opinion as to what you command us. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: By God, had you done that, you would have been nothing but a war against them; nor would you have been but as the kohl in the eye, or as the salt in the provision. The community has agreed upon him — the community that has abandoned the word of its prophet and lied against its Lord. I consulted my household about that, and they would have nothing but silence, for what they know of the rancour [1] of the people's breasts and their hatred of God, mighty and exalted, and of the people of the house of His prophet; and that they are seeking the blood-vengeances of the age of ignorance. — until he said, peace be upon him: But go to the man and tell him what you heard from your prophet, and do not leave him in doubt concerning his affair, that it may be the greater proof against him and the more effective in his punishment when he comes to his Lord, having disobeyed his prophet and opposed his command. So they went, until they stood about the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family — and it was a Friday.
95:1: When Abu Bakr mounted the pulpit, each one of them spoke words concerning the right of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and his merit, and what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had said concerning him — which we have passed over, seeking brevity. The first of them to begin the speaking was Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As, then the rest of the Emigrants, then after them the Ansar. And it is related that when they had finished their speech, Abu Bakr was struck dumb upon the pulpit, until he said: I have been given charge of you, and I am not the best of you; release me, release me. 'Umar b. al-Khattab said: Come down from it, you fool! If you cannot stand against the arguments of Quraysh, why did you set yourself in this station? By God, I have a mind to depose you and to set it in Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa. He said: So he came down; then he took his hand and went off to his dwelling. And they remained three days without entering the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
95:2: Then on the fourth day Khalid b. al-Walid came to them, and with him a thousand men, and said to them: What is this sitting of yours?
95:3: By God, the Banu Hashim have set their hopes upon it. And Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa came to them, and with him a thousand
96:0: men; and Mu'adh b. Jabal came to them, and with him a thousand men. And man after man kept gathering until four thousand men were gathered. They went out with their swords drawn, 'Umar b. al-Khattab at their head, until they halted in the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. And 'Umar said: By God, O companions of 'Ali, if any man of you goes on to speak as he spoke yesterday, we shall take that in which his two eyes are.
96:1: Khalid b. Sa'id b. al-'As rose to him and said: O son of Suhak the Abyssinian, is it with your swords that you threaten us, or with your numbers that you would frighten us?
96:2: By God, our swords are keener than your swords, and we are the more, though we be few — for the proof of God is among us. By God, did I not know that obedience to my Imam is the more binding upon me, I would have drawn my sword and striven against you in God until I had discharged my excuse. [2] The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to him: Sit down, Khalid; God has known your station and has thanked you for your striving. So he sat.
96:3: And Salman the Persian, may God be pleased with him, rose to him and said: God is greatest, God is greatest! I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family — and otherwise may I be struck dumb — say: While my brother and the son of my uncle is seated in my mosque with a number of his companions, a company of the dogs of the people of the Fire shall fall upon him, seeking to kill him and to kill those with him. And I do not doubt — indeed, you are they. 'Umar b. al-Khattab made to set upon him, and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, sprang at him and seized the gathers of his garment and threw him to the ground, and then said: O son of Suhak the Abyssinian, were it not for a writ from God that has preceded and a covenant from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that has gone before, I would have shown you which of us is the weaker in helpers and the fewer in number. Then he turned to his companions and said: Disperse, may God have mercy on you. By God, I shall not enter the mosque save as my two brothers Musa and Harun entered, when his companions said to him: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight; we are sitting here.” By God, I shall not enter save to visit the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, or for a case that I must judge; for it is not lawful for a proof whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has established to leave the people in bewilderment. [3]
96:n2: Ablahu 'udhran: that is, he discharged it to him.
96:n3: Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, p. 97; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, p. 189.
97:0: Section (on the mention of a sermon he delivered to the people). Al-Shaykh al-Kulayni related in al-Rawda, with his chain, from Abu al-Haytham al-Tayyihan, that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, addressed the people at Medina and said: Praise belongs to God, beside whom there is no god; He was living without how, and there was no “was” for Him — and he mentioned his words, peace be upon him, in the praise of God and the blessing upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, until he said, addressing the people: By Him who split the seed and created the soul, had you taken knowledge from its mine, and drunk the water in its sweetness, and stored up the good from its place, and taken of the road its clear part, and travelled of the truth its open way, the paths would have been made plain [1] for you, and the signposts would have appeared to you, and Islam would have shone for you; and you would have eaten in plenty, and no poor man among you would have been in want, nor would any Muslim or protected person among you have been wronged. But you travelled the road of darkness, so your world was darkened upon you for all its breadth [2], and the doors of knowledge were shut upon you. So you spoke by your desires and differed in your religion, and gave judgement in the religion of God without knowledge, and followed the misguided and they misguided you, and left the Imams and they left you. So you became such as judge by your desires: when a matter is mentioned you ask the people of the reminder, and when they give you judgement you say: This is knowledge itself. How so — when you have left it and cast it away and opposed it? Gently: in a little while you will reap all that you have sown, and find the evil consequence of what you have committed
97:n1: Nahaja: that is, it became clear.
98:0: and of what you have brought upon yourselves. By Him who split the seed and created the soul, you knew that I am your companion, and he whom you were commanded to obey; and that I am your learned one, by whose knowledge is your deliverance, and the legatee of your prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and the chosen of your Lord, and the tongue of your light, and the one who knows what sets you right. So in a little while, gently, there will come down upon you what you were promised, and what came down upon the nations before you. And God, mighty and exalted, will ask you concerning your Imams: with them you will be gathered, and to God, mighty and exalted, you will come tomorrow.
98:1: By God, had I the number of the companions of Talut, or the number of the people of Badr, and they your equals [a variant: your enemies], I would strike you with the sword until you returned to the truth and turned back to what is true. That would be the better mending of the rent and the surer taking of gentleness. O God, judge between us with the truth; and You are the best of judges.
98:2: He said: Then he went out, peace be upon him, from the mosque and passed by a fold [3] in which were about thirty sheep, and he said: By God, had I men sincere to God, mighty and exalted, and to His Messenger, may God bless him and his Family, to the number of these sheep, I would remove the son of the eater of flies [4] from his rule.
98:3: He said: And when evening came, three hundred and sixty men pledged to him unto death. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to them: Come with us in the morning to Ahjar al-Zayt [5], with heads shaven. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, shaved his head; and none of the people came with head shaven save Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Hudhayfa al-Yaman and 'Ammar b. Yasir; and Salman came at the end of the company.
98:4: So he raised his hands, peace be upon him, to the sky and said: O God, the people have held me weak as the Children of Israel held Harun weak. O God, You know what we hide and what we make public, and nothing is hidden from You in the earth or in the sky. Take me as a Muslim, and join me to the righteous. But by the House, and by him who goes
98:n3: Al-sira: an enclosure made of stones and the branches of trees, for sheep and cattle.
98:n4: Al-dhibban, with kasra and doubling: the plural of dhubab, flies. And by “the son of her who ate them” he alluded to the ruler of the time; for in the age of ignorance they used to eat of every foul thing they came by.
98:n5: Ahjar al-Zayt: a place within Medina.
98:n6: “And he who goes to the House”: that is, one who touches it with his hand.
99:0: to the House [6] — and in another copy: and by al-Muzdalifa and those who go lightly to the casting of the pebbles — were it not for a covenant that the unlettered Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, made with me, I would have brought the opponents down to the gulf of death, and sent upon them the downpours of the thunderbolts of death; and in a little while they shall know. [7]
100:0: Section (on a report related by Ibn Abi al-Hadid). Ibn Abi al-Hadid related, from the Book of the Saqifa, with his chain to Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him, that 'Ali carried Fatima, the blessings of God be upon them both, upon a donkey and went with her by night to the houses of the Ansar, asking them for help and Fatima asking them for support. And they would say: O daughter of the Messenger of God, our pledge to this man has already passed; had your cousin come to us before Abu Bakr, we would not have held any equal to him. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Was I to leave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, dead in his house, without preparing him for burial, and go out to the people to contend with them over his rule? And Fatima said: Abu al-Hasan did nothing but what was fitting for him; and they did what God will reckon against them. [1] And he also said: And of the well-known speech of Mu'awiya to 'Ali, peace be upon him: And it was only yesterday that you carried the mistress of your house by night upon a donkey, your two hands in the hands of your two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, on the day Abu Bakr was pledged to; and you left not one of the people of Badr nor of those foremost in Islam without calling them to yourself, and you walked to them with your wife, and you brought your two sons near to them, and you called them out [2] against the companion of the Messenger of God!!!
100:1: Yet not one of them answered you save four or five. And by my life, had you been in the right they would have answered you; but you claimed a falsehood, and said what is not known,
100:n1: Sharh al-Nahj, vol. 6, p. 13; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, p. 352.
100:n2: A copy of the Nahj has: and you sought their help.
101:0: and you aimed at what is not to be attained. And however much I forget, I shall not forget your words to Abu Sufyan when he stirred and roused you: Had I found forty men of resolve, I would have risen against the people. So the Muslims have had more than one day from you. [3]
102:0: Section (on what Malik b. Nuwayra said to Abu Bakr, and how Khalid deceived him). One of the investigators said, in his summary of the book Iltihab Niran al-Ahzan, in these words: When Abu Bakr was pledged to, Malik b. Nuwayra entered Medina to see who had taken charge of the affair after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and it was a Friday. When he entered the mosque he found Abu Bakr preaching upon the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And when he looked at him he said: Is this the brother of Taym?!
102:1: They said: Yes. He said: Then what has become of the legatee of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded me to follow and to take as my friend? Al-Mughira b. Shu'ba said to him: You were absent and we were present, and one matter arises after another. Malik said: By God, nothing has arisen; rather you have betrayed God and His Messenger.
102:2: Then he advanced to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, why have you climbed the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, while the legatee of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, sits there?
102:3: Abu Bakr said: Put this bedouin out of the mosque, backwards on his heels. So 'Umar, Khalid and Qunfudh rose to him, and did not cease striking him in the back until they had put him out of the mosque by force, after insult and beating. So Malik mounted his riding-camel, reciting and saying: — We obeyed the Messenger of God while he was among us; — so, my people, what have I to do with Abu Bakr,
103:0: — that when Bakr dies a Bakr should stand in his place? [1] — That, by the House of God, is the breaking of the back. — He creeps about, and the ten-month camels crowd upon him, [2] as though — he were striving with hornless sheep, [3] or standing over my grave. — Had the legatee risen with the affair over them, [4] — we would have risen, though the standing were upon live coals. The narrator said: When the affair was settled for Abu Bakr, he sent Khalid b. al-Walid at the head of an army and said to him: You know what Ibn Nuwayra said in the mosque before all the witnesses, and what he recited of his verse; and we are not safe from a rent opening upon us from him that will not be mended. The right course is that you deceive him and kill him, and kill whoever would fight you in his defence, and take their women captive — for they have apostatized and withheld the alms.
103:1: So Khalid marched against them. When Malik b. Nuwayra saw the army coming towards him, he put on his coat of mail and sat straight upon the back of his horse; and Malik was a brave man among the brave of the Arabs, reckoned the equal of a hundred horsemen. When Khalid saw that he had come out, he feared him and stood in awe of him, and gave him covenants and compacts of safe-conduct; but he did not rely upon him. So he swore to him with the most binding oaths that he would not betray him. So Malik turned back and took off his coat of mail and received them as guests that night.
103:2: Then when the people slept, Khalid entered with those who were with him upon Malik in his house and killed him treacherously, and went in to his wife that same night; and he took his head and set it in a pot in which was the flesh of a slaughtered camel for the wedding feast, and commanded his companions to eat of it. Then he took them captive and called them the people of apostasy — a fabrication against God and against His Messenger. [5]
103:n1: “When Bakr dies, 'Umar stands before him” — in the Bihar.
103:n2: Al-'ishar, with kasra: the plural of 'ushara', the she-camel whose pregnancy has passed ten months. Perhaps the likening of the people to the ten-month camels is for what they consumed of forbidden things and coveted of false governorships; and the denying that they are hornless is a threat that he and his people are complete in resolve and in arms. Bihar al-Anwar.
103:n3: Al-jumm is the plural of al-jamma', the ewe that has no horn; and al-ajamm is the man without a spear.
103:n4: A variant: “Had a band of Quraysh gone round among us”.
103:n5: Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 8, old edition, p. 230.
104:0: When the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, heard of the killing of Malik b. Nuwayra and the taking captive of his women, he grieved over it with a severe grief and said: Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we return.
104:1: — Be patient a little; after hardship comes ease, — and every matter has its time and its measure. — The Guardian has regard for our conditions, — and above our ordering is an ordering that belongs to God. End of quotation. [6] I say: this story is among those related by opponent and adherent alike. And it is related that when Khalid killed Malik and took his wife, there was in his army Abu Qatada al-Ansari; and he mounted his horse and went to Abu Bakr, and swore that he would never march in an army under Khalid's banner again; and he told Abu Bakr the story. Abu Bakr said: The spoils have seduced the Arabs, and Khalid has abandoned what I commanded him. And when 'Umar heard that, he spoke about him before Abu Bakr, and spoke at length, and said: Retaliation has become due upon him. Then when Khalid b. al-Walid came, unaware, he entered the mosque wearing a tunic upon which were the traces of iron, wrapped in a turban of his in which he had stuck arrows. And when he entered the mosque, 'Umar rose to him and pulled the arrows from his head and broke them.
104:2: Then he said: O enemy of yourself! You set upon a Muslim man and killed him, and then leapt upon his wife! By God, we shall stone you with your own stones. And Khalid did not speak to him, supposing only that Abu Bakr's opinion of him was like 'Umar's — until he entered upon Abu Bakr and excused himself to him, and he excused him and passed over it. So Khalid went out, and 'Umar was sitting in the mosque; and he said: Come here to me, O son of Umm Shamla! Then 'Umar knew that Abu Bakr was pleased with him, so he did not speak to him and went into his house.
104:3: The 'allama al-Majlisi, may his secret be sanctified, said: 'Umar's reproach and his rage against Khalid over the killing of Malik b. Nuwayra were not out of regard for the religion nor out of care for the law of the Master of the Messengers; rather he was pained at his killing because he had been his ally in the age of ignorance. And he pardoned Khalid when he learned that he was the killer of Sa'd b.
105:0: 'Ubada. [7] It is related from some of our companions, from the People of the House, peace be upon them: that 'Umar met Khalid b. al-Walid one day during his caliphate in one of the walled gardens of Medina, and said to him: O Khalid, are you the one who killed Malik?
105:1: He said: O Commander of the Faithful, if I killed Malik b. Nuwayra for matters that were between me and him, then I killed for you Sa'd b. 'Ubada for matters that were between you and him. And his words pleased 'Umar, and he drew him to his breast and said to him: You are the sword of God and the sword of His Messenger. End of quotation. [8]
105:n7: Bihar al-Anwar, the Book of Trials and Tribulations, p. 257.
106:0: Section [on his presenting the Qur'an to the people, peace be upon him, and what they said in reply to him]. Sulaym b. Qays related from Salman the report of the Saqifa, and carried the account on until he said: When 'Ali, peace be upon him, saw their treachery and the little faith they kept with him, he kept to his house and turned to the Qur'an, composing and collecting it; and he did not go out of his house until he had collected it. It had been on sheets, and on palm-stalks, and on shoulder-blades, and on pieces of parchment. When he had collected all of it and written with his own hand its revelation and its interpretation, and what abrogates in it and what is abrogated, Abu Bakr sent to him: Come out and pledge. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, sent to him: I am occupied, and I have bound myself by an oath that I shall put on no cloak except for the prayer until I have composed the Qur'an and collected it. So they left him alone for some days; and he collected it in a single garment and sealed it. [1]
106:1: And it is related from another that he, peace be upon him, brought it to the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and set it down and prayed two units and gave the greeting to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. Then he went out to the people, and they were gathered with Abu Bakr in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, called out at the top of his voice: O people, I have not ceased, since the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, to be occupied — first with washing him, then with the Qur'an, until I collected all of it in this single garment. God did not send down upon His Messenger a single verse of it but that I have collected it; and there is not a verse of it but that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, recited it to me
107:0: and taught me its interpretation. Then 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: lest you say tomorrow, “We were heedless of this.” Then 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to them: Do not say on the Day of Resurrection that I did not call you to help me, nor remind you of my right, nor call you to the Book of God from its opening to its sealing. 'Umar said to him: How little need we have, with what we have of the Qur'an, of that to which you call us. [2]
107:1: And in another report 'Umar said: Leave it and go about your business. So he said to them, peace be upon him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, charged you and said: I leave among you the two weighty things, the Book of God and my kindred, the people of my house; and they shall not part until they return to me at the Pool. If you accept it, then accept me with it, that I may judge between you by what God has sent down in it; for I know better than you its interpretation, and what abrogates in it and what is abrogated, and its clear and its ambiguous, and its lawful and its forbidden. 'Umar said: Then take it away with you, so that it does not leave you and you do not leave it. We have no need of it, nor of you.
107:2: So he turned back, peace be upon him, to his house with the Qur'an, and sat, peace be upon him, upon his prayer-place and set the Qur'an in his lap and began to recite it, his two eyes pouring with tears. And his brother 'Aqil b. Abi Talib came in upon him and saw him weeping, and said: My brother, what ails you that you weep?
107:3: May God not make your eyes weep. He said, peace be upon him: My brother, my weeping, by God, is over the affair of Quraysh, and their galloping in error, and their circling about in discord, and their bolting in the wilderness. For they have agreed upon war against me as they agreed upon war against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, before me. So may Quraysh be requited with the requitals [3] — for they have cut my kinship and stripped me of the rule of my cousin. Then he sobbed, weeping, and then said “we return to Him”, and said, quoting a verse: — If you ask me how I am, then I am — enduring against the vicissitudes of time, hard as iron.
107:n2: Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 8, p. 51, old edition.
107:n3: “So may Quraysh be requited for the requitals” — a variant in 'Ilm al-Yaqin.
108:0: — It is hard upon me that you should see gloom in me, — so an enemy gloats or a loved one is grieved. [4] We return to the report of Sulaym. Then 'Ali, peace be upon him, went into his house, and 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: Send to 'Ali that he may pledge; for we are in nothing until he pledges, and if he pledges we are safe. So Abu Bakr sent to him: Answer the successor of the Messenger of God. And the messenger came to him and said that to him. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to him: Glory be to God — how quickly you have lied against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family! He knows, and those around him know, that God and His Messenger appointed no successor but me.
108:1: And the messenger went and told him what he had said. He said: Go and say to him: Answer the Commander of the Faithful, Abu Bakr. So he came to him and told him what he had said, and 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Glory be to God! By God, the time has not been so long that it should be forgotten. By God, he knows that this name is fitting for none but me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded him — and he was the seventh of seven — and they greeted me as Commander of the Faithful; and he and his companion, of the seven, asked for confirmation and said: Is this from God and His Messenger? And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to them: “Yes, truly, from God and His Messenger. He is the Commander of the Faithful, and the master of the Muslims, and the bearer of the banner of those with shining brows and limbs. God, mighty and exalted, shall seat him on the Day of Resurrection upon the Path, and he shall admit his friends to the Garden and his enemies to the Fire.” So the messenger went off and told him what he had said, peace be upon him; and they left him alone that day of theirs.
108:2: He said: Then when night came, 'Ali, peace be upon him, carried Fatima, peace be upon her, upon a donkey and took the hands of his two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, and he left not one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, without coming to him in his dwelling; and he adjured them by God for his right and called them to help him. And not one man of them answered save the four of us: Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad and al-Zubayr b. al-'Awwam. [5] For we shaved our heads and gave him our help; and al-Zubayr was the most clear-sighted of us in helping him.
108:n4: 'Ilm al-Yaqin, by the traditionist al-Kashani, may God have mercy on him, vol. 2, p. 686.
108:n5: I say: perhaps the phrase “they are Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad and al-Zubayr b. al-'Awwam” is an explanation by the compiler, may God have mercy on him; for otherwise the copy of the source and the Bihar are free of it.
109:0: Section (the kindling of the fire at the house of Fatima, peace be upon her). When 'Ali, peace be upon him, saw the people's abandoning of him and their leaving off to help him, and the gathering of their word with Abu Bakr and their exalting of him, he kept to his house. 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: What prevents you from sending to him that he may pledge? For there remains no one who has not pledged except him and these four. And Abu Bakr was the gentler of the two men and the more lenient and the more cunning and the deeper in his depths, while the other was the harsher of them and the rougher and the coarser. Abu Bakr said to him: Whom shall we send to him?
109:1: 'Umar said: We shall send Qunfudh to him; for he is a harsh man, rough and coarse, one of the freed captives, of the Banu 'Adi b. Ka'b. So he sent him, and sent helpers with him; and he went and asked leave to enter upon 'Ali, peace be upon him, and he refused to give them leave. So Qunfudh's companions returned to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, who were sitting in the mosque with the people around them, and said: We were not given leave. 'Umar said: Go; and if you are given leave, well; and if not, then enter without leave.
109:2: So they went and asked leave, and Fatima, peace be upon her, said: I forbid you to enter my house without leave. So they returned, and the accursed Qunfudh stood firm; and they said: Fatima said such and such, so we shrank from entering her house without leave. 'Umar grew angry and said: What have we to do with women? Then he ordered people around him to gather firewood; and they carried the firewood, and 'Umar carried it with them, and they set it around the dwelling of 'Ali — and in it were 'Ali and Fatima and their two sons, peace be upon them. Then 'Umar called out, so that 'Ali and Fatima, peace be upon them, might hear:
109:3: By God, you shall come out, O 'Ali, and you shall pledge to the successor of the Messenger of God — or I shall set the fire upon you. So Fatima, peace be upon her, rose and said: O 'Umar, what have we to do with you?
109:4: He said: Open the door, or we shall burn your house down upon you. She said: O 'Umar, do you not fear God, that you enter upon me in my house? But he refused to turn away, and 'Umar called for the fire and kindled it at the door. Then he pushed it and entered; and Fatima, peace be upon her, met him and cried out: O my father! O Messenger of God! So 'Umar raised the sword, and it was in its scabbard, and struck her side with it, and she cried out:
110:0: O my father! Then he raised the whip and struck her arm with it, and she called out: O Messenger of God, how evilly did Abu Bakr and 'Umar succeed you!
110:1: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, sprang up and seized him by the gathers of his garment and threw him down and struck his nose and his neck, and was minded to kill him; then he remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and what he had charged him with. So he said: By Him who honoured Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, with prophethood — O son of Suhak, were it not for a writ from God that has preceded and a covenant that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, charged me with, you would have known that you shall not enter my house. So 'Umar sent out a call for help, and the people came until they entered the house; and 'Ali, peace be upon him, sprang for his sword. And Qunfudh returned to Abu Bakr, fearing that 'Ali, peace be upon him, would come out with his sword, for what he knew of his might and his severity. Abu Bakr said to Qunfudh: Go back; and if he comes out, well; and if not, then burst in upon him in his house; and if he resists, then set the fire upon their house. So the accursed Qunfudh went and burst in, he and his companions, without leave; and 'Ali, peace be upon him, sprang for his sword, but they reached it before him and overpowered him by numbers, for they were many. And he took hold of one of their swords, but they overpowered him by numbers and cast a rope about his neck. And Fatima, peace be upon her, stood between them and him at the door of the house; and the accursed Qunfudh struck her with the whip, so that when she died she died with a mark upon her upper arm like an armlet from his blow — may God curse him.
110:2: Then they went off with 'Ali, peace be upon him, dragging him along [6] until he brought him to Abu Bakr; and 'Umar stood over his head with the sword, and Khalid b. al-Walid, and Abu 'Ubayda b. al-Jarrah, and Salim the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, and Mu'adh b. Jabal, and al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, and Usayd b. Hudayr, and Bashir b. Sa'd, and the rest of the people around Abu Bakr bearing arms. [7]
110:3: [The argument of Fatima, peace be upon her, with Abu Bakr] And in the report of al-'Ayyashi: Fatima, peace be upon her, came out and said: O Abu Bakr, do you intend
110:n6: In the source: “dragging him a dragging”, that is, pulling him a pulling. And atallahu: that is, he bound him and dragged him.
110:n7: The book of Sulaym b. Qays, pp. 83-84; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, p. 269.
111:0: to widow me of my husband? By God, if you do not desist from him, I shall loose my hair and rend my collar and come to my father's grave and cry out to my Lord. Then she took the hand of al-Hasan and al-Husayn and went out, making for the grave of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to Salman: Overtake the daughter of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, for I see the two sides of Medina heaving (8). By God, if she looses her hair and rends her collar and comes to her father's grave and cries out to her Lord, it will not be waited upon in Medina but that it be swallowed up with her and with all who are in it. So Salman, may God be pleased with him, overtook her and said: O daughter of Muhammad, God sent your father only as a mercy — so turn back. She said: O Salman, they intend to kill 'Ali, peace be upon him, and I have no patience for it. So let me be, that I may come to my father's grave and loose my hair and rend my collar and cry out to my Lord. Salman said: I fear that Medina will be swallowed up; and 'Ali sent me to you, commanding you to return to your house for his sake, and to help me. So she said, peace be upon her: Then I shall return, and be patient, and hear him and obey (9).
111:1: Al-Ihtijaj: It is related from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said: When the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was brought out of his dwelling, Fatima, peace be upon her, went out, and not a Hashimite woman remained but she went out with her, until she came near to the grave. And she said to them: Let go of my cousin. For by Him who sent Muhammad with the truth, if you do not let go of him, I shall loose my hair and set the shirt of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, upon my head and cry out to God, blessed and exalted. For Salih was no nobler before God than my father, nor the she-camel nobler than I, nor the young camel nobler before God than my child. Salman, may God be pleased with him, said: I was near to her, and by God I saw the foundations of the walls of the mosque — the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family — torn up from beneath, so that had a man wished to pass under them he could have passed. So I drew near to her and said: My lady and my mistress, God, blessed and exalted, sent your father as a mercy; so do not be a punishment. So she turned back; and the walls returned, until the dust rose from beneath them and entered into our nostrils (1).
111:2: (8) His words “takfa'an”: that is, they are shaking and turning over.
111:3: (9) Al-'Ayyashi, vol. 2, p. 67, and Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, p. 227. (10) Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, p. 113.
112:0: And al-Shaykh al-Kulayni, may his secret be sanctified, related from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon them both, who said: When there had been of their affair what there was, Fatima, peace be upon her, took hold of the gathers of 'Umar's garment and pulled him towards her and then said: Now, by God, O son of al-Khattab, were it not that I hate that the affliction should strike one who has no sin, you would know that I would swear an oath upon God, and then find Him swift to answer. [11]
112:1: And it is also related that: when 'Ali, peace be upon him, was brought out, Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, went out with the shirt of the Messenger of God upon her head, taking the hands of her two sons, and said: What have I to do with you, O Abu Bakr? Do you intend to orphan my two sons and to widow me of my husband?
112:2: By God, were it not that it would be an evil deed, I would loose my hair and cry out to my Lord. A man of the people said: What do you intend by this? Then she took his hand and went off with him. [12]
112:3: And in another report, from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, he said: By God, had she loosed her hair, they would all have died. [13]
112:4: [On 'Umar and Khalid bringing 'Ali (peace be upon him) and al-Zubayr to the pledge.
112:5: ] Ibn Abi al-Hadid related, from the Book of the Saqifa by al-Jawhari, with his chain from al-Sha'bi, who said: Abu Bakr said: O 'Umar, where is Khalid b. al-Walid?
112:6: He said: Here he is. He said: Go, the two of you, to them — meaning 'Ali and al-Zubayr — and bring them both to me. So 'Umar entered, and Khalid stood at the door outside; and 'Umar said to al-Zubayr: What is this sword?
112:7: He said: I have made it ready to pledge to 'Ali. He said: And in the house were many people, among them al-Miqdad b. al-Aswad and the body of the Hashimites. So 'Umar drew the sword and struck a stone in the house with it and broke it. Then he took al-Zubayr by the hand and made him stand, then pushed him and put him out, and said: O Khalid, take this one. So Khalid held him; and outside the house there was with Khalid a great gathering of people whom Abu Bakr had sent
113:0: as a support for the two of them. Then 'Umar entered and said to 'Ali, peace be upon him: Rise and pledge. And he hung back and held off; so he took him by his hand and said: Rise. And he refused to rise, so he lifted him and pushed him as he had pushed al-Zubayr. Then Khalid held them both, and 'Umar and those with him drove them along with a violent driving; and the people gathered, looking on, and the streets of Medina were filled with men.
113:1: And Fatima, peace be upon her, saw what 'Umar had done, and she cried out and wailed, and many women of the Hashimites and others gathered with her. And she came out to the door of her chamber and called out: O Abu Bakr, how swiftly have you fallen upon the household of the Messenger of God! By God, I shall not speak to him until I meet God. He said: And when 'Ali, peace be upon him, and al-Zubayr had pledged, and that outburst had subsided, Abu Bakr walked to her after that and interceded for 'Umar and made request of her, and she was reconciled to him.
113:2: Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: And the sound view, with me, is that she died holding a grievance against Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and that she charged that the two of them should not pray over her. And that, with our companions, is among the minor matters [14] forgiven them. It would have been more fitting for the two of them to honour her and to respect her station; but they feared division and were apprehensive of discord, so they did what was most conducive to good according to their own supposition; and they were in religion and in strength of certainty in a firm place. And the like of this, were it established to be an error, would not be a grave sin, but would be of the category of minor sins that do not call for disavowal nor make allegiance obligatory. End of the words of Ibn Abi al-Hadid — upon him be what he deserves and what he seeks. [15]
114:0: Section [the story of the house of Fatima, peace be upon her, and her being struck, and the casting of her unborn child]. The 'allama al-Majlisi said in the Bihar: I found in the book of Sulaym b. Qays al-Hilali, in the transmission of Aban b. Abi 'Ayyash from him, from Salman and 'Abd Allah b. al-'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, died on the day he died, and he was not laid in his grave before the people broke faith and turned back and gathered upon opposition. And 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, was occupied with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, until he had finished washing him and shrouding him and embalming him and laying him in his grave.
114:1: Then he turned, peace be upon him, to the composing of the Qur'an, and was kept from them by the charge of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. So 'Umar said to Abu Bakr: You there — all the people have pledged to you except this man and his household and these few. So send to him. And he sent to him a cousin of 'Umar's called Qunfudh, and said to him: O Qunfudh, go to 'Ali and say to him: Answer the successor of the Messenger of God. And they sent repeatedly, and 'Ali refused to come to them. So 'Umar sprang up in anger and called Khalid b. al-Walid and Qunfudh and ordered them to carry firewood and fire. Then he came on until he reached the door of 'Ali and Fatima, peace be upon them; and Fatima, peace be upon her, was seated behind the door, her head bound up and her body wasted at the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
114:2: And 'Umar came up and struck the door, then called out: O son of Abi Talib, open the door. Fatima, peace be upon her, said: O 'Umar, what have we to do with you? Will you not leave us and what we are in? He said: Open the door, or
115:0: we shall burn it down upon you. She said: O 'Umar, do you not fear God, mighty and exalted, that you would enter upon me in my house and break in upon my dwelling?
115:1: But he refused to turn away. Then 'Umar called for the fire and kindled it at the door, and burned the door. Then 'Umar pushed it, and Fatima, peace be upon her, met him and cried out: O my father! O Messenger of God! So 'Umar raised the sword, and it was in its scabbard, and struck her side with it, and she screamed. Then he raised the whip and struck her arm with it, and she cried out: O my father! So 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, sprang up and seized 'Umar by the gathers of his garment, then shook him and threw him down and struck his nose and his neck, and was minded to kill him; then he remembered the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and what he had charged him with of patience and obedience.
115:2: So he said: “By Him who honoured Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, with prophethood — O son of Suhak, were it not for a writ from God that has preceded, you would know that you shall not enter my house.” So 'Umar sent out a call for help, and the people came until they entered the house and overpowered him by numbers and cast a rope about his neck. And Fatima, peace be upon her, stood between them and him at the door of the house; and the accursed Qunfudh struck her with the whip, so that when she died she died with a mark upon her upper arm like an armlet from his blow — may God curse him. And he forced her against the doorpost of her house and pushed her, and broke her rib in her side, so that she cast the unborn child from her womb; and she did not cease to be confined to her bed until she died of that, the blessings of God be upon her, a martyr. [1]
115:3: I say: and it is also related, from the book of Sulaym, that 'Umar b. al-Khattab in one of the years fined all his governors half their wealth, save Qunfudh. Sulaym said: I came to a circle in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, in which there was none but a Hashimite, apart from Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, Muhammad b. Abi Bakr, 'Umar b. Abi Salama, and Qays b. Sa'd b. 'Ubada. And al-'Abbas said to 'Ali, peace be upon him: What do you think prevented 'Umar from fining Qunfudh as he fined all his governors?
115:4: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, looked at those around him, and then his two eyes brimmed with tears, and then he said: He thanked him for a blow he struck Fatima, peace be upon her, with the whip — and she died, and upon her upper arm was its mark, as though it were an armlet. [2]
115:n1: Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 28, pp. 297-299, and also p. 270.
116:0: It is related in al-Ihtijaj: the argument of al-Hasan b. 'Ali, peace be upon them both, against Mu'awiya and his companions, in a long report — that he said to al-Mughira b. Shu'ba, in reply to his calumny against the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and his reviling of him, the peace of God be upon him: As for you, O Mughira b. Shu'ba, you are an enemy to God, a caster-away of His Book, a denier of His Prophet — until he said to him: And you struck the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, until you made her bleed and she cast what was in her womb, in humiliation from you towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and in opposition from you to his command, and in violation of his sanctity. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had said to her: “O Fatima, you are the mistress of the women of the people of the Garden.” And by God, your destination is to the Fire, and He will make the evil consequence of what you have uttered fall upon you. [3]
117:0: Section [Fatima's coming, peace be upon her, to her father's grave, and what she said]. The author of the book 'Ilm al-Yaqin said, quoting from the book Iltihab Niran al-Ahzan, in these words: Then 'Umar gathered a company of the freed captives and the hypocrites and brought them to the dwelling of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him; and they found his door shut, and they shouted at him: Come out, O 'Ali, for the successor of the Messenger of God calls you. And he did not open the door to them.
117:1: So they brought firewood and set it at the door and brought fire to kindle it; and 'Umar shouted and said: By God, if you do not open, we shall set it alight with fire. And when Fatima, peace be upon her, knew that they were burning her dwelling, she rose and opened the door; and the people pushed her before she could withdraw from them. And Fatima, peace be upon her, hid behind the door, and 'Umar pushed it until he crushed her between the door and the wall. Then they leapt upon the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, while he was sitting upon his bed, and gathered upon him until they brought him out of his house dragged along, seized by his garment at the throat, hauling him to the mosque. And Fatima, peace be upon her, came between them and her husband and said: By God, I shall not let you drag my cousin away wrongfully.
117:2: Woe to you! How swiftly have you betrayed God and His Messenger concerning us, the People of the House! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, charged you to follow us and to love us and to hold fast to us; and God, exalted, said: “Say: I ask of you no reward for it save love for my kindred.” He said: So most of the people let him be, for her sake. Then 'Umar ordered Qunfudh, his cousin, to strike her with his whip; and Qunfudh struck her with the whip upon her back and her sides until he had worn her down
118:0: and left a mark upon her noble body; and that beating was the strongest cause in the casting of her unborn child — and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had named him Muhsin. And they set to leading the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, to the mosque, until they made him stand before Abu Bakr; and Fatima, peace be upon her, followed him to the mosque to free him, and was not able to do so. So she turned aside to her father's grave, and pointed towards it with burning grief and lamentation, saying: — My soul is held prisoner by its sighs; — would that it had gone out along with the sighs. — There is no good in life after you; and I weep — only for fear that my life should be long. Then she said: Alas for you, O my father! And bereaved is your beloved, Abu al-Hasan the trusted, and the father of your two grandsons al-Hasan and al-Husayn; he whom you raised while he was small and took as a brother when he was grown, and the greatest of those dear to you in your sight, and the most beloved of your companions to you, the first of them to hasten to Islam and to emigrate to you, O best of mankind. And here he is, driven along in captivity as a camel is led.
118:1: Then she gave a moan, and said: Alas for Muhammad! Alas for the beloved! Alas for my father! Alas for Abu al-Qasim! Alas for Ahmad! Alas for the fewness of his helpers! Alas, for rescue! Alas for the length of my distress! Alas for my sorrow! Alas for my calamity! Alas for the evil of this morning! And she fell down in a swoon. So the people clamoured with weeping and lamentation, and the mosque became a house of mourning. Then they made the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, stand before Abu Bakr and said to him: Stretch out your hand and pledge!!!
118:2: So he said: By God, I shall not pledge; and the pledge to me is upon your own necks.
118:3: And it is related from 'Adi b. Hatim that he said: By God, I never pitied anyone as I pitied 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, when he was brought seized by his garment at the throat, being led to Abu Bakr; and they said: Pledge!! He said: And if I do not?
118:4: They said: We shall strike that in which your two eyes are. He said: So he raised his head to the sky and said: “O God, I call You to witness that they have come to kill me; and I am the servant of God and the brother of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.” So they said to him: Stretch out your hand and pledge!!!
118:5: And he refused them; so they stretched out his hand by force, and he closed his fingertips, peace be upon him; and they all strove to open it and were not able. So Abu Bakr wiped over it while it was closed, and he,
119:0: peace be upon him, was saying, looking at the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family: “O son of my uncle, the people held me weak and were near to killing me.”
119:1: The narrator said: 'Ali, peace be upon him, addressed Abu Bakr with these two verses: — If by consultation you have come to hold their affairs, — then how is this, when those to be consulted were absent? — And if by nearness of kin you argued against their adversary, — then another than you is worthier of the Prophet and nearer. And he, peace be upon him, would often say: “How strange! That the caliphate should be by companionship, and not be by kinship and companionship!” End of quotation. [1]
120:0: Section [what 'Umar said in a letter of covenant to Mu'awiya]. In the letter of 'Umar's covenant to Mu'awiya: So I came to his house, intending to bring him out of it; and the bondmaid Fidda spoke — and I had said to her: Say to 'Ali that he should come out to the pledge of Abu Bakr, for the Muslims have gathered upon it. And she said: The Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali, is occupied. So I said: Leave this aside, and say to him: Let him come out, or we shall enter upon him and bring him out by force. So Fatima came out and stood behind the door and said: O you who are astray, you liars, what do you say? And what thing do you want? So I said: O Fatima. And she said: What do you wish, O 'Umar?
120:1: So I said: What is the matter with your cousin, that he has put you forward to answer and has sat behind the veil?
120:2: She said to me: Your insolence, O wretched one, has brought me out, and has bound the proof upon you and upon every straying, misguided one. So I said: Leave aside your falsehoods and the fables of women, and say to 'Ali: Let him come out. She said: Neither willingly nor with any honour. Do you frighten me with the party of Satan, O 'Umar?
120:3: — and the party of Satan was ever weak. So I said: If he does not come out, I shall bring thick firewood and set it ablaze as a fire upon the people of this house, and burn whoever is in it, or 'Ali shall be led to the pledge. And I took the whip of Qunfudh and struck her, and said to Khalid b. al-Walid: You and our men, come, gather the firewood. And I said: I am setting it alight. And she said: O enemy of God, and enemy of His Messenger, and enemy of the Commander of the Faithful! And Fatima set her two hands against the door, keeping me from opening it; and she held it fast, and it went hard with me. So I struck her two palms
121:0: with the whip, and it pained her; and I heard from her a gasping and a weeping, and I was near to softening and turning away from the door.
121:1: Then I remembered the rancours of 'Ali, and his avidity in the blood of the chiefs of the Arabs, and the guile of Muhammad and his sorcery; so I kicked the door — and she had pressed her womb against the door to hold it as a shield. And I heard her, and she had cried out a cry which I thought had turned the top of Medina to its bottom; and she said: O my father, O Messenger of God, thus was your beloved and your daughter treated! Ah, Fidda, come here and take me — for by God, what is in my womb of a child has been killed. And I heard her going into labour, leaning against the wall. So I pushed the door and entered, and she turned to me with a face that dimmed my sight; and I struck a blow upon her cheeks from outside the head-covering, so that her earring broke off and scattered to the ground — the report in its full length. [1]
121:2: And from Irshad al-Qulub, from her, peace be upon her, she said: So they gathered thick firewood at our door and brought the fire, to burn it and to burn us. And I stood at the doorpost and adjured them by God and by my father to hold back from us and to help us. So 'Umar took the whip from the hand of Qunfudh, the freedman of Abu Bakr, and struck my upper arm with it, and the whip coiled upon my arm until it became like an armlet. And he kicked the door with his foot and drove it back upon me while I was pregnant, and I fell upon my face, the fire blazing and scorching my face. And he struck me with his hand until my earring was scattered from my ear, and the labour came upon me, and I cast Muhsin, slain without any crime.
121:n1: Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 8, old edition, p. 222; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 8, old edition, p. 231.
122:0: Section [what God, exalted, told His Prophet on the night of the Ascension about the wronging of his daughter and the taking of her right]. And of what God, exalted, told His Prophet on the night of the Ascension was that He said: As for your daughter, she shall be wronged and deprived, and her right, which you assign to her, shall be taken by force; and she shall be struck while she is pregnant, and her sanctuary and her dwelling shall be entered without leave; then humiliation and abasement shall touch her, and then she shall find no protector; and she shall cast what is in her womb from the beating, and shall die of that beating. The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, said: Truly we belong to God, and truly to Him we return. I have accepted, my Lord, and submitted; and from You is the granting of success and of patience. [1]
122:1: And it is related that the first matter in which judgement shall be given is that of Muhsin b. 'Ali, peace be upon them both, concerning his killer, and then concerning Qunfudh. So he and his companion shall be brought and beaten with whips of fire — were one whip of them to fall upon the seas, they would boil from their east to their west; and were it set upon the mountains of this world, they would melt until they became ashes. And with them the two shall be beaten. [2]
122:2: And al-Mufaddal b. 'Umar related from al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, in a long report: And Muhsin shall come, carried by Khadija bint Khuwaylid and Fatima bint Asad, the mother of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and they crying out; and his mother Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, saying: “This is your day which you were promised. [3]
123:0: Today every soul shall find what it has done” — the verse. [4] He said: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, wept until his beard was drenched with tears; then he said: May no eye be comforted that does not weep at this remembrance. [5]
123:1: Al-Shaykh al-Saduq said, concerning the meaning of the Prophet's words to 'Ali, peace be upon them both — that you have a treasure in the Garden, and you are the master of its companion: I heard one of the shaykhs mention that this treasure is his child al-Muhsin, and he is the miscarried child whom Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, cast when she was crushed between the two doors. And he argued for that by what is related concerning the miscarried child: that he shall stand sullen at the door of the Garden, and it shall be said to him: Enter the Garden; and he shall say: No, not until my two parents enter before me — and so on. [6]
123:2: The most noble sayyid, our master al-Mir Hamid Husayn al-Hindi, may God perfume his resting-place, mentioned in 'Abaqat al-Anwar, from al-Wafi bi-l-Wafayat of Salah al-Din al-Safadi, that he mentioned in the entry on al-Nazzam, the teacher of al-Jahiz, that al-Nazzam said: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, designated the Imam, 'Ali, peace be upon him, and appointed him, and the companions knew that; but 'Umar concealed it for the sake of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both. And he said: 'Umar struck the belly of Fatima on the day of the pledge until she cast al-Muhsin from her womb. End of quotation. [7]
123:3: [The statement of Ibn Abi al-Hadid in the commentary on the Nahj] And Ibn Abi al-Hadid mentioned in the commentary on the Nahj the report of Habbar b. al-Aswad: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, declared his blood lawful on the day of the conquest of Mecca, because he had terrified Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, with the spear while she was in the howdah, and she was pregnant; and she saw blood and cast what was in her womb. He said: I read this report to the naqib Abu Ja'far, and he said: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, declared the blood of Habbar lawful because he terrified Zaynab so that she cast what was in her womb, then it is evident that, had he been alive, he would have declared lawful the blood of whoever terrified Fatima until she cast what was in her womb. So I said: May I relate from you what a people say — that Fatima was terrified
124:0: so that she cast al-Muhsin? He said: Do not relate it from me, nor relate from me that it is void; for I hold back in this place on account of certain reports I have concerning it. [8]
124:1: I say: and let us know what al-Sayyid al-Jaz'i said: — Her two parents afterwards made her swallow rage — many times; and evil is what they made her swallow. — They angered her, and thereby angered — God, the Lord of heaven, when they angered her. — Daughter of whom? Mother of whom? Wife of whom? — Woe to him who set the example of wronging and harming her. [Mention of how they grieved and were pained, peace be upon them, at the calamity of Fatima, peace be upon her] It is related from the Dala'il of al-Tabari, with his chain, from Zakariyya b. Adam, may mercy be upon him, who said: I was with al-Rida, peace be upon him, when Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, was brought in, and his age was less than four years. And he struck the ground with his hand and raised his head to the sky and was long in thought. So al-Rida, peace be upon him, said to him: By my soul — why is your thinking so long?
124:2: He said, peace be upon him: Over what was done to my mother Fatima, peace be upon her. Now by God, I shall bring the two of them out, then I shall burn them, then I shall scatter them, then I shall winnow them into the sea, a winnowing. So he drew him near and kissed his eyes and then said: By my father and my mother, you are the one for it — meaning the Imamate. [9]
124:3: And from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, peace be upon him: that when he was feverish he would seek relief with cold water, and then call out, so that his voice was heard at the door of the house: O Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family! [10]
124:4: The 'allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, said: Perhaps the call was a seeking of her intercession, the blessings of God be upon her, for healing.
124:n10: Rawdat al-Kafi, p. 19; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 62, p. 102.
125:0: I say: I hold it strongly probable that, just as the fever left its mark upon his delicate body, so the concealing of his grief for his wronged mother left its mark upon his noble heart. And as he quenched the heat of his body with water, so he quenched his burning and his sorrow by mentioning the name of Fatima, mistress of women — and that is like what appears in the grieving and the careworn in the drawing of a deep breath. For the effect of her calamity, the blessings of God be upon her, upon the hearts of her children, the pure Imams, is a pain sharper than the cutting of blades and hotter than the ember of fire. For they, the blessings of God be upon them, being bound by dissimulation to conceal it and unable to make it public — when Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, was mentioned, there would appear from them, the peace of God be upon them, something of what they had concealed, by which the shrewd and discerning may infer what is in their noble hearts of sorrow and of trials.
125:1: As it is related from Abu 'Abd Allah al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, that he said to al-Sakuni — and God, exalted, had granted him a daughter: What have you named her?
125:2: He said: I said, Fatima. He said: Ah, ah! And then he put his hand upon his forehead — and so on. [11]
125:3: And I mentioned earlier that when al-'Abbas said to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: What prevented 'Umar from fining Qunfudh as he fined all his governors?
125:4: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, looked at those around him, and then his two eyes brimmed with tears, and then he said: He thanked him for a blow he struck Fatima, peace be upon her, with the whip — and she died, and upon her upper arm was its mark, as though it were an armlet. [12]
125:5: And whoever reflects upon what is related of them, of their tenderness and their compassion and the softness of their noble hearts and their mercy, will affirm what I have said.
125:6: Look at what the shaykhs related from Bashshar al-Makari, that he said: I came in upon Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, at Kufa, and a tray of tabarzad dates had been set before him, and he was eating. And he said to me: O Bashshar, come near and eat. I said: May God give you joy, and may He make me your ransom — a jealous anger has seized me at something I saw on my way, which pained
125:n12: Sulaym b. Qays, p. 134. And al-dumluj, on the pattern of qunfudh: a thing resembling a black band which a woman wears upon her upper arm.
126:0: my heart and overcame me. So he said to me: By my right upon you, come near and eat. He said: So I came near and ate. Then he said to me: Your account. I said: I saw a constable [13] striking the head of a woman, driving her to the prison, and she calling out at the top of her voice: Help is sought of God and of His Messenger! — and no one came to her aid. He said, peace be upon him: And why did he do that to her?
126:1: He said: I heard the people saying that she stumbled and said: May God curse those who wronged you, O Fatima — so he committed against her what he committed. He said: So he broke off eating, peace be upon him, and did not cease weeping until his kerchief and his beard and his breast were wet with tears. Then he said: O Bashshar, rise with us to the mosque of al-Sahla, that we may call upon God and ask Him for the deliverance of this woman — and so on. [14]
