126:2: So if the state of al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, was such at hearing of an event that befell a woman of the partisans of Fatima, peace be upon her, then how must his state have been, peace be upon him, when he himself related what befell his mother Fatima, peace be upon her?
126:3: And he says: Then he struck her; and it is as though I look upon the earring in her ear when it snapped — that is, was broken by the blow.
126:4: And from what we have mentioned there appears the severity of the calamity of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and the greatness of his patience. Indeed it may be said that some of his calamities are greater than what stands against them of the calamity of his son al-Husayn, peace be upon him — beside whose calamity all calamities are small.
126:5: For I have mentioned in my book translated as Nafas al-Mahmum, among the events of 'Ashura', from al-Tabari: that Shimr b. Dhi al-Jawshan charged until he pierced the tent of al-Husayn, peace be upon him, with his spear and called out: Bring me fire, that I may burn this house down upon its people. He said: So the women screamed and came out of the tent; and al-Husayn, peace be upon him, cried out at him: O son of Dhi al-Jawshan, you call for fire to burn my house down upon my family? May God burn you with fire.
126:6: Abu Mikhnaf said: Sulayman b. Abi Rashid related to me, from Humayd b. Muslim, who said: I said to Shimr b. Dhi al-Jawshan: Glory be to God! This is not fitting for you. Do you wish to gather upon yourself
127:0: two traits — that you be punished with the punishment of God, and that you kill the children and the women? By God, in your killing of the men there is that with which your commander is pleased. He said: So he said: Who are you? I said: I shall not tell you who I am. He said: And by God I feared that, had he known me, he would harm me before the ruler. He said: Then a man came who was more obeyed by him than I, Shabath b. Rib'i, and said: I have not seen a saying worse than your saying, nor a stand uglier than your stand. Have you become a frightener of women? He said: And I bear witness that he was ashamed and went off to turn away. [15]
127:1: I say: this is Shimr — and for all that he was coarse and rough and of little shame, he was ashamed at the saying of Shabath, and then turned away!!
127:2: But as for the one who came to the door of the Commander of the Faithful and his household, peace be upon them, and threatened to burn them, and said: By Him in whose hand is the soul of 'Umar, he shall come out, or I shall burn it down upon whoever is in it — and it was said to him: But in it are Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, and the child of the Messenger of God, and the relics of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family [16] — then I bear witness that he was not ashamed, and did not turn away, but did what he did.
127:3: And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had none to help him and defend him save what is related of al-Zubayr: that when he saw the people had brought 'Ali, peace be upon him, out of his dwelling seized by the throat of his garment, he came on with his sword drawn, saying: O company of the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib! Is this done to 'Ali while you are alive? And he charged at 'Umar to strike him with the sword; and Khalid b. al-Walid threw a rock at him which struck the back of his neck, and the sword fell from his hand. So 'Umar took it and struck it upon a rock, and it broke. [17]
127:4: And al-Shaykh al-Kulayni related from Sadir, who said: We were with Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, and we mentioned what the people brought about after their prophet, and their humiliating of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. And a man of the company said: May God set you right — where then was the might of the Banu Hashim, and the numbers they had?
127:5: So Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: And who remained of the Banu Hashim? There were only Ja'far and Hamza, and they had passed away; and there remained with him two men, weak and abased, new in their covenant with Islam: al-'Abbas and 'Aqil — and they were of the freed captives. Now
127:n15: The Maqtal of Abu Mikhnaf, p. 141.
128:0: by God, had Hamza and Ja'far been present before those two, they would not have attained what they attained; and had the two of them witnessed it, they would have destroyed themselves. [18] And for that reason it is related from the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: that he never once stood upon the pulpit without saying, at the end of his words before he came down: “I have not ceased to be wronged since God took His Prophet.” [19]
128:1: And al-Musayyab b. Najiya said: While 'Ali, peace be upon him, was preaching, a bedouin was saying: Alas for my wrong! And 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Come near. So he came near; and he said: I have been wronged as many times as the clods of earth and the hairs of the flock. [20]
128:2: And a bedouin came pressing through and called out: O Commander of the Faithful, I am wronged. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: Woe to you — and I too am wronged; I have been wronged as many times as the clods of earth and the hairs of the flock. [21]
128:3: And Abu Dharr used to speak of him, peace be upon him, as the wronged shaykh whose right was usurped. [22]
128:4: And al-Kulayni related, among what is said at the grave of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, from Abu al-Hasan the Third, peace be upon him, who said: He says: “Peace be upon you, O friend of God. You are the first wronged one and the first whose right was seized. You were patient and sought the reward until certainty came to you. So I bear witness that you met God as a martyr. May God punish your killer with every kind of punishment, and renew the punishment upon him.” [23]
128:5: I say: and this is the breath of one whose breast is afflicted, and a portion of the disasters from which the rocks would melt. And let us seal the discourse with the verses of al-Shaykh Salih al-Hilli, may God have mercy on him: The verses of al-Shaykh Salih al-Hilli (may God have mercy on him) — Those who leapt to wrong the Family of Muhammad — while Muhammad lay cast down without a shroud; — and those who said to Fatima: You have hurt us — with a long, unceasing wailing and lament; — and those who cut down the arak tree, that there might not rest — in its shade, by wrong, a leaf of theirs nor a bough;
129:0: — and those who gathered firewood against the house which, — but for it, the gathering of the religion would never have been made whole; — and those who broke in upon the Chaste One in her house — and made her miscarry the most cherished unborn child; — and those who led their leader away by his sword-belt — while the Pure One called out behind him with a ringing cry: — Let go of my cousin, or I shall uncover in supplication — my head, and complain of my griefs to God. — The she-camel of Salih and her young were never, — in merit before God, anything but below me. — And she turned towards the noble grave with an eye — brimming with tears, and a heart burning and sorrowful. — She said, while the talons of affliction were in her heart: — Help! Say to the enemies: who is my helper? — O my father, this is the Samiri and his calf — followed, while the people have turned away from Harun. — Which of the disasters shall I ward off with my endurance, — when it has been my companion among misfortunes since I lived? — The loss of my father? Or the seizing of my husband's right? — Or the breaking of my rib? Or the falling of my unborn child? — Or their taking of my inheritance and the surplus of my gift? — Or their ignoring of my right, when they had known me? — They overcame your two orphans, al-Husayn and his brother; — and I asked them for my right, and they rebuked me.
130:0: Section [a quotation of al-Mas'udi's words in the book Ithbat al-Wasiyya]. Al-Mas'udi said in the book Ithbat al-Wasiyya: The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, rose with the command of God, mighty and exalted, and his age was thirty-five years. And the believers followed him, and the hypocrites held back from him, and they set up for the kingship and the affair of this world a man whom they chose for themselves, rather than him whom God, mighty and exalted, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had chosen. And it is related that al-'Abbas, may God have mercy on him, went to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had been taken, and said to him: Stretch out your hand, that I may pledge to you. And he said: And who seeks this affair? And who is fit for it besides us?
130:1: And there went to him a number of the Muslims, among them al-Zubayr and Abu Sufyan Sakhr b. Harb; but he refused. And the Emigrants and the Ansar differed, and the Ansar said: A commander from us and a commander from you. And a group of the Emigrants said: We heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: The caliphate is in Quraysh. So the Ansar gave way to Quraysh, after they had trampled Sa'd b. 'Ubada and trodden upon his belly. And 'Umar b. al-Khattab pledged to Abu Bakr and struck his hand upon his; then a group pledged to him of those who had come to Medina at that time of the bedouin and of those whose hearts were reconciled, and others followed them in that.
130:2: And the report reached the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, after he had finished washing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and embalming him and shrouding him and preparing him and burying him, after the prayer over him with those present of the Banu Hashim and a group of his companions such as Salman, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, 'Ammar, Hudhayfa, and Ubayy b. Ka'b
131:0: and a company of about forty men. So he rose to speak, and praised God and extolled Him, and then said: If the Imamate is in Quraysh, then I am the worthiest of Quraysh for it; and if it is not in Quraysh, then the Ansar stand upon their claim. Then he withdrew from them and entered his house, and stayed in it, and those of the Muslims who followed him.
131:1: And he said: I have in five of the prophets a pattern. Noah, when he said: “I am overcome, so grant help”; [1] and Abraham, when he said: “And I shall withdraw from you and from what you call upon besides God”; [2] and Lot, when he said: “Would that I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a strong support”; [3] and Moses, when he said: “So I fled from you when I feared you”; [4] and Aaron, when he said: “The people held me weak and were near to killing me.” [5]
131:2: Then he composed the Qur'an, peace be upon him, and went out to the people, and he had carried it in a wrapper with him, and it was stretching [6] out from under him.
131:3: And he said to them: This is the Book of God; I have composed it as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, commanded me and charged me, as it was sent down. And some of them said to him: Leave it and go. So he said to them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to you: I leave among you the two weighty things, the Book of God and my kindred; they shall not part until they return to me at the Pool. So if you accept it, then accept me with it, that I may judge between you by what is in it of the judgements of God. And they said: We have no need of it, nor of you; so take it away with you — you shall not leave it and it shall not leave you. So he turned away from them; and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and those with him of his partisans remained in their dwellings, according to what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had charged him with.
131:4: So they made for his dwelling and broke in upon him and burned his door and brought him out of it by force, and crushed the Mistress of Women with the door until she miscarried Muhsin. And they seized him for the pledge, and he refused and said: I shall not do it.
131:n6: Nattahu: that is, he stretched it out.
132:0: So they said: We shall kill you. And he said: If you kill me, then I am the servant of God and the brother of His Messenger. And they stretched out his hand, and he closed it, and it went hard with them to open it; so they wiped over it while it was shut.
132:1: Then, some days after this deed, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, met one of the people, and adjured him by God and reminded him of the days of God, and said to him: Would you like me to bring you together with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that he may command you and forbid you? And he said to him: Yes. So the two of them went out to the mosque of Quba, and he showed him the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, seated in it; and he said to him: O so-and-so, was it upon this that you made covenant with me — to deliver the affair to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and he is the Commander of the Faithful? So he returned, resolved to deliver the affair to him; but his companion prevented him from that and said: This is manifest sorcery, well known of the sorcery of the Banu Hashim. Do you not remember a day when we were with the son of Abi Kabsha?
132:2: And he commanded two trees, and they came together, and he relieved himself behind them; then he commanded them, and they parted and returned to their state.
132:3: So he said to him: Since you have reminded me of this — I was with him in the cave, and he wiped his hand over my face, then he stretched out his leg and showed me the sea; then he showed me Ja'far and his companions in a ship swimming upon the sea. So he turned back from what he had resolved upon. And they were minded to kill the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and charged one another and appointed a time for that, and that Khalid b. al-Walid should undertake his killing. So Asma' bint 'Umays sent a slave-girl of hers to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and she took hold of the two doorposts and called out: “The assembly are taking counsel about you, to kill you; so go out — truly I am of the sincere advisers to you.” (7) So he went out wrapped about with his sword. And the appointment for his killing was that their leader should give the greeting, (8) and then Khalid should rise to him with his sword. But they sensed his might; and the leader said, before he gave the greeting: Khalid, do not do what you were ordered to do. Then there was of their tales what the people have related. (7) Al-Qasas: 20.
132:4: (8) [their leader should finish his prayer with the greeting] — a variant in the printed copy. (9) Ithbat al-Wasiyya, pp. 142-144.
133:0: Section [Abu Bakr's sending to remove Fatima's agent, peace be upon her, from Fadak]. The author of al-Ihtijaj and the most noble shaykh 'Ali b. Ibrahim al-Qummi related, from Hammad b. 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: When Abu Bakr was pledged to, and the affair was settled for him over all the Emigrants and the Ansar, he sent to Fadak one who removed from it the agent of Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family.
133:1: So Fatima, peace be upon her, came to Abu Bakr and said: O Abu Bakr, why have you barred me from my inheritance from my father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and removed my agent from Fadak, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, assigned it to me by the command of God, exalted? He said: Bring witnesses to that. So she brought Umm Ayman, and she said: I shall not testify, O Abu Bakr, until I have argued against you with what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said. [She said:] I adjure you by God — do you not know that the Messenger of God said: Umm Ayman is a woman of the people of the Garden?
133:2: He said: Yes indeed. She said: Then I bear witness that God, mighty and exalted, revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and his Family: “So give the near of kin his right”; [1] and he assigned Fadak to Fatima by the command of God. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, came and testified to the like of that. So he wrote her a document and handed it to her. Then 'Umar entered and said: What is this document?
133:3: So [Abu Bakr] said: Fatima, peace be upon her,
134:0: has made a claim concerning Fadak, and Umm Ayman and 'Ali have testified for her, so I wrote it. [2] So 'Umar took the document from Fatima and tore it up and said: This is the spoil of the Muslims. And he said: Aws b. al-Hadathan and 'A'isha and Hafsa testify of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that he said: We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is alms. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, is her husband, drawing it to himself; and Umm Ayman, she is a righteous woman — had there been another with her, we would have looked into it. [The argument of 'Ali, peace be upon him, with Abu Bakr concerning Fadak] So Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, went out from the two of them weeping and grieved. Then, after that, 'Ali, peace be upon him, came to Abu Bakr, and he was in the mosque with the Emigrants and the Ansar around him, and said: O Abu Bakr, why have you barred Fatima from her inheritance from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, when she possessed it in the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family?
134:1: Abu Bakr said: This is spoil for the Muslims; if she establishes witnesses that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, assigned it to her, well; and if not, she has no right in it. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: O Abu Bakr, do you judge among us contrary to the judgement of God among the Muslims?
134:2: He said: No. He said: Then if there is in the hands of the Muslims a thing which they possess, and then I make a claim concerning it — of whom do you ask the proof?
134:3: He said: Of you I would ask the proof. He said: Then how is it with Fatima, peace be upon her, that you asked her the proof for what is in her hands, when she possessed it in the lifetime of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and after him; and you did not ask the Muslims proof for what they claimed against her, as witnesses, as you asked me for what I claimed against them? So Abu Bakr fell silent. And 'Umar said: O 'Ali, spare us your speech, for we have no strength against your argument. If you bring upright witnesses, well; and if not, it is spoil for the Muslims, and you have no right in it, nor has Fatima.
134:4: So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: O Abu Bakr, do you read the Book of God?
134:5: He said: Yes. He said: Then tell me concerning the words of God, mighty and exalted: “God only wishes to put away all uncleanness from you, O People of the House,
134:n2: “So I wrote for her concerning Fadak” — a variant.
135:0: and to purify you with a thorough purifying” [3] — was it sent down concerning us, or concerning other than us?
135:1: He said: Rather, concerning you. He said: Then if witnesses testified against Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, to an indecency, what would you do with her?
135:2: He said: I would carry out the penalty upon her as I would carry it out upon the rest of the women of the Muslims. He said: Then you would be with God among the unbelievers. He said: And why?
135:3: He said: Because you rejected God's testimony to her purity and accepted the testimony of people against her — just as you rejected the judgement of God and the judgement of His Messenger when he assigned Fadak to her and she took possession of it (4) in his lifetime; then you accepted the testimony of a bedouin who urinates upon his own heels against her, and took Fadak from her, and claimed that it is spoil for the Muslims.
135:4: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: The proof is upon the claimant, and the oath upon the one against whom the claim is made. So you rejected the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family: the proof is upon him who claims, and the oath upon him against whom the claim is made. He said: So the people murmured, and some of them denied it, [5] and said: By God, 'Ali has spoken truly. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, returned to his dwelling. He said: And Fatima, peace be upon her, entered the mosque and went round her father's grave, saying: — There have been after you tidings and a turmoil; — had you been present at them, the troubles would not have grown great — the verses. [The preparing for the killing of 'Ali, peace be upon him] He said: So Abu Bakr and 'Umar returned to their dwellings; and Abu Bakr sent for 'Umar and called him, and then said to him: Did you not see 'Ali's stand against us this day? If he takes such a stand again he will ruin our affair. So what is the right course?
135:5: 'Umar said: The right course is that you order his killing. He said: Then who shall kill him? He said: Khalid b. al-Walid. [3] Al-Ahzab: 33.
135:n3: “She had taken possession of it” — a variant.
135:n5: In al-Ihtijaj: so the people murmured and denied it, and some of them looked at others.
136:0: So the two of them sent for Khalid, and he came to them. And they said to him: We wish to charge you with a grave matter. He said: Charge me with what you will, even with the killing of 'Ali b. Abi Talib. They said: That is it. Khalid said: When shall I kill him?
136:1: Abu Bakr said: Be present in the mosque and stand at his side in the prayer; and when I give the greeting, rise to him and strike his neck. He said: Yes.
136:2: And Asma' bint 'Umays heard — and she was the wife of Abu Bakr — and she said to her slave-girl: Go to the dwelling of 'Ali and Fatima, peace be upon them, and give them the greeting, and say to 'Ali, peace be upon him: “The assembly are taking counsel about you, to kill you; so go out — truly I am of the sincere advisers to you.” [6] So the slave-girl came to them and said to 'Ali, peace be upon him: Asma' bint 'Umays gives you the greeting and says: The assembly are taking counsel — “the verse”. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Say to her: “God shall come between them and what they intend.”
136:3: Then he rose and made himself ready for the prayer and came to the mosque, and prayed by himself behind Abu Bakr, with Khalid b. al-Walid [praying] at his side and the sword with him. And when Abu Bakr sat for the testimony of faith, he regretted what he had said and feared discord, and knew the severity of 'Ali, peace be upon him, and his might. So he did not cease pondering, not daring to give the greeting, until the people supposed he had forgotten. Then he turned to Khalid and said: O Khalid, do not do what I ordered you. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.
136:4: So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: O Khalid, what was it that he ordered you to do?
136:5: He said: He ordered me to strike your neck. He said: And would you have done it?
136:6: He said: Yes, by God; had he not said to me “Do not do it” before the greeting, I would have killed you.
136:7: He said: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, took hold of him and dashed him to the ground; and the people gathered upon him. And 'Umar said: He will kill him, by the Lord of the Ka'ba. And the people said: O Abu al-Hasan, God, God — by the right of the one in the grave! So he let him go. [7]
136:n7: Tafsir al-Qummi, vol. 2, pp. 155-159; al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, pp. 119-127.
137:0: And the report of Abu Dharr, may God have mercy on him: that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, took Khalid at that moment with his two fingers, the forefinger and the middle, and squeezed him a squeezing; and Khalid gave a hideous cry, and the people were terrified and each was concerned for himself. And Khalid fouled his clothes and began to strike with his legs and could not speak. And Abu Bakr said to 'Umar: This is your upside-down counsel; it is as though I had been looking at this — and I praise God for our safety. And whenever anyone drew near to free him from his hand, peace be upon him, he glanced at him, glance by glance, and he withdrew and turned back. So Abu Bakr sent 'Umar to al-'Abbas, and he came and interceded with him and adjured him, and said: By the right of the grave and of the one in it, and by the right of his two sons and their mother — that you let him go. So he did that; and al-'Abbas kissed him between his eyes. [8]
137:1: And in another report: then 'Ali, peace be upon him, rose to 'Umar and took him by the gathers of his garment and said: O son of Suhak the Abyssinian, were it not for a writ from God that has preceded and a covenant from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, you would know which of us is the weaker in helpers and the fewer in number. And those present came between him, peace be upon him, and the people, and freed 'Umar from the hand of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. And at that al-'Abbas rose and came forward to Abu Bakr and said: Now by God, had you killed him, we would not have left a man of Taym walking upon the face of the earth. [9]
137:2: In the Bihar, Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: I asked the naqib Abu Ja'far Yahya b. Zayd, and said to him: I marvel at 'Ali, peace be upon him — how he remained that long period after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and how he was not assassinated and struck down in the midst of his dwelling, with their livers burning against him. And he said: Had he not rubbed his nose in the dust and set his cheek in the low ground of the earth, he would have been killed. But he made himself obscure and occupied himself with worship and prayer and looking into the Qur'an, and departed from that former garb and that emblem, and forgot the sword, and became like the assassin who repents and becomes a wanderer in the earth or a monk in the mountains. And when he obeyed the people who took charge of the affair, and became more abased before them than a sandal, they let him be and were silent about him. And the Arabs would not have advanced against him except by an understanding with the holder of the affair and a secret inward assent from him. So when the holders of the affair had no motive and no call to kill him, the holding back from him came about; and but for that he would have been killed. Then the appointed term
137:n9: 'Ilm al-Yaqin, by the traditionist al-Kashani, may God have mercy on him, vol. 2, p. 698.
138:0: is the strongest stronghold. So I said: Is what is said in the report of Khalid true? And he said: A group of the 'Alids mention that. And it has been related that a man came to Zufar b. al-Hudhayl, the companion of Abu Hanifa, and asked him what Abu Hanifa says about the permissibility of leaving the prayer by something other than the greeting — such as speech, or much movement, or a breaking of ablution. And he said: It is permitted; Abu Bakr said in his testimony of faith [what he said]. So the man said: And what is it that Abu Bakr said?
138:1: He said: Never mind. He said: So he repeated the question to him a second and a third time, and he said: Put him out, put him out! I had been saying that he is of the companions of Abu al-Khattab. I said: Then what is it that you yourself say?
138:2: He said: I hold that far-fetched, and that it is the Imamiyya who related it — and so on. [10]
138:3: [The letter of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, to Abu Bakr] Al-Ihtijaj: the letter of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, to Abu Bakr, when word of his speech reached him after the barring of al-Zahra', peace be upon her, from Fadak: You have split the surging waves of the trials with the breasts of the ships of deliverance, and cast down the crowns of the people of glory by gathering the people of treachery, and sought light from the Light of lights, and divided among yourselves the inheritances of the pure and righteous women, and loaded upon your backs [11] the burden of sins by your usurping of the gift of the Chosen Prophet. It is as though I see you going back and forth in blindness as the camel goes back and forth in the mill.
138:4: Now by God, were I permitted what you have no knowledge of, I would have reaped your heads from your bodies like the reaped grain, with cutting blades of iron; and I would have torn from the skulls of your champions that which would make your eye-corners fester and desolate your dwelling-places. For I, since you have known me, am the destroyer of armies and the annihilator of hosts and the ruiner of your green pastures and the quencher of your clamour and the slaughterer of those who wheel about — while you were secluded in your houses; and I was your companion but yesterday. By the life of my father and my mother, you will never love that the caliphate and the prophethood should both be among us, while you remember the rancours of Badr and the blood-vengeances of
138:n11: Ihtaqabu: that is, they carried upon their backs.
139:0: Uhud. Now by God, were I to say what God has already decreed concerning you, your ribs would fold into your bellies as the teeth of the turning millstone fold together. And if I speak, you say: Envy; and if I am silent, it is said: The son of Abi Talib has flinched from death. Far from it, far from it! Is this said to me now — and I am death and the dealer of death, [12] the plunger into destinies in the depths of a still night, [13] the bearer of the two heavy swords and the two long spears, and the shatterer of the banners in the tumult [14] of the overwhelming floods, and the reliever of distresses from the face of the best of creatures? Be at ease.
139:1: For by God, the son of Abi Talib is more familiar with death than the infant with the breasts of its mother. May the bereavers bereave you! Had I disclosed what God has sent down concerning you in His Book, you would have shaken as the well-ropes shake in the deep wells, and you would have gone out of your houses fleeing and wandering distracted upon your faces. But I make light of my sorrow, that I may meet my Lord with a hand cut off, empty of your pleasures, free of your quarrels. For your world is to me no more than a cloud that rose and towered, then thickened and levelled, then was torn and cleared away. Gently — for in a little while the dust of battle [15] shall clear for you, and you will find [16] the fruit of your deed bitter; nay, you will reap the planting of your own hands as a swift poison, [17] tearing, [18] a killing venom. And God suffices as judge, and His Messenger as adversary, and the Resurrection as the standing-place. And may God send none further off there than you, and bring none to ruin there but you; and peace be upon whoever follows guidance.
139:2: And when Abu Bakr read the letter he was seized with a severe terror at it, and said: Glory be to God! How bold he is against me, and how restrained against [19] others!
139:n12: In the source: and I am the dealer of death, the one who dies, the plunger into destinies.
139:n15: Al-qastal: the dust rising in battle.
139:n17: Al-dhu'aq: the poison that kills within the hour.
139:n18: A copy of the source has mumqiran: and that is the bitter.
140:0: O company of the Emigrants and the Ansar, you know that I consulted you concerning the estate of Fadak after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and you said: The prophets are not inherited from, and these are properties that must be joined to the property of the spoil and spent on the price of mounts and arms and the various means of striving and the needs of the frontiers. So we carried out your opinion; but he who lays claim to it has not carried it out. And here he is, flashing with menace and thundering with threat, swearing by the right of his Prophet that he will stain it with a deadly blood.
140:1: By God, I asked to be released from it and was not released, and sought to put it aside from myself and it was not put aside — all of that out of wariness of the son of Abi Talib's displeasure and in flight from his contention. And what have I to do with the son of Abi Talib? Has anyone ever contended with him and prevailed over him?
140:2: So 'Umar said: You refuse to speak except thus; and you are the son of one who was neither forward in wars nor generous in famines. Glory be to God — how craven [20] is your heart and how small your soul!!!
140:3: I have made clear for you great bucketfuls [21] to drink, and you refuse anything but to thirst with your own thirst. And I have made the necks of the Arabs kneel for you, and have made firm for you the rule over the people of counsel and of governance.
140:4: And but for that, the son of Abi Talib would have made your bones crumbled dust. So praise God for what He has bestowed upon you through me, and thank Him for that; for whoever mounts the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, it is fitting that he should render thanks to God. And this 'Ali b. Abi Talib is the solid rock whose water does not gush forth save after its breaking; and the speckled serpent that answers to nothing but the charm; and the bitter tree which, were it smeared with honey, would yield nothing but bitterness. He killed the chiefs of Quraysh and destroyed them, and fastened shame upon the last of them and disgraced them. So be easy in yourself; let his thunderbolts not deceive you, nor his thunder and his lightning dismay you — for I shall shut his door before he shuts yours. So Abu Bakr said to him: I adjure you by God, O 'Umar, that you spare me your blunders and your bluster.
140:5: For by God, had [the son of Abi Talib] intended to kill me and to kill you, he would have killed us with his left hand and not his right. Nothing
141:0: delivers us from him but three traits: the first, that he is one man with no helper; the second, that he follows [22] concerning us the charge of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and the third, that there is not one of these tribes but he has chewed it up as the young camel chews the herbage in springtime. So know that, but for this, the affair would return to him even though we were unwilling. Now, this world is lighter to me than that one of us should meet death — and so on. [23]
141:1: (Mention of the sermon of Fatima al-Zahra', peace be upon her) Al-Ihtijaj: 'Abd Allah b. al-Hasan related, with his chain from his forefathers, peace be upon them: that when Abu Bakr [and 'Umar] resolved upon barring Fatima, peace be upon her, from Fadak, and that reached her, she wound [24] her head-covering upon her head and wrapped herself in her outer garment [25] and came forward in a company of her attendants and the women of her people, trailing her skirts, her gait not departing in anything from the gait of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, until she entered upon Abu Bakr, and he was in a throng of the Emigrants and the Ansar and others.
141:2: And a curtain was hung [26] before her, and she sat. Then she gave a moan at which the people burst out [27] weeping, and the assembly shook. Then she waited a little, until, when the people's sobbing had quietened and their outburst had stilled, she opened her speech with the praise of God and extolling of Him and the blessing upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And the people returned to their weeping; and when they held back, she returned to her speech, and said, the blessings of God be upon her: Praise belongs to God for what He has bestowed, and thanks to Him for what He has inspired, and extolling for what He has sent before of the universal favours
141:n23: Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, pp. 127-131-145; and the 'allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, also gave it in the Bihar, vol. 8, old edition, p. 94, with added explanation of his own in its expressions — consult it there.
141:n24: She wound her head-covering: that is, she wrapped it.
141:n25: And al-jilbab: the cloak and the wrap.
141:n26: Nitat: it was hung. And al-mula'a: the wrap.
141:n27: The people burst out: that is, they made ready.
142:0: He began, and the fullness of the bounties He bestowed, and the completeness of the graces He conferred: their number too abundant to be counted, their reach too far for requital, their utmost limit beyond attainment. And He called them to seek increase of them by thankfulness for their continuance, and sought praise from His creatures by lavishing them, and repeated the call to the like of them.
142:1: And I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, who has no partner — a word whose inner meaning He made sincerity, whose bond He lodged within the hearts, and whose intelligible sense He illumined in thought: He whose sight is withheld from eyes, and His description from tongues, and His modality from imaginations. He originated things from no thing that was before them, and brought them into being with no copying of patterns He followed — until she said, the peace of God be upon her: O people, know that I am Fatima, and my father is Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family. I say it at the end and at the beginning; and I do not say what I say in error, nor do I do what I do unjustly. “There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is your suffering, solicitous for you, to the believers kind and merciful.” [28] So if you trace him and know him, you will find him my father and not the father of your women, and the brother of my cousin and not of your men. And excellent is he to whom such tracing is made, may God bless him and his Family.
142:2: So he delivered the message, proclaiming the warning aloud, turning aside from the course [29] of the polytheists, striking their main body, [30] seizing their throats, [31] calling to the way of his Lord with wisdom and goodly exhortation — breaking the idols and shattering the oracles — until the host was routed and they turned their backs; until the night was cloven [32] from its dawn and the truth shone forth in its purity, and the chief of the religion spoke and the frothings [33] of the satans were struck dumb, and the dregs of hypocrisy perished [34] and the knots of unbelief and discord were loosed. And you uttered the word of sincerity among
142:n29: Al-madraja: the path and the way.
142:n30: Al-thabaj: the main bulk of a thing.
142:n31: Al-kazam, with the vowels: the passage of the breath from the throat.
142:n32: The night was cloven: that is, it split open until the face of the morning appeared.
142:n33: Shaqashiq: the plural of shiqshiqa, a thing like a lung which the camel brings out of its mouth when it is in rut.
142:n34: Taha: he perished. And al-washiz: the lowly and base among people.
143:0: a few, white-faced and lean-bellied; [35] and you were on the brink of a pit of fire — a gulp for the drinker and a snatch for the greedy, [36] a firebrand for the hasty and a treading-place for feet. You drank what water the camels had fouled [37] and fed upon leaves, abased and driven off, fearing that the people around you would snatch you away. Then God, blessed and exalted, rescued you through Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, after this and after that, and after he had been tried with the champions [38] of men and the wolves of the Arabs and the rebels among the People of the Book.
143:1: Whenever they kindled a fire for war, God put it out; or a horn of Satan appeared, or a gaping mouth [39] opened among the polytheists, he cast his brother into its jaws; [40] and he would not turn back until he had trodden its ear with the sole of his foot [41] and quenched its flame with his sword — worn out in the cause of God, striving in the affair of God, near to the Messenger of God, a master among the friends of God, girded up, sincere, earnest, toiling. And you were in ease of living, tranquil, [42] merry, secure, awaiting for us the turns of fortune, watching for the news, [43] shrinking back at the encounter and fleeing at the battle.
143:2: Then, when God chose for His Prophet the abode of His prophets and the dwelling of His chosen, there appeared among you the thorns of hypocrisy, and the garment of religion grew threadbare, [44] and the one who had kept silent among the misguided spoke, and the obscure among the lowliest rose to prominence, and the stallion [45] of the falsifiers bellowed. So he strutted in your courtyards, and Satan put forth his head from his hiding-place, calling out to you; and he found you
143:n35: The white-faced and lean-bellied: by them are meant the People of the House, peace be upon them.
143:n36: A gulp for the drinker: his draught. A snatch for the greedy: the opportunity, that is, the place of his snatching and his chance.
143:n37: Al-tarq, with fatha: rain-water in which the camels urinate.
143:n38: The champions of men: that is, their brave ones.
143:n39: Faghara fahu: that is, he opened it.
143:n40: And al-lahawat: the plural of lahat, the flesh at the furthest part of the mouth.
143:n41: Yankafi': he turns back. And al-akhmas: what does not touch the ground of the sole of the foot.
143:n44: The thorns of hypocrisy: that is, its enmity. Samala: that is, it became worn out.
143:n45: Al-hadir: the camel's repeating of its voice in its throat. And al-faniq: the honoured stallion among camels.
144:0: answering to his call and observant of the might in it. Then he roused you, and found you light; and he stirred you, [46] and found you angry. So you branded camels that were not yours and came down to a watering-place that was not yours.
144:1: This — and the covenant was near, the wound wide, the injury not yet healed, and the Messenger not yet buried: a haste for which you claimed the fear of discord. Lo, into discord they have fallen; and truly Hell encompasses the unbelievers.
144:2: Far be it from you! And how is it with you, and where are you turned away — while the Book of God is among you, its matters manifest, its rulings radiant, its signs shining, its prohibitions plain, its commands clear? You have cast it behind your backs. Is it in aversion from it that you desire this, or by other than it that you judge? Evil for the wrongdoers is the exchange. And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it shall not be accepted of him, and in the hereafter he is among the losers.
144:3: Then you tarried only so long as it took for her wildness to settle and her leading-rein to run smooth. Then you set to kindling her flame and stirring her embers, and answering the call of the misleading Satan, and putting out the lights of the manifest religion, and extinguishing the practices of the chosen Prophet. You sip in secret, skimming the froth; [47] and you walk towards his family and his children in the covert and the thicket; and we must bear it as one bears the cutting of knives [48] and the thrust of the spearhead [49] in the entrails. And now you claim that we have no inheritance. “Is it the judgement of the age of ignorance that they seek? And who is better than God in judgement for a people who are certain?” Do you then not know?
144:4: Nay, it has become clear to you as the shining sun that I am his daughter. O Muslims, am I to be overcome in the matter of his inheritance?
144:5: O son of Abi Quhafa, is it in the Book of God that you should inherit your father and I should not inherit mine? You have surely brought a monstrous thing!
144:6: Was it deliberately that you abandoned the Book of God and cast it behind your backs, when He says: “And Solomon inherited David”; [50] and said, in what He recounted of the report of Yahya b. Zakariyya, when he said: My Lord,
144:n46: Ahmashakum: that is, he incited you.
144:n47: And al-irtigha' is the drinking of the froth, which is milk mixed with water — it is given as a proverb. And al-haswu is drinking a thing little by little.
144:n48: Al-hazz: the cutting. And al-mudi: the knife.
144:n49: And the thrust of the spearhead: that is, its wounding in the entrails.
145:0: “so grant me from Yourself an heir, who shall inherit me and inherit from the House of Jacob”; [51] and He said: “Those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God”; [52] and He said: “God charges you concerning your children: to the male the like of the portion of two females”; [53] and He said: “If he leaves goods, the bequest is for the parents and the near of kin, according to what is right — an obligation upon the God-fearing.” [54] And you claim that I have no standing [55] and no inheritance from my father, and that there is no kinship between us. Has God singled you out with a verse from which He excluded my father, may God bless him and his Family? Or do you say: The people of two religions do not inherit from one another — and am I and my father not of one religion?
145:1: Or are you more knowing of the particular and the general of the Qur'an than my father and my cousin?
145:2: Then take it, haltered and saddled; [56] it shall meet you on the day of your gathering.
145:3: And excellent is God as judge, and Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, as advocate, and the Resurrection as the appointed time. And at the Hour the falsifiers shall lose, and it shall not profit you when you repent. And for every tiding there is a fixed time, and you shall come to know upon whom a punishment comes that disgraces him, and upon whom an abiding punishment descends. Then she turned her glance, the peace of God be upon her, towards the Ansar and said: O company of young men, and arms of the community, and helpers of Islam! What is this slackness concerning my right and this drowsing [57] over my wrong?
145:4: Did not the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, my father, say: “A man is guarded in his children”? How swiftly have you brought about a change! And how soon is this fat melted! [58] Yet you have the capacity for what I seek, and the strength for what I ask and pursue.
145:5: And she carried the noble sermon on, the peace of God be upon her, to her words: Now, I have said what I have said in full knowledge of the abandonment [59] that has mingled with you and the treachery that
145:n56: Makhtuma: from al-khitam, with kasra, which is everything put into the nose of a camel that it may be led by it. And al-rahl, with fatha, is for the she-camel what the saddle is for the camel.
145:n58: And “how soon is this fat”: a proverb applied to one who reports the coming to be of a thing before its time.
145:n59: Al-jadhla: the abandoning of help. Khamaratkum: it mingled with you.
146:0: your hearts have taken to themselves. But it is the overflowing of the soul and the breathing-out of rage and the weakness of the spear-shaft [60] and the outpouring of the breast and the setting forth of the proof. So take it: load it upon a galled back and a worn hoof, lasting in shame, branded with the anger of God and with everlasting disgrace, joined to the kindled fire of God which rises over the hearts. It is before the eye of God, what you do; “and those who have done wrong shall know to what a place of turning they shall turn.”
146:1: And I am the daughter of a warner to you before a severe punishment. So act — we too are acting; and wait — we too are waiting. [61]
146:2: And al-Shaykh al-Azari, may God have mercy on him, did well in this place, in his words: — They broke the covenant of Ahmad concerning his brother, — and made the Chaste One taste what grieved her, — the day she came to 'Adi and Taym, — and of sorrow there was that which made her weeping long. — She drew near and complained to God a complaint — at which the firm mountains shook. — I do not know, when she was terrified and bare-headed, — whether the people opposed her husband or her father. — She admonished the people in the most perfect address; — she resembled the Chosen One in it, and he resembled her. — These are the Books — ask them, and you will see them — speaking of inheritance; so take hold of them. — And in the sense of “God charges you” is a command — that includes mankind in its kinship. — So the hearts were set at rest by her, and the rancours — were near to departing from him who had folded them. — O people, desire God in our regard: — we are what the garden of the Majestic has plucked. — And know that we are the rites of God's religion — among you; so honour him who dwells with them. — And we have from the treasuries of the Unseen an overflow — from which the rightly guided draw their guidance. — O people, what daughter of a prophet is there — whose father has withheld from her his inheritance? — How is my legacy taken from me for a curst one, — by sayings which he has forged of his own? — How is it that our Master did not charge us with that, — and charged Taym with it instead of us?
146:n60: Al-khawr: weakness; and al-qanat: the spear-shaft.
147:0: — Did he see us as not deserving guidance, — while Taym deserved guidance, so He guided them? — Or do you hold that He led us astray among mankind — after knowledge, that we might light upon their error? — Do me justice against two oppressors who wasted — the sanctity of the Chosen One and did not keep it. A return to the beginning: And Abu Bakr 'Abd Allah b. 'Uthman answered her and said: O daughter of the Messenger of God, your father was to the believers tender and noble, kind and merciful, and to the unbelievers a painful torment and a mighty punishment. If we trace him, we find him your father and not the father of the women, and a brother to your husband and not to the other intimates; [62] he preferred him above every close friend and aided him in every weighty affair. None loves you but every blessed one, and none hates you but every wretched one. You are the kindred of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, the goodly, the chosen elect; our guides to good and our paths to the Garden. And you, O best of women and daughter of the best of the prophets, are truthful in your saying, foremost in the abundance of your understanding, not turned back from your right nor barred from your truthfulness.
147:1: And by God, I have not overstepped the opinion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, nor acted save by his leave; and the scout does not lie to his own people!!
147:2: And I call God to witness — and He suffices as a witness — that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: We, the company of prophets, do not leave as inheritance gold nor silver nor house nor estate; we leave as inheritance only the Books and wisdom and knowledge and prophethood.
147:3: And whatever we had of sustenance, it is for the holder of the affair after us to judge concerning it by his own judgement. And we have set what you seek to the mounts [63] and the arms with which the Muslims fight and strive against the unbelievers and contend with the rebellious and the wicked; and that was by the agreement of the Muslims!!
147:4: I did not act alone in it, nor did I keep to myself what my own opinion was concerning it. And this is my state and my property: it is yours and before you!!! We do not withhold it from you, nor
147:n62: “And a brother to your mate rather than the intimates” — a variant.
147:n63: Al-kura': livestock such as camels, horses and mules.
148:0: do we store it away from you. And you are the mistress of your father's community and the goodly tree for your sons. Your property is not to be denied you out of your merit, nor is your branch and your root to be lowered. Your judgement is carried out in what my two hands have possessed!!!
148:1: So do you see that I should oppose in this your father, may God bless him and his Family?
148:2: So she said, peace be upon her: Glory be to God! My father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was not one to turn away from the Book of God nor to oppose its rulings; rather he followed its traces and trod in the wake of its chapters. Will you then add to treachery a pretext against him with falsehood? And this, after his death, resembles the calamities that were plotted against him in his lifetime. This is the Book of God, a just judge and a decisive speaker; it says: “He shall inherit me and inherit from the House of Jacob”; [64] and it says: “And Solomon inherited David.” [65] So He, mighty and exalted, made clear in what He apportioned of the shares, and legislated of the obligations and the inheritance, and permitted of the portion of males and females, that by which He removed the pretext of the falsifiers and did away with conjecture and doubts among those who come after. Nay, rather your souls have enticed you to a thing; so a comely patience — and God is He whose help is sought against what you describe.
148:3: So Abu Bakr said: God has spoken truly, and His Messenger has spoken truly, and his daughter has spoken truly. You are the mine of wisdom and the dwelling of guidance and mercy, and the pillar of the religion and the source of the proof. I do not set your rightness far off, nor do I deny your address. These Muslims are between me and you; they invested me with what I have taken charge of, and by an agreement from them I took what I took, not overbearing nor arbitrary nor self-serving — and they are witnesses to that.
148:4: So Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, turned [to the people] and said: O company of people, hasty towards a false saying, conniving at an ugly and ruinous deed! Will you not then ponder the Qur'an, or are there locks upon the hearts?
148:5: Nay, rather there has settled upon your hearts the rust of the evil you have done, so that it has seized your hearing and your sight. And evil is the interpretation you have made, and wretched is that to which you have pointed,
149:0: and evil is that which you have wrested away. By God, you shall find its carrying heavy and its outcome grievous, when the covering is lifted from you and what lies behind it of adversity appears, and there becomes clear to you from your Lord what you had not reckoned upon; and there the falsifiers shall lose.
149:1: Then she turned towards the grave of the Prophet (may God bless him and his Family) and said: — There have been after you tidings and a turmoil; — had you been present at them, the troubles would not have grown great. — We have lost you as the earth loses its rain; — and your people are in disorder, so witness them, for they have gone astray. — And every household that has nearness and station — with God is brought near above those who are close. — Men disclosed to us the secrets of their breasts — when you departed and the dust came between us and you. — Men scowled at us and we were held in contempt — when you were lost, and all the earth is seized by force. — You were a light and a full moon by which we sought light; — upon you the Books came down from the Lord of Might. — And Gabriel used to console us with the verses; — but now you are lost, and every good is veiled. — Would that before you death had come upon us, — when you departed and the writings came between us and you. — We have been afflicted with what no sorrowing one of creation — has been afflicted with, neither non-Arab nor Arab. [66] And in al-Durr al-Nazim, he said: And she joined to that, saying: — You were a defender while you lived for me; — the open land is dimmed, and you were my wing. — So today I submit to the abased and guard myself — against him, and push away my oppressor with the palm of my hand. — And when a dove weeps a sorrow of her own — by night upon a branch, I weep my morning. And al-Shaykh related, with his chain, from Zaynab bint 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, who said:
150:0: When Abu Bakr's mind was settled upon barring Fatima, peace be upon her, from Fadak and al-'Awali, and she despaired of his answering her, she turned aside to the grave of her father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and cast herself upon it and complained to him of what the people had done to her, and wept until she had wetted his earth, peace be upon him, with her tears; and she lamented him. Then she said at the end of a lament: — There have been after you tidings and a turmoil — the verses. [67]
150:1: And in the report of al-Ihtijaj: then she turned back, peace be upon her, and the Commander of the Faithful, the blessings of God be upon him, was awaiting her return to him and watching for her appearance before him. And when the house had settled about her, she said to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: O son of Abi Talib, you have wrapped yourself in the wrapping of the unborn child and sat in the seclusion of the suspected; [68] you broke the foremost pinion of the falcon, [69] and the feathers of the flightless bird have failed you. This is the son of Abi Quhafa robbing me of my father's gift and my two sons' sustenance. He has been open in his enmity to me, and I have found him most obstinate in my speech, until Qila [70] has withheld her help from me, and the Emigrants their bond, and the community has lowered its eyes before me. So there is neither one to repel nor one to prevent.
150:2: You went out suppressing your rage and returned defeated. You humbled [71] your cheek on the day you lost your edge. You were preyed upon by the wolves and you spread out the dust. You did not restrain a speaker nor avail against a falsehood; and I have no choice. Would that I had died before this little while of mine and short of my abasement. God is my excuser [72] against you as an aggressor, and from you as a protector. Alas for me at every sunrise; alas for me at every sunset! The support is dead and the arm is weakened. My complaint is to my father and my plea is to my Lord. O God, You are stronger in power and might, and more severe in force and in punishment.
150:3: So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: There is no woe upon you; rather, woe to your hater. Restrain
150:n67: Al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Mufid, may God have mercy on him, p. 40, al-Ghaffari edition.
150:n68: The 'allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, said: And the meaning is: you have hidden from the people like the unborn child, and held back from seeking the right, and come down to the station of the fearful and suspected.
150:n69: Al-ajdal: the falcon. And al-a'zal among birds: that which is not able to fly.
150:n70: Qila withheld her help: the name of a tribe; the Ansar are traced to their mother Qila.
150:n71: Dara'a: he submitted and was abased.
150:n72: Al-'adhir: in the sense of the one who excuses — that is, God accepts my excuse against one who is aggressive and transgressing.
151:0: your sorrow, [73] O daughter of the elect and remnant of prophethood. For I have not been slack in my religion nor have I fallen short of what is in my power. And if you desire sustenance, your provision is guaranteed and your surety is trustworthy; and what has been prepared for you is better than what has been cut off from you. So seek your reward with God. And she said: God is my sufficiency — and she fell silent. [74]
151:n73: Restrain your sorrow: that is, hold back from your grief.
152:0: Section [Abu Bakr's speech to the people after the saying of Fatima (peace be upon her)]. Ibn Abi al-Hadid related, in the course of the reports of Fadak, from Ahmad b. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Jawhari: that when Abu Bakr heard the sermon of Fatima, peace be upon her, concerning Fadak, her speech weighed heavily upon him. So he mounted the pulpit and said: O people, what is this eager listening to every tale? Where were these desires in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family?
152:1: Let him who has heard speak, and him who has witnessed say his word. He is but a fox whose witness is his own tail, clinging to every discord; he it is who says: Turn it back young again, after it has grown old. You seek aid of the weak and seek help of the women, like Umm Tihal, whose dearest to her of her people was the adulterer. Now, were I to wish to speak, I would speak; and were I to speak, I would disclose. I am silent so long as I am left alone. Then he turned to the Ansar and said: Word has reached me, O company of the Ansar, of the speech of your fools. And the worthiest to keep the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, are you — for he came to you and you sheltered and helped. Now, I am not one to stretch out a hand or a tongue against him who does not deserve it from us. Then he came down; and Fatima, peace be upon her, went away to her dwelling.
152:2: Then Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: I read this speech to the naqib Yahya b. Abi Zayd al-Basri, and said to him: At whom is he hinting?
152:3: And he said: Rather, he is speaking openly. I said: Had he spoken openly I would not have asked you. So he laughed and said: At 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him. I said: Is all this speech said by him of 'Ali, peace be upon him? He said: Yes — it is kingship, my son. I said: Then what was the speech of the Ansar? He said:
153:0: They called out with the mention of 'Ali, peace be upon him; so he feared that the affair would be shaken against him, and forbade them. Then I asked him about the rare words in it.
153:1: And he said: As for al-ri'a, without doubling, it is listening and giving ear; and al-qala is speech. And Thu'ala is a name for the fox, a proper noun not declined, like Dhu'ala for the wolf. And “his witness is his tail” — that is, he has no witness for what he claims but a part and a portion of himself. And its origin is a proverb: they said that the fox wished to set the lion against the wolf, and said: He ate the sheep that you had prepared for yourself, and I was present. He said: Then who will testify to that?
153:2: So he raised his tail, and upon it was blood; and the lion had missed the sheep, so he accepted his testimony and killed the wolf. And murib is one who clings — ariba, he kept to the place. And “turn it back young again”: bring it back to its first state, meaning the discord and the tumult. And Umm Tihal was an adulterous woman in the age of ignorance, and she is given as a proverb: it is said, “more adulterous than Umm Tihal.” End of quotation. [1]
153:3: I say: and in the book al-Durr al-Nazim of Jamal al-Din Yusuf b. Hatim, the jurist of Syria, the pupil of al-Muhaqqiq al-Hilli, he said: Umm Salama said, when she heard what had befallen Fatima, peace be upon her: Is it to the like of Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that this saying is said? She, by God, is the houri among mankind, and the soul for the soul. She was raised in the laps of the God-fearing, and the hands of the angels took her, and she grew in the laps of the pure women, and came up in the best of growth and was raised in the best of raising.
153:4: Do you claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, forbade her his inheritance and did not inform her of it?!!!
153:5: And God, exalted, has said: “And warn your nearest kindred.” [2] Did he then warn her, and she opposed him by making a demand?
153:6: And she is the best of women and the mother of the chiefs of the youths and the peer of the daughter of 'Imran. Through her father the messages of his Lord were completed. By God, he used to be tender towards her against the heat and the cold, and would pillow her [3] upon his right hand and cover her with his left — gently! And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, is in your sight, and to God you shall return. Woe to you! You shall come to know. So Umm Salama was deprived of her stipend that year. End of quotation.
153:n3: I say: in both copies it is yushidduha. And what is apparently correct is yuwassiduha bi-yaminihi — that is, he makes his right hand a pillow for her.
154:0: And Ibn Abi al-Hadid also related, from Ahmad b. 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Jawhari, from Hisham b. Muhammad, from his father, who said: Fatima, peace be upon her, said to Abu Bakr: Umm Ayman testifies for me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, gave me Fadak. And he said to her: O daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, by God, God has not created a creature dearer to me than the Messenger of God, your father; and I would have loved that the sky had fallen upon the earth the day your father died!!
154:1: By God, that 'A'isha should become poor is dearer to me than that you should become poor!!
154:2: Do you suppose that I would give the black and the red and the white his right, and wrong you of your right?!
154:3: And you are the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family! This property was not the Prophet's, may God bless him and his Family; it was only a property of the properties of the Muslims, with which the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, mounted the men and which he spent in the way of God. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, died, I took charge of it as he used to take charge of it.
154:4: She said: By God, I shall never speak to you. He said: By God, I shall never shun you. She said: By God, I shall call upon God against you. He said: By God, I shall call upon God for you. And when death came to her, she charged that he should not pray over her. So she was buried by night, and al-'Abbas b. 'Abd al-Muttalib prayed over her. And between her death and her father's death were seventy-two nights. [4]
154:5: [A quotation of al-Jahiz's words] I say: Abu 'Uthman al-Jahiz said, according to what 'Alam al-Huda al-Murtada, may God be pleased with him, related from him: Some people have claimed that the proof of the truthfulness of the report of those two — meaning Abu Bakr and 'Umar — in the barring of the inheritance, and of the clearness of their record, is the companions of the Messenger of God's leaving off to condemn them. Then he said: It is said to them: If the leaving off of condemnation is a proof of their truthfulness, then the leaving off of condemnation of those who complained of the wrong in it, and argued against the two of them, and made demands of them, must be a proof of the truth of their claim and of the soundness of their saying — the more so as the disputes were long and the exchanges and the wranglings were many, and the resistance appeared and the grievance grew severe; and it reached such a point with Fatima, peace be upon her, that she charged that Abu Bakr should not pray over her.
155:0: And she had said to him, when she came to him seeking her right and arguing by her kin: Who inherits you, O Abu Bakr, when you die?
155:1: He said: My family and my children. She said: Then why is it that we do not inherit the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family? So when he barred her from her inheritance and diminished her right and made pretexts against her and wavered in her affair, and she saw the injustice and despaired of his relenting, and felt the touch of weakness and the fewness of the helper, she said: By God, I shall call upon God against you. He said: By God, I shall call upon God for you. She said: By God, I shall never speak to you. He said: By God, I shall never shun you.
155:2: So if the leaving off of condemnation of Abu Bakr is a proof of the rightness of his barring, then in the leaving off of condemnation of Fatima, peace be upon her, is a proof of the rightness of her demand. And the least that was obligatory upon them in that was to teach her what she did not know, and to remind her of what she had forgotten, and to turn her away from error, and to raise her worth above coarseness, and that she should not speak foully nor wrong one who was just nor cut off one who kept ties. So when we do not find that they condemned the two disputants alike, then the matters are equal and the grounds are even; and the return to the original ruling of God concerning inheritance is worthier for us and for you, and more binding upon us and upon you.
155:3: Then he said: And if they say: How can Abu Bakr be supposed to have wronged her and transgressed against her, when the more harshness Fatima, peace be upon her, showed him the more gentleness and tenderness he showed her — where she says: By God, I shall never speak to you, and he says: By God, I shall never shun you; and then she says: By God, I shall call upon God against you, and he says: By God, I shall call upon God for you;
155:4: and then he bears this harsh speech and these severe words in the house of the caliphate and in the presence of Quraysh and the companions, together with the caliphate's need of splendour and elevation and what is due to it of dignity and awe; and then that did not prevent him from saying, by way of excuse or of drawing near, the speech of one who magnifies her right and exalts her station and guards her face and is tender towards her: There is no one dearer to me than you in poverty, nor more beloved to me than you in wealth; but I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say: We, the company of prophets, are not inherited from; what we leave is alms.
155:5: It is said to them: Is that a proof of clearance from wrongdoing and of soundness from injustice? For the guile of the wrongdoer and the cunning of the schemer may reach, when he is shrewd and practised in disputation, the point of making a show of the speech of the wronged and the abasement of the one who yields his due and the affection of the loving and truthful. End of the words of al-Jahiz. [5]
156:0: Al-Tabari and al-Thaqafi related — they both said in their histories: that 'A'isha came to 'Uthman and said: Give me what my father and 'Umar used to give me. He said: I find no place for it in the Book nor in the Sunna; but your father and 'Umar used to give it to you out of the goodness of their own souls, and I shall not do it. She said: Then give me my inheritance from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. He said: Did Fatima not come seeking her inheritance from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family?
156:1: And you and Malik b. Aws al-Basri testified that the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, is not inherited from, and you voided the right of Fatima, peace be upon her — and now you come seeking it? I shall not do it.
156:2: And al-Tabari added: and 'Uthman was reclining, and he sat up straight and said: Fatima shall know today what kind of cousin she has in me. Were you not — you and a bedouin who performs his ablution with his own urine — the ones who testified before your father? Both of them said it in their histories. [6]
157:0: Section [“the producing of witnesses in the demand for her right, peace be upon her”]. From al-Ikhtisas, from 'Abd Allah b. Sinan, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, and Abu Bakr sat in his seat, Abu Bakr sent to the agent of Fatima, peace be upon her, and removed him from Fadak. So Fatima, peace be upon her, came to him and said: O Abu Bakr, you have claimed that you are the successor of my father and have sat in his seat; and you sent to my agent and removed him from Fadak, when you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, gave it to me as a charitable gift, and that I have witnesses to that. And he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, is not inherited from.
157:1: So she returned to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and told him; and he said: Go back to him and say to him: You claimed that the Prophet is not inherited from — yet Solomon inherited David, and Yahya inherited Zakariyya. And how is it that I do not inherit my father? So 'Umar said: You have been taught. She said: And if I have been taught, it is only my cousin and my husband who taught me. So Abu Bakr said: 'A'isha and 'Umar testify that they heard!!
157:2: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, saying: The Prophet is not inherited from. And she said: This is the first false testimony they have borne in Islam.
157:3: Then she said: Fadak — the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, gave it to me only as a charitable gift, and I have proof of that. And he said to her: Bring your proof.
157:4: He said: So she brought Umm Ayman and 'Ali, peace be upon him. And Abu Bakr said: O Umm Ayman, did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, say anything concerning Fatima? So the two of them said: We heard the Messenger of God,
158:0: may God bless him and his Family, say: Fatima is the mistress of the women of the people of the Garden. Then Umm Ayman said: And would one who is the mistress of the women of the people of the Garden claim what is not hers? And I am a woman of the people of the Garden — I would not testify to what I had not heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. So 'Umar said: Spare us, O Umm Ayman, these tales. To what do you testify?
158:1: She said: I was sitting in the house of Fatima, peace be upon her, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was sitting, when Gabriel came down and said: O Muhammad, rise; for God, blessed and exalted, has commanded me to mark out Fadak for you with my wing. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, rose with Gabriel, and it was not long before he returned. And Fatima, peace be upon her, said: O my father, where did you go?
158:2: And he said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) marked out Fadak for me with his wing and set its bounds for me. She said: O my father, I fear want and need after you; so give it to me as a charitable gift. And he said: It is a gift to you. So she took possession of it.
158:3: She said: Yes. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said: O Umm Ayman, bear witness; and O 'Ali, bear witness. So 'Umar said: You are a woman, and we do not admit the testimony of a woman alone; and as for 'Ali, he draws it to himself. He said: So she rose in anger and said: O God, these two have wronged the daughter of Your Prophet of her right; so make heavy Your grip upon them. Then she went out. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, carried her upon a she-ass with a cloak upon it that had a fringe, [1] and went round with her for forty mornings among the houses of the Emigrants and the Ansar, with al-Hasan and al-Husayn with her, and she saying: O company of the Emigrants and the Ansar, help God and the daughter of your Prophet — until he said: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to her: Go to Abu Bakr alone, for he is the gentler of the two, and say to him: You have claimed the seat of my father and that you are his successor and have sat in his seat; and had Fadak been yours and then I had asked it of you as a gift, its return to me would have been obligatory. And when she came to him and said that to him, he said: You have spoken truly. He said: So he called for a document and wrote it for her with the return of Fadak. So she went out with the document with her; and 'Umar met her and said: O daughter of Muhammad, what is this document that is with you?
158:4: And she said: A document that Abu Bakr wrote for me with the return of Fadak. He said: Give it to me. And she refused to hand it
158:n1: Al-khaml, with the vowels: the nap of a coverlet and the like.
159:0: to him; so he kicked her with his foot, and she was pregnant with a son named al-Muhsin, and she miscarried al-Muhsin, peace be upon him, from her womb. Then he struck her a blow; and it is as though I look upon the earring in her ear when it was broken. [2] Then he took the document and tore it up. So she went away and remained seventy-five days ill from what 'Umar had struck her with, and then was taken.
159:1: And when death came to her, she called 'Ali, the blessings of God be upon him, and said: Either you undertake it, or I shall make my bequest to Ibn al-Zubayr. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: I shall undertake your bequest, O daughter of Muhammad. She said: I ask you by the right of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that when I die those two should not attend me nor pray over me. He said: That is yours. And when she was taken, the blessings of God be upon her, he buried her by night in her house — and so on. [3]
159:2: I say: this report is not, with me, at the level of reliability of the rest of the reports mentioned; but since the 'allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him, quoted it in the Bihar, I wished not to leave my book free of it, so I followed him and quoted it from him. And as for her words, the blessings of God be upon her, “or I shall make my bequest to Ibn al-Zubayr” — I think the word “Ibn” is from the copyists, and that the original was “I shall make my bequest to al-Zubayr”; this if the supposition is correct. But if the word “Ibn” is sound, then what is meant by it is 'Abd Allah b. al-Zubayr b. 'Abd al-Muttalib, one of the nine Hashimites who stood firm with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, at Hunayn when all his companions fled, and there remained of them none but these, and Ayman b. Umm Ayman, who was the tenth of them; and Ayman was killed and these nine remained, until those who had been routed repented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And he, may God have mercy on him, was brave and bold, and was killed on the day of Ajnadayn in the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
159:3: But as for 'Abd Allah b. Zubayr b. al-'Awwam, he is certainly not the one meant; for he was a small child, not fit to be pointed to or turned to, let alone that Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, should make her bequest to him. For his birth was in the first year of the Hijra, and it is said in the second year, in Shawwal, as Ibn al-Athir said — besides that he was turned away from the People of the House, peace be upon them. The Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said: Al-Zubayr never ceased to be a man of us, the People of the House, until his ill-omened son grew up. [4] And God is the Knowing.
159:n2: His words “when it was broken”: in the passive, that is, it was broken by the blow of the accursed one. — the Bihar.
159:n4: Bahjat al-Amal fi Sharh Zubdat al-Maqal, vol. 5, p. 227.
160:0: Section [the sending by Zaynab, the daughter of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his Family), of a ransom for Abu al-'As her husband]. It is related from the masters of the campaigns and the transmitters of the reports: that when Quraysh marched to Badr, Abu al-'As, the son of Khadija's sister and the husband of Zaynab the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, marched with them; and he was taken among the captives on the day of Badr and brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and was with him among the prisoners. And when the people of Mecca sent for the ransom of their captives, Zaynab sent for the ransom of Abu al-'As her husband with property; and among what she sent was a necklace that had belonged to Khadija her mother, may God be pleased with her, with which she had brought her in to Abu al-'As on the night of her wedding to him. And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, saw it, he was moved with a deep tenderness for her and said to the Muslims: If you see fit to release her captive and to return to her what she has sent of the ransom, then do so. And they said: Yes, O Messenger of God; we ransom you with ourselves and our properties. So they returned to her what she had sent, and released Abu al-'As for her without ransom. [1]
160:1: Ibn Abi al-Hadid said: I read this report to the naqib Abu Ja'far Yahya b. Abi Zayd al-Basri al-'Alawi, and he said: Do you suppose that Abu Bakr and 'Umar did not witness this scene?!!
