160:2: Did not nobility and kindness require that Fatima's heart, peace be upon her, should be made glad with Fadak, and that it should be asked of the Muslims as a gift for her?
160:3: Is her station with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, less than the station of Zaynab her sister?!!
161:0: And she is the mistress of the women of the worlds!!! This, even if no right were established for her, neither by the gift nor by inheritance.
161:1: So I said to him: Fadak, by the requirement of the report which Abu Bakr related, had become a right of the rights of the Muslims; so it was not permitted him to take it from them. And he said: And the ransom of Abu al-'As had become a right of the rights of the Muslims, and the Messenger of God took it from them. So I said: The Messenger of God is the master of the Law, and the ruling is his ruling; and Abu Bakr is not so.
161:2: And he said: I did not say that Abu Bakr should have taken it from the Muslims by force and handed it to Fatima, peace be upon her. I said only that he should have persuaded the Muslims to yield it and asked it of them as a gift for her, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, asked for the ransom of Abu al-'As as a gift. Do you suppose that had he said: This is the daughter of your Prophet, may God bless him and his Family; she has come seeking these palm-trees — will you be glad in your souls to yield them to her? — that they would have refused her that?
161:3: So I said to him: The chief judge Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Jabbar b. Ahmad has said the like of that. He said: The two of them did not bring what is good in the law of nobility, even if what they brought was good in the religion. End of quotation. [2]
161:4: And excellent is what al-Sayyid al-Judhu'i said — and God reward him: — And Fatima came demanding the inheritance — from the Chosen One, and they did not give her his inheritance. — Would that I knew: why did they oppose the ways — of the Qur'an concerning her, when God had made them clear? — Was the verse of inheritance abrogated as regards her, — or did the two of them alter it after it was ordained? — Or do you hold that the verse of love did not — bring love for al-Zahra' in her kinship? — Then the two of them said: Your father brought this — as a proof out of their obstinacy, which they set up. — He said: For the prophets there is a ruling that they are not — inherited from, of old — and they rebuffed her. — Did the Prophet's daughter then not know that — the Prophet of guidance had uttered that? — Did a portion of Muhammad oppose what — he said? God forbid our Lady, God forbid! — She heard him say that, and then came — demanding the inheritance, in error and folly?
161:n2: Sharh al-Nahj, vol. 14, pp. 190-191; Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 19, p. 349.
162:0: — She was more God-fearing before God, and was — the most excellent of creation in chastity and purity. — Ask, for the voiding of their saying, the sura of the Ant, — and ask Maryam, which comes before Ta Ha. — In them both there is news of the inheritance of Yahya — and of Solomon, for whoever desires to be awakened. — So she called out and complained to God of that, — and her two eyes overflowed with her tears. — Then she said: A gift, then, from — my father the Chosen One? And they did not grant her the gift. — So she produced witnesses for it, and they said: — Her husband is a witness for her, and her two sons. — They did not admit the testimony of the two sons of the Messenger — of God, the guide of mankind, when they opposed her. — 'Ali was not truthful, nor was — Fatima, in their eyes, nor her two sons. — A household who did not know the ways of injustice, — so that it was confused and doubtful to them. — Was 'Atiq more God-fearing than they? — Ugly is the speaker of the absurd, and disgraced. — They made her swallow, after her father, — rage many times; and evil is what they made her swallow. — Would that I knew what harm it would have done the two of them, — in keeping the covenant of the Prophet, had they kept it. — It would have been an honouring of the Seal of the Messengers, the guide, — the bearer of glad tidings and the warner, had they honoured her. — And the fair thing would have been that they give her — Fadak, not that they cut it off from her entirely. — Do you suppose the Muslims would have blamed the two of them — for the giving, had they given it to her? — Was there beneath the green sky a daughter of a prophet, — truthful, speaking, trustworthy, other than her? — Daughter of whom? Mother of whom? Wife of whom? — Woe to him who set the example of wronging and harming her.
163:0: The Fourth Chapter On the greatness of her sorrow and her weeping for her father (may God bless him and his Family) and for herself, and the beginning of her illness, and the length of her stay in this world after her father, and the Commander of the Faithful's (peace be upon him) concealing of her grave by a charge from her, the peace of God be upon her Section When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, the small and the great and the men and the women were stricken with grief for him, and the wailing and the weeping over him grew great. And Medina became one clamour, shedding tears for him in streams, [1] and its people had an outcry of weeping like the outcry of the pilgrims when they raise their voices in the state of consecration. And there was none but a weeping man and a weeping woman, and a lamenting man and a lamenting woman. And his loss was grievous upon his goodly household, especially upon 'Ali, his cousin and his brother, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. For there came down upon him from the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, what he did not suppose the mountains, had they borne it, would have been able to rise under. And his household were between one in anguish who could not master his anguish nor restrain himself nor find strength to bear the crushing weight of what had come down upon him —
163:1: anguish having taken away his patience and bewildered his mind and come between him and understanding and being understood, and speaking and hearing — and the rest of the people, other than the Banu 'Abd al-Muttalib, between a consoler who bids patience and a sympathizer weeping for their weeping, in anguish for their anguish. And there was not among them all one more intense in sorrow than our Lady Fatima al-Zahra',
164:0: the blessings of God be upon her. For there entered upon her of sorrow what none knows but God, mighty and exalted. And her sorrow was ever renewed and her weeping ever more severe; her moaning would not still and her yearning would not quiet. And every day that came, her weeping was more than the first day.
164:1: The narrator said: So she sat for seven days; and when it was the eighth day she went out to visit her father's grave, and came on lamenting, stumbling in her skirts, seeing nothing for her tears and for the flowing of her weeping, until she drew near the noble grave, and she fainted. So the women hastened to her and sprinkled water upon her until she revived. And when she revived from her swoon,
164:2: she said: My strength has been taken from me, and my endurance has betrayed me, and my enemy gloats over me, and grief is my killer. O my father, I am left distracted and alone, bewildered and solitary. My voice has been quenched and my back is broken, and my living is embittered and my time made foul. I find, O my father, after you, no companion for my desolation, nor any that turns back my tears. Then she called out: O my father: — My sorrow for you is a sorrow ever new, — and my heart, by God, is captive and unyielding. — Every day my griefs increase in it, — and my dejection for you does not pass away. — O my father, who is there for the widows and the destitute, — and who for the community until the Day of Judgement? O my father, we have come, after you, to be among the oppressed. O my father, the people have come to turn away from us. So what tear at your parting does not pour forth, and what sorrow after you is not unending, and what eyelid after you is anointed with sleep? I have been struck, O my father, with the mighty calamity; and the affliction was no small thing. So your pulpit after you is desolate, and your prayer-niche is empty of your intimate discourse, and your grave is glad at your presence in it. Alas for you — until I come to you! Then she gave a deep breath and a moan at which her soul was near to going out; and then she said: — My patience has grown little and my solace has left me — after my loss of the Seal of the Prophets. — O eye, O eye, pour out the tear in a flood; [2] — woe to you, be not miserly with an outpouring of blood.
165:0: — O Messenger of the God, O chosen of God, — and shelter of the orphans and the weak: — if you could see the pulpit which you used to mount, — darkness has covered it after the light. — O my God, hasten my death swiftly; — life has been made bitter, O my Master. The narrator said: Then she returned to her dwelling and took to weeping and wailing, her night and her day, her tears not ceasing and her sighing not quieting. So the elders of the people of Medina gathered and came to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said to him: O Abu al-Hasan, Fatima weeps night and day, and not one of us can enjoy sleep by night upon our beds, nor by day have we any rest at our occupations and the seeking of our livelihoods. And we ask you to request of her that she weep either by night or by day. And he said, peace be upon him: Gladly and with honour.
165:1: So the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, came until he entered upon Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, and she was not recovering from weeping, and consolation availed her nothing. And when she saw him she quieted a little for him, and he said to her: O daughter of the Messenger of God, the elders of Medina ask me to request of you that you weep for your father either by night or by day. And she said: O Abu al-Hasan, how little is my stay among them, and how near my departure from their midst! By God, I shall not be silent by night nor by day until I join my father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to her: Do, O daughter of the Messenger of God, what seems good to you. Then he, peace be upon him, built for her a house in al-Baqi', set apart from Medina, called “the House of Sorrows”. And she, peace be upon her, when she rose in the morning, would set al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, before her and go out to al-Baqi' weeping; and she would not cease to be among the graves, weeping. And when the night came, the Commander of the Faithful would come to her and drive her along before him to her dwelling. [3]
166:0: Section [her verses at her father's grave (may God bless him and his Family)]. It is related that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, and there befell Fatima, peace be upon her, from the people what befell her, she kept to her bed, and her body wasted and her flesh melted away and her skin dried upon her bone, and she became like a phantom. [1]
166:1: And it is also related that she, the blessings of God be upon her, never ceased after her father to be bound about the head, wasted of body, broken in her pillar, weeping of eye, burning of heart, swooning hour after hour and saying to her two sons: Where is your father, who used to honour you and carry you time after time? Where is your father, who was of all people the most tender towards you?
166:2: He does not let you walk upon the ground; and I do not think he will ever open this door again, nor carry you upon his shoulder as he never ceased to do with you. [2]
166:3: So she was, the peace of God be upon her, as her father had foretold of that day of hers: sorrowful, distressed, weeping; remembering at one time the cutting off of the revelation from her house, and remembering at another the parting from her father; and growing desolate when the night covered her, for the loss of his voice which she used to listen to when he kept vigil with the Qur'an; and then seeing herself abased after she had been, in the days of her father, honoured.
166:n1: And al-khayal: what resembles a form to you in waking and in dream; and a black garment set upon a stick by which beasts are made to imagine something.
167:0: And she would elegize her father and say: — What is it to him who has smelt the earth of Ahmad — that he should never smell a perfume through all time? — Calamities were poured upon me which, had they — been poured upon the days, would have become nights. [3] And she also said: — When one dies on a day, the mention of him grows little; — but the mention of my father, since he died, by God, increases. — I remembered, when death parted us, — and I consoled myself for the Prophet Muhammad, — and I said to my soul: death is our road, — and whoever does not die on his day dies on the morrow. And she also said: — When my longing grows strong I visit your grave weeping, — I lament and I complain, and I do not see you answering me. — O dweller of the wilderness (a variant: of the dust), you have taught me weeping, — and the mention of you has made me forget all calamities. — And if you are hidden from me in the earth, — you were never absent from my sorrowing heart. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had washed the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, in his shirt; and Fatima, peace be upon her, would say: Show me the shirt. And when she smelt it she would faint. So when
167:n3: And in the margin of the printed copy of the book, from the author, may God have mercy on him: he said: al-Muhaqqiq said in al-Mu'tabar, and al-Shahid in al-Dhikra: it is related that she took a handful of the earth of the Prophet's grave, may God bless him and his Family, and set it upon her eye, and said: What is it — and so on.
168:0: the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, saw that, he hid it away. [4]
168:1: [Her weeping at hearing the mention of her father (may God bless him and his Family) in the call to prayer] And it is related that she said one day: I long to hear the voice of my father's caller giving the call to prayer. And that reached Bilal, who had refrained from the call to prayer after the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family; and he began the call. And when he said: God is greatest, God is greatest — she remembered her father and his days, and could not contain herself from weeping. And when he reached his words: “I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family” — Fatima, peace be upon her, gave a sob and fell upon her face and fainted. So the people said to Bilal: Hold back, O Bilal, for the daughter of the Messenger of God has departed this world — and they supposed that she had died. So he cut short his call and did not complete it. Then Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, revived, and asked him to complete the call; but he did not do it, and said to her: O mistress of women, I fear for you from what you bring upon yourself when you hear my voice in the call. So she excused him from that. [5]
168:2: And from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, that he said: Fatima, peace be upon her, lived after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, seventy-five days; she was not seen smiling nor laughing. She would come to the graves of the martyrs twice every week, on Monday and Thursday, and say: Here was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and here were the polytheists. [6]
168:3: And in another report: she used to pray there and supplicate until she died, the blessings of God be upon her. [7] And it is related from Mahmud b. Labid, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, was taken, Fatima, peace be upon her, used to come to the graves of the martyrs and to the grave of Hamza and weep there. And one day I came to the grave of Hamza, may God have mercy on him, and found her weeping there. So I gave her time until she had quieted, and then I came to her
169:0: and greeted her and said: O mistress of women, by God you have cut the cords of my heart [8] with your weeping. And she said: O Abu 'Umar, it is right for me to weep; for I have been stricken in the best of fathers, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. Oh, my longing for the Messenger of God! Then she began to say: — When one dies on a day, the mention of him grows little; — but the mention of my father, since he died, by God, is greater. [9] And from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, remained after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, sixty days; then she fell ill and her sickness grew severe. And of her supplication in her illness was: O Living, O Self-Subsisting, by Your mercy I seek help — so help me. O God, remove me far from the Fire and admit me to the Garden and join me to my father Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, would say to her: May God grant you health and keep you. And she would say: O Abu al-Hasan, how swift is the meeting with God! And she charged him to marry Umama bint Abi al-'As, and said: She is my sister's daughter, and she will be tender to my children. [10]
169:1: [Her charge to 'Ali, peace be upon them both] And in another report she said to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: I have a need of you, O Abu al-Hasan. He said: It shall be fulfilled, O daughter of the Messenger of God. And she said: I adjure you by God and by the right of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, that Abu Bakr and 'Umar should not pray over me. For I have never concealed a saying from you. And she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to me: O Fatima, you are the first of my household to join me. And I
169:n8: Niyat: a thick vein by which the heart is suspended.
170:0: disliked to grieve you. [11] And from Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, who said: The beginning of Fatima's illness, peace be upon her, was after fifty nights from the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And she knew that it was death; so she gathered herself for that, charging 'Ali, peace be upon him, with her affair and giving him her bequest and making her covenants with him. And the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, was in anguish at that, and obeyed her in all that she commanded him. And she said: O Abu al-Hasan, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, made a covenant with me and told me that I am the first of his family to join him; and there is no escape from what there is no escape from. So be patient at the command of God, and be content with His decree. He said: And she charged him with her washing and her preparation and her burial by night; and he did so. [12]
170:1: And from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Fatima, peace be upon her, saw the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, in her sleep. She said: So I complained to him of what befell us after him. She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, said to me: Yours is the abode of the hereafter which has been prepared for the God-fearing; and you shall come to me before long. [13]
171:0: Section [“the two shaykhs' asking leave to visit her, peace be upon her”]. When Fatima, peace be upon her, fell ill with the illness in which she died, she charged 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, that he should conceal her affair and hide news of her and inform no one of her illness. And he did that, the peace of God be upon him, and nursed her himself; and Asma' bint 'Umays helped him in that, keeping it secret as she had charged. [1] And the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, had foretold that illness of hers, and said, after mentioning what would befall her of wrong and injustice: Then the pain shall begin in her and she shall fall ill; and God shall send to her Maryam bint 'Imran to nurse her and to keep her company in her sickness — the report. [2]
171:1: And when she grew grave, and the two men learned of that, they came to her to visit her and asked leave of her; and she refused to give them leave. So 'Umar came to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and said to him: Abu Bakr is an old man, tender of heart, and he was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, in the cave, and his companionship is his. And we have come to her more than this once, many times, seeking leave to enter upon her, and she refuses to give us leave. So if you see fit to ask leave for us to enter upon her, then do so. He said: Yes. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, entered upon Fatima, peace be upon her, and said: O daughter of the Messenger of God, there has been
171:n1: Amali al-Mufid, p. 281; Bihar, vol. 43, p. 211.
172:0: from these two men what you have seen; and they have come repeatedly, many times, and you have turned them back and not given them leave. And they have asked me to ask leave for them to enter upon you.
172:1: And she said: By God, I shall not give them leave, nor shall I speak a word to them from my head until I meet my father and complain of them to him for what they have done and what they have committed against me. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: I have guaranteed them that. She said: If you have guaranteed them something, then the house is your house and the women follow the men; I shall not oppose you in anything. So give leave to whom you wish. So he went out, peace be upon him, and gave them leave.
172:2: And when their eyes fell upon Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, they greeted her, and she did not return the greeting to them, and turned her face away from them. So they moved round and faced her face, until she had done this several times; and she said: O 'Ali, draw the cloth across. And she said to the women around her: Turn my face away. And when they had turned her face away, the two of them moved round to her and asked her to be reconciled to them and to pardon what had come from them towards her. So Fatima, peace be upon her, said: I adjure you both by God — do you remember that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, brought you out in the middle of the night over a thing that had happened in the affair of 'Ali, peace be upon him? And they said: By God, yes. And she said: I adjure you both by God — did you hear the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, say: Fatima is a part of me and I am of her; whoever harms her has harmed me, and whoever harms me has harmed God; and whoever harms her after my death is as one who harmed her in my lifetime, and whoever harmed her in my lifetime has harmed her after my death? They said: By God, yes. So she said: Praise belongs to God. Then she said: O God, I call You to witness — and bear witness, you who are present with me — that these two have harmed me in my lifetime and at my death. By God, I shall not speak a word to you from my head until I meet my Lord and complain of you to Him for what you have done to me and committed against me. [3]
172:3: And in another report she raised her hand to the sky and said: O God, these two have harmed me; so I complain of them to You and to Your Messenger. No, by God, I shall never be reconciled to you, until I meet my father, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and tell him what you have done — and he shall be the judge between you. He said: So at that Abu
173:0: Bakr called out in woe and ruin and said: Would that my mother had not borne me! [4] And 'Umar said: How strange of the people — how did they put you in charge of their affairs!
173:1: And you are an old man grown senile, who is distressed at a woman's anger and rejoices at her being pleased. And what is there for one whom a woman has angered? And the two of them rose and went out. [5]
173:2: And when the two of them had gone out, Fatima, peace be upon her, said to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: Have you done what you wished?
173:3: He said: Yes. She said: Then will you do what I command you?
173:4: He said: Yes. She said: Then I adjure you by God that they should not pray over my bier nor stand at my grave. [6]
173:5: And it is related that she said to Asma' bint 'Umays: I have found ugly what is done with women — that a cloth is thrown over the woman and it describes her to whoever sees. And she said: I have wasted away and my flesh has gone. Will you not make for me something to cover me? Asma' said: When I was in the land of Abyssinia I saw them make a thing. Shall I not make it for you, and if it pleases you I shall make it for you?
173:6: She said: Yes. So she called for a bier and turned it upon its face, then called for palm-branches and bound them to its legs, then covered it with a cloth; and she said: Thus I saw them do. So she said, the peace of God be upon her: Make the like of it for me; cover me — may God cover you from the Fire. [7]
173:7: And it is related that when she saw what Asma' had fashioned she smiled; and she was not seen smiling except on that day. And she said: How good this is and how fair! By it the woman is not known from the man. [8]
173:8: [The visit of the women of the Emigrants and the Ansar to her, and what she said in answer to them] In al-Ihtijaj, Suwayd b. Ghafala said: When our Lady Fatima, peace be upon her, fell ill with the illness in which she died, the women of the Emigrants and the Ansar came in upon her to visit her, and said to her:
173:n6: The wording of the text itself is not found in the Bihar nor in al-'Awalim, but its sense is found, widely transmitted.
173:n7: Al-'Awalim, vol. 6, p. 291; al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 213.
174:0: How have you risen from your illness, O daughter of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family?
174:1: So she praised God and blessed her father, and said: I have risen, by God, loathing your world, detesting your men. I have spat them out after I had chewed them, and hated them after I had tested them. So ugliness upon blunted blades, and play after earnestness, and the striking of the smooth rock, and the splitting of the spear-shaft, and the corruption of opinions and the slipping of desires! “And evil is what their souls have sent before for them, that God is angry with them; and in the punishment they shall abide.” No doubt of it: I have fastened its halter upon them and loaded upon them its burden and poured upon them its raids. So mutilation and ruin and barrenness and distance be upon the wrongdoing people! Woe to them — how did they shift it away from the firm mountains of the messengership and the foundations of prophethood and its evidence, and the place of the descent of the revelation and of the Trustworthy Spirit, and from those skilled in the affairs of this world and of religion? Lo, that is the manifest loss! And what was it that they held against Abu al-Hasan? They held against him, by God, the severity of his sword, and the little care he had for his own death, and the weight of his tread, and the exemplary punishment of his onslaught, and his fierceness in the cause of God.
174:2: And by God, had they inclined away from the clear highway and swerved from accepting the plain proof, he would have brought them back to it and carried them upon it, and would have led them a gentle leading in which the nose-ring does not wound and the traveller does not tire and the rider does not weary; and he would have brought them down to a watering-place flowing, pure, clear and abundant, whose two banks overflow and whose sides are not made muddy — until she said, the peace of God be upon her: They have, by God, exchanged the tail-feathers for the wing-feathers and the rump for the withers. So may the noses of a people be rubbed in the dust who “reckon that they are doing good work — lo, they are the corrupters, but they do not perceive.” Woe to them! “Is he who guides to the truth worthier to be followed, or he who does not guide unless he is guided? What ails you? How do you judge?” Now by my life, she has conceived; so wait a while until she gives birth; then milk, in place of a bowlful, fresh blood and a destroying poison. There the falsifiers shall lose, and those who come after shall know the consequence of what the first laid down. Then be easy in your souls concerning your world, and be calm of heart for the trials, and receive the glad tidings of a cutting sword and the onslaught of a transgressing oppressor and a general distress and a tyranny from the wrongdoers that will leave your spoil scant and your gathering reaped. So alas for you — and where are you bound? “While it has been made blind to you: shall we compel you to it while you are averse to it?”
174:3: Suwayd b. Ghafala said: So the women repeated her words to their men; and a group of the notables of the Emigrants and the Ansar came to her excusing themselves and said: O mistress of women, had Abu al-Hasan, peace
175:0: be upon him, mentioned this matter to us before we bound the covenant and made firm the contract, we would not have turned from him to another. And she said, peace be upon her: Away from me! There is no excuse after your excusing, and no command after your falling short. (9)
175:1: And in the Bihar, from al-'Ayyashi, he said: Umm Salama came in upon Fatima, peace be upon her, and said to her: How have you risen from your night, O daughter of the Messenger of God?
175:2: She said: I have risen between grief and distress: the loss of the Prophet and the wronging of the legatee. His veil has been rent, by God — I have risen between grief and distress: the loss of the Prophet and the wronging of the legatee; his veil has been rent, by God — of one whose leadership was taken over (10) contrary to what God laid down in the revelation and what the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, appointed in the interpretation. But these are the rancours of Badr and the blood-debts of Uhud, over which the hearts of hypocrisy were lying in wait for an opportunity for the slanderers. So when the affair became their target, they sent upon us the downpours of the traces from the cloud of discord; and the string of faith is cut from the bows of their breasts. And evil is what they have done regarding what God promised of the guarding of the messengership and the sheltering of the believers. They secured their gain — the deception of this world — after the seeking of help from one who slew their fathers in the places of distress and the stations of martyrdom. (11) (9) Al-Ihtijaj, vol. 1, p. 147. (10) In the Bihar: seized.
175:3: (11) Al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 156; 'Awalim al-'Ulum, vol. 6, p. 250. And the report is found in al-Manaqib, vol. 2, p. 203. Her words, peace be upon her, “'a'ifa”: that is, loathing.
175:4: And “al-qaliya”: the detesting. “Lafaztuhum”: that is, I cast them out and threw them away. And “al-'ajm”: the chewing. And “shana'ahu”, on the pattern of mana'ahu: he hated him. And “sabartuhum”: that is, I tested them.
175:5: And “al-fulul”, with damma: the plural of fall, with fatha, which is the notch and the break in the edge of a sword. And “al-khawr”, with fatha: weakness. And “al-qanat”: the spear.
175:6: And “al-khatal”: corrupt speech. And “the striking of the smooth rock”: al-safat is the smooth stone — that is, you made yourselves a striking-place for your adversaries until they struck your rock. And “the splitting of the spear-shaft”: its cleaving. “Al-awq”: the weight. “Shannat”: that is, she scattered. Al-jad': the cutting of the nose. Al-'aqr: the wounding. And al-tabin: the shrewd and skilful. And al-sujh, with two dammas: the gentle and easy. And al-kalm: the wound.
175:7: And al-khishash, with kasra: what is put in the nose of a camel. Al-namir: the water that grows in abundance — meaning a spring whose water does not cease. And the two daffas of a river: its two banks. And tatfah: that is, it fills until it overflows.
175:8: And al-tarnuq: the mud that is in rivers and watercourses. And the meaning is that the water does not diminish so that the mud and the black slime appear from the two sides of the river. Al-dhunaba: the tail of the bird.
175:9: Dhu'aq: a killing disease. “The consequence of what the first laid down”: meaning its outcome.
175:10: Al-ja'sh: the rising and the agitation. Ghashama: that is, he wronged.
175:11: I say: the explanation of the obscure words in her speech, peace be upon her, is mostly from the Bihar of the 'allama al-Majlisi, may God have mercy on him.
176:0: Section [“her charge to 'Ali, peace be upon them both, to conceal her grave”]. From Rawdat al-Wa'izin and others: Fatima (peace be upon her) fell severely ill and remained forty nights in her illness until she died, the blessings of God be upon her. And when her death was announced to her, she called Umm Ayman and Asma' bint 'Umays and sent for 'Ali, peace be upon him, and had him brought, and said: O son of my uncle, my death has been announced to me, and I do not see what is with me to be anything but that I am joining my father hour by hour; and I charge you with things that are in my heart. 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to her: Charge me with what you wish, O daughter of the Messenger of God. And he sat at her head and put out whoever was in the house. Then she said: O son of my uncle, you have never known me to be a liar nor a betrayer, nor have I opposed you since I lived with you. And he said: God forbid! You are more knowing of God and more dutiful and more God-fearing and more noble and more severe in fear of God than that I should reproach you with opposing me. Your parting and your loss are grievous to me — but it is a matter from which there is no escape. By God, you have renewed upon me the calamity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and your death and your loss are grievous. So truly we belong to God and truly to Him we return — from a calamity, how harrowing and painful and bitter and sorrowful! This, by God, is a calamity for which there is no consolation, and an affliction for which there is no substitute. Then they both wept together for a while, and 'Ali, peace be upon him, took her head and drew her to his breast, and then said: Charge me with what you wish; for you will find me carrying it out as you have commanded me, and choosing your command over my own.
177:0: Then she said: May God reward you on my behalf with the best of rewards, O son of the uncle of the Messenger of God. [1]
177:1: Then she charged him to marry after her Umama, the daughter of her sister Zaynab; and to make for her a bier; and that none of those who had wronged her and taken her right should attend her funeral; and that none of them nor of their followers should pray over her; and that he should bury her at night, when the eyes had quietened and the sights had gone to sleep.
177:2: And from Misbah al-Anwar, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, he said: When Fatima, peace be upon her, was at the point of death, she charged 'Ali, peace be upon him, and said: When I die, undertake yourself my washing, and prepare me, and pray over me, and lower me into my grave, and lay me in the niche, and level the earth over me, and sit at my head facing my face, and recite much of the Qur'an and of supplication; for it is an hour in which the dead has need of the companionship of the living. And I entrust you to God, exalted, and charge you with good concerning my children. Then she drew Umm Kulthum to herself and said to him: When she comes of age, hers is what is in the house; then God is for her. And when she died, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, did that — and so on. [2]
177:3: And it is related that she said to the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him: When I die, inform no one save Umm Salama and Umm Ayman and Fidda; and of the men, my two sons and al-'Abbas [a variant: and 'Abd Allah b. 'Abbas] and Salman and 'Ammar and al-Miqdad and Abu Dharr and Hudhayfa. And she said: I have released you from the prohibition of seeing me after my death; so be with the women among those who wash me. And do not bury me except by night, and let no one know my grave. [3]
177:4: And from Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his forefathers, peace be upon them, he said: When death came to Fatima she wept; and the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said to her: My lady, what makes you weep?
177:5: She said: I weep for what you will meet after me. He said to her: Do not weep; for by God that is a small thing to me in the cause of God. He said: And she charged him that the two shaykhs should not be informed of her; and he did so. [4]
177:6: And the Shaykh of the Community related: that when Fatima, peace be upon her, grew grave, al-'Abbas b. 'Abd
177:n1: Al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 191; Rawdat al-Wa'izin, vol. 1, p. 151; 'Awalim al-'Ulum, vol. 6, p. 274.
178:0: al-Muttalib came to her visiting. And it was said to him: She is grave, and no one enters upon her. So he went away to his house and sent to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and said to his messenger: Say to him: O son of my brother, your uncle gives you greeting and says to you: By God, there has come upon me suddenly of grief, at the sickness of the beloved of the Messenger of God and the coolness of his eyes and of my eyes, Fatima, peace be upon her, what has broken me. And I think she is the first of us to join the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family; and God chooses for her and bestows upon her and brings her near to Him. So if there be of her affair what there is no escape from, then let me gather for you — I am your ransom — the Emigrants and the Ansar, that they may attain the reward in attending her and praying over her; and in that is a beauty for the religion.
178:1: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to his messenger — the narrator said, and he is 'Ammar: I was present with him: Convey to my uncle the greeting and say: May you never lack your compassion and your tenderness. I have understood your counsel, and your opinion has its merit. Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, has never ceased to be wronged, barred from her right and pushed away from her inheritance. The charge of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, concerning her was not kept, nor was his right regarded concerning her, nor the right of God, mighty and exalted. And God suffices as judge and as avenger from the wrongdoers. And I ask you, O uncle, to permit me to leave aside what you have advised; for she charged me with the concealing of her affair — and so on. [5]
178:2: And the two parties related from Umm Salma, the wife of Abu Rafi', who said: Fatima, peace be upon her, suffered the sickness in which she was taken, and I was nursing her. And one day she rose calmer than she had been; and 'Ali, peace be upon him, went out for some need of his. And she said: Pour out for me water for a washing. So I poured, and she rose and washed with the best of washings. Then she put on her new garments, and then said: Spread out my bed for me in the middle of the house. Then she faced the qibla and lay down and said: I am to be taken, and I have washed; so let no one uncover me. Then she put her cheek upon her hand, and died, the blessings of God be upon her. [6]
178:3: [Her greeting, the peace of God be upon her, to Gabriel and the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, when they came down to her] And it is related that she died between the sunset and the evening prayers; and that when death came upon her she looked a piercing look, then
178:n5: Amali al-Shaykh, vol. 1, p. 155; al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 209.
178:n6: 'Awalim al-'Ulum, Fatima al-Zahra', vol. 6, p. 276; al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 183.
179:0: said: Peace be upon Gabriel; peace be upon the Messenger of God. O God, with Your Messenger. O God, in Your good pleasure and Your neighbourhood and Your abode, the abode of peace. Then she said: Do you see what I see? And it was said to her: What do you see?
179:1: She said: These are the processions of the people of the heavens; and this is Gabriel; and this is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and he says: My little daughter, come forward — for what is before you is better for you. [7]
179:2: And from Zayd b. 'Ali: that she, the peace of God be upon her, when death came upon her, gave the greeting to Gabriel and to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and to the angel of death; and they heard the stirring of the angels and found a fragrance of perfume like the sweetest of perfume. [8]
179:3: And from Asma' bint 'Umays, who said: When death came to Fatima, peace be upon her, she said to me: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, when death came to him, with camphor from the Garden; and he divided it in three: a third for himself, a third for 'Ali, peace be upon him, and a third for me — and it was forty dirhams. And she said: O Asma', bring me the remainder of my father's embalming from such and such a place, and set it at my head. Then she wrapped herself in her cloth and said: Wait for me a little while, then call me; and if I answer you, well; and if not, then know that I have come to my father (a variant: my Lord).
179:4: The narrator said: So Asma' waited for her a little while, then called her, and she did not answer. So she called: O daughter of Muhammad the Chosen! O daughter of the noblest whom women have borne! O daughter of the best who ever trod the pebbles! O daughter of him who was from his Lord at two bows' length or nearer! He said: And she did not answer her. So she uncovered the cloth from her face, and there she was, departed from this world. So she fell upon her, kissing her and saying: O Fatima, when you come to your father, the Messenger of God, give him greeting from Asma' bint 'Umays. Then Asma' tore her collar and went out; and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, met her, and said: Where is our mother? And she was silent. So the two of them entered the house, and there she was, stretched out. And al-Husayn, peace be upon him, moved her, and there she was, dead. And he said: O my brother, may God reward you in the matter of our mother. And al-Hasan, peace be upon him, fell upon her, kissing her again and again and saying: O my mother, speak to me before
180:0: my spirit parts from my body. She said: And al-Husayn, peace be upon him, came forward — and the two of them told him of the death — kissing her feet and saying: O my mother, I am your son al-Husayn; speak to me before my heart is split and I die. Asma' said to them: O sons of the Messenger of God, go to your father 'Ali, peace be upon him, and tell him of your mother's death. So the two of them went out calling: O Muhammad! O Ahmad! Today your death is renewed for us, since our mother has died. Then they told 'Ali, peace be upon him, and he was in the mosque; and he fainted, until water was sprinkled upon him and he revived. And he was saying, peace be upon him: With whom is the consolation, O daughter of Muhammad? By you I used to be consoled; so in what is the consolation after you? [9]
180:1: Al-Mas'udi said: And when she was taken, peace be upon her, 'Ali, peace be upon him, was in a severe anguish, and his weeping grew intense and his moaning and yearning appeared; and he said concerning that: — For every gathering of two friends there is a parting, — and all that falls short of death (a variant: of separation) is little. — And my losing of one after another (a variant: of Fatima after Ahmad) — is a proof that no friend endures. The narrator said: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, carried al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, until he brought them into the house of Fatima, peace be upon her. And at her head was Asma', weeping and saying: And O orphans of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family! We used to be consoled after you. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, uncovered her face, and there was a slip of paper at her head. He looked into it, and in it was: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. This is what Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has charged. She charged, and she bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, is His servant and His Messenger, and that the Garden is true and the Fire is true, and that the Hour is coming, no doubt of it, and that God raises up whoever is in the graves. O 'Ali, I am Fatima the daughter of Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family; God married me to you that I might be that in this world and the next. You are worthier of me than another. Embalm me and wash me and shroud me by night, and pray over me and bury me by night, and let no one know. And I entrust you to God, and give greeting to my children until
180:n9: Kashf al-Ghumma, p. 500; al-Bihar, vol. 43, pp. 214-186-187.
181:0: the Day of Resurrection. [10] Her shrouding and her washing, peace be upon her, by night The narrator said: And the people of Medina cried out with one cry, and the women of the Banu Hashim gathered in her house and screamed with one scream at which Medina was near to being shaken, saying: O our mistress! O daughter of the Messenger of God! And the people came on like the mane of a horse to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and he was sitting with al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, before him, weeping; and the people wept at their weeping. And Umm Kulthum came out with a veil upon her, trailing her skirt, wrapped in her cloak, her sobbing upon her, [11] saying: O my father! O Messenger of God! Now in truth have we lost you, a loss after which there is no meeting ever. And the people gathered and sat, clamouring and waiting for the bier to come out that they might pray over her. So Abu Dharr, may God have mercy on him, came out and said: Disperse; for the bringing out of the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, has been put off this evening. So the people rose and dispersed. And when the night grew dark, the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, washed her, and none was present at her but he, and al-Hasan and al-Husayn and Zaynab and Umm Kulthum, peace be upon them, and Fidda her maidservant, and Asma' bint 'Umays, the mercy of God be upon them both. [12]
181:1: And Asma' said: Fatima, peace be upon her, charged me that when she died none should wash her but I and 'Ali, peace be upon him; so I helped 'Ali in washing her. [13]
181:2: And it is related that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said when he washed Fatima, peace be upon her: O God, she is Your bondwoman and the daughter of Your Messenger and Your chosen one and Your elect from among Your creation. O God, prompt her with her proof and make great her evidence and raise her degree and join her with her father Muhammad, may God bless him
181:n10: Al-Bihar, vol. 43, p. 214; 'Awalim al-'Ulum, vol. 6, p. 278.
181:n11: Tasabbaja al-rajul bi-l-sabja: he wore it; and al-sabja is a black garment. And in al-'Awalim: tashabuha.
182:0: and his Family. And it is related that she was dried with the mantle with which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, had been dried. And when 'Ali, peace be upon him, had washed her, he laid her upon the bier and said to al-Hasan, peace be upon him: Call Abu Dharr for me. So he called him; and the two of them carried her to the place of prayer, and with him were al-Hasan and al-Husayn; and he prayed over her. [14]
182:1: And in a report of Waraqa, 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: By God, I undertook her affair and washed her in her shift and did not uncover it from her; for by God she was blessed, pure and purified. Then I embalmed her from the remainder of the embalming of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and shrouded her and wrapped her in her shrouds. And when I was about to tie the mantle, I called: O Umm Kulthum, O Zaynab, O Sukayna, O Fidda, O Hasan, O Husayn — come, take your provision from your mother; for this is the parting, and the meeting is in the Garden. So al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, came forward calling: Alas for a grief that shall never be quenched, at the loss of our grandfather Muhammad the Chosen and our mother Fatima al-Zahra'! O mother of al-Hasan, O mother of al-Husayn, when you meet our grandfather Muhammad the Chosen, give him greeting from us and say to him: We have remained after you two orphans in the abode of this world. So the Commander of the Faithful, 'Ali, peace be upon him, said: I call God to witness that she yearned and moaned and stretched out her hands and drew them to her breast for a long while. And behold, a caller from the sky called: O Abu al-Hasan, lift them from her; for by God they have made the angels of the heavens weep. The beloved has longed for the Beloved. He said, peace be upon him: So I lifted them from her breast. [15]
182:2: And it is related that Kathir b. 'Abbas wrote upon the edges of the shroud of the Mistress of Women, “Fatima, peace be upon her”: She bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. [16]
183:0: And it appears from the report of Misbah al-Anwar that the garments of her shroud were coarse and rough; for it is related that when death came to Fatima, peace be upon her, she called for water and washed, then called for perfume and embalmed herself with it, then called for the garments of her shroud, and she was brought coarse, rough garments, and she wrapped herself in them — and so on. [17]
183:1: And it is also related that she was shrouded in seven garments. [18]
183:2: In the report of Rawdat al-Wa'izin he said: And when the eyes had quietened and a part of the night had passed, 'Ali and al-Hasan and al-Husayn, peace be upon them, and 'Ammar and al-Miqdad and 'Aqil and al-Zubayr and Abu Dharr and Salman and Burayda and a number of the Banu Hashim and his close companions brought her out; and they prayed over her and buried her in the middle of the night. And 'Ali, peace be upon him, levelled around her false graves to the number of seven, so that her grave should not be known. [19]
183:3: And from Misbah al-Anwar, from Ja'far b. Muhammad, peace be upon them, that he was asked: How many takbirs did the Commander of the Faithful say over Fatima, peace be upon her?
183:4: And he said: The Commander of the Faithful would say a takbir, and Gabriel would say a takbir, and the angels brought near — until the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had said five. And it was said to him: And where did he pray over her? He said: In her house; then he brought her out. [20]
183:5: [('Ali's) returning of the trust, peace be upon him, and his complaint at the grave of the Prophet (may God bless him and his Family)] And al-Shaykh Abu Ja'far al-Tusi, may God have mercy on him, related that when the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, had buried Fatima, the blessings of God be upon her, and effaced the place of her grave, and his hand had come away from the earth of the grave, grief surged in him and he let his tears go upon his cheeks, and turned his face towards the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, and said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. Peace be upon you from your daughter and your beloved and the coolness of your eye, and your visitor
184:0: and she who lies this night in the dust in your plot [a variant: in your Baqi'], whom God chose for swiftness of joining you. My patience, O Messenger of God, has grown little for your chosen one, and my endurance has weakened for the Mistress of Women. Except that in taking your way as my pattern, and in the sorrow that has come upon me at parting from you, there is a place of consolation. For I laid you down in the niche of your grave after your soul had flowed out upon my breast, and I closed your eyes with my hand and undertook your affair myself.
184:1: Yes, and in the Book of God is the fairest acceptance: truly we belong to God and truly to Him we return. The trust has been taken back and the pledge has been seized; and al-Zahra' has been snatched away. How ugly are the green sky and the dusty earth, O Messenger of God! As for my sorrow, it is unending; and as for my night, it is sleepless. Sorrow shall not leave my heart until God chooses for me your abode in which you dwell — a festering grief [21] and a stirring care. How swiftly has God parted us! And to God I complain. And your daughter shall tell you of your community's banding together against me and against her, wronging her of her right; so ask her of the state. For how much burning was surging in her breast for which she found no way to pour it out! And she shall say: “And God shall judge between us, and He is the best of judges.”
184:2: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God — the peace of one taking leave, not of one wearied nor of one who detests. For if I turn away, it is not out of weariness; and if I stay, it is not out of ill thought concerning what God has promised the patient. Patience is more blessed and more comely. And but for the overpowering of those who have gained mastery over us, I would have made my stay at your grave a binding thing and my tarrying beside it a retreat, and I would have wailed the wailing of the bereaved mother at the greatness of the affliction. So before the eye of God is your daughter buried in secret, and her right wronged by force, and her inheritance withheld openly; and the covenant is not long past, nor has the memory of you worn out. And to God, O Messenger of God, is the complaint; and in you is the fairest consolation. May God bless him and his Family, and the mercy of God and His blessings. [22]
184:3: And excellently did he say who said: — And for what cause is a portion of the Chosen One — buried in secret, and her earth effaced? — So she passed away, the greatest of people in grief, — a bitterness [a variant: a bite] in the mouth of time for him who contained her. — And she dwelt where the people do not see a dwelling for her — what sanctity her dwelling-place enfolds!
184:n21: A festering grief: that is, an illness with pus. Qayyaha al-jurh: it became suppurating.
185:0: And from Misbah al-Anwar, from Abu 'Abd Allah, from his forefathers, peace be upon them: that the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, when he laid Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, God bless them both and their families, in the grave, said: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. In the name of God, and by God, and upon the creed of the Messenger of God, Muhammad b. 'Abd Allah, may He bless him and his Family. I have delivered you up, O most truthful one, to Him who is worthier of you than I, and I have been content for you with what God, exalted, has been content for you. Then he recited: “From it We created you, and into it We return you, and from it We shall bring you forth another time.” And when he had levelled the earth over her, he commanded her grave and water was sprinkled upon it. Then he sat at her grave weeping and grieving; and al-'Abbas took his hand and led him away. [23]
185:1: ['Umar's dispute with 'Ali, peace be upon him] The narrator said: And al-Baqi', on the night she was buried, “the peace of God be upon her”, rose with forty new graves in it. And when the Muslims learned of her death they came to al-Baqi' and found in it forty graves; and her grave was confused for them among the rest of the graves. So the people clamoured and blamed one another and said: Your Prophet left among you only one daughter; she dies and is buried, and you did not attend her death nor the prayer over her, and you do not know her grave. Then the holders of the affair among them said: Bring from the women of the Muslims those who will dig up these graves until we find her, that we may pray over her and visit her grave.
185:2: And that reached the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him. So he went out in anger, his eyes reddened and the veins of his neck swollen, wearing his yellow tunic that he used to wear at every grim encounter, leaning upon his sword Dhu al-Fiqar, until he came to al-Baqi'. And the warner hastened to the people and they said: This is 'Ali b. Abi Talib; he has come as you see him, swearing by God that if a stone of these graves is moved, he will set the sword upon the last of them.
185:3: So 'Umar met him, and those of his companions who were with him, and said to him: What ails you, O Abu al-Hasan?
185:4: By God, we shall dig up her grave and we shall pray over her. So 'Ali, peace be upon him, struck his hand to the gathers of his garment and shook him, then dashed
186:0: him to the ground and said to him: O son of the black woman, as for my right, I have left it for fear that the people should turn back from their religion. But as for the grave of Fatima, peace be upon her — by Him in whose hand is the soul of 'Ali, if you and your companions aim at anything of that, I shall water the earth with your blood. So if you wish, then come forward, O 'Umar. Then Abu Bakr met him and said: O Abu al-Hasan, by the right of the Messenger of God and by the right of Him who is above the Throne, let him go; for we shall do nothing that you dislike. He said: So he let him go, and the people dispersed and did not return to that. [24]
186:1: And in al-Safi, related from 'Ilal al-Shara'i', after mentioning that 'Ali, peace be upon him, brought out the bier and the fire was kindled in palm-branches, and he walked with the bier with the fire until he prayed over her and buried her by night: He said: And when Abu Bakr and 'Umar rose in the morning, they returned to visit Fatima, peace be upon her; and they met a man of Quraysh and said to him: Where have you come from?
186:2: He said: I have consoled 'Ali over Fatima. They said: And has she died?
186:3: He said: Yes, and she was buried in the middle of the night. So the two of them were in a severe anguish. Then they came to 'Ali, peace be upon him, and met him and said to him: By God, you have left nothing of our troubling and our vexation; and this is only from something in your breast against us. Is this anything but as you washed the Messenger of God apart from us and did not bring us in with you; and as you taught your son to shout at Abu Bakr: Come down from the pulpit of my father?
186:4: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to them: Will you believe me if I swear to you?
186:5: They said: Yes. So he swore; and 'Ali, peace be upon him, brought them into the mosque and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family, charged me and had laid it upon me that no one should look upon his nakedness but his cousin. So I washed him while the angels turned him, and al-Fadl b. al-'Abbas handed me the water, and his eyes were bound with a cloth. And I wished to pull off the shirt, and a caller cried out at me from the house — I heard the voice and did not see the form: Do not pull off the shirt of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his Family. And I heard the voice repeating it to me. So I put my hand in from within the shirt and washed him. Then the shroud was brought to me and I shrouded him; then I pulled off the shirt after I had shrouded him.
186:6: And as for al-Hasan my son, you both know, and the people of Medina know, that he used to step over the rows until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, while he was prostrating, and would mount upon his back; and the Prophet, may God bless him
187:0: and his Family, would rise with his hand upon al-Hasan's back and the other upon his knee, until he completed the prayer. They said: Yes, we have known that. Then he said: You both know, and the people of Medina know, that al-Hasan used to run to the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, and mount upon his neck, and al-Hasan would let his legs hang down upon the breast of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, until the gleam of his two anklets was seen from the far end of the mosque, while the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, was preaching; and he would not cease to be upon his neck until the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family, finished his sermon, with al-Hasan upon his neck. So when the child saw another upon the pulpit of his father, that weighed heavily upon him. By God, I did not command him to that, nor did he do it by my command.
187:1: And as for Fatima, she is the woman for whom I asked leave for you to enter; and you both saw what came of her speech to you. By God, she charged me that you should not attend her funeral nor the prayer over her; and I was not one to oppose her command and her charge to me concerning you. So 'Umar said: Leave aside this muttering of yours. I shall go to the graves and dig her up, that I may pray over her.
187:2: So 'Ali, peace be upon him, said to him: By God, if you went aiming at anything of that — and you know that you would not reach it until that in which your two eyes are had been struck away from you — for I would deal with you with nothing but the sword before you reached anything of that. So there fell between 'Ali and 'Umar words, until they wrangled and reviled one another; and the Emigrants and the Ansar gathered and said: By God, we are not content with this, that it should be said concerning the cousin of the Messenger of God and his brother and his legatee. And discord was near to falling out; so the two of them parted. [25]
187:3: From 'Ali b. 'Isa al-Irbili, who said: One of the companions recited to me, of the qadi Abu Bakr Qurai'a: — O you who ask persistently — about every feeble knotty question: — do not uncover what is covered, — for perhaps you would uncover a carcass. — And many a thing concealed in this way — is like the drum beneath the coverlet. — The answer is indeed ready, — but I hide it out of fear.
188:0: — Were it not for the aggression of a flock — whose governance the caliph has cast aside, — and the swords of enemies by which — our skulls are forever split, [26] — I would have spread out of the secrets of the Family of Muhammad — rare and choice matters — that would make you need nothing of what Malik — and Abu Hanifa have related, — and I would have shown you [27] that al-Husayn — was struck down on the day of the Saqifa, — and for what cause the noble Fatima — was laid in the niche by night, — and how she kept your two shaykhs — from treading her lofty chamber. — Alas for the daughter of Muhammad: — she died of her anguish, sorrowing. [28] Al-Shaykh al-Kulayni, may his secret be sanctified, related from Abu Basir, who said: Abu Ja'far, peace be upon him, said: Shall I not read to you the bequest of Fatima, peace be upon her? He said: I said: Yes indeed. So he brought out a casket [29] or a chest, and brought out of it a document, and read it: In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. This is what Fatima, the daughter of Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may He bless him and his Family, has charged. She charged her seven gardens — al-'Awaf, and al-Dalal, and al-Burqa, and al-Maythab, and al-Husna, and al-Safiya, and what belonged to Umm Ibrahim — to 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him; and if 'Ali, peace be upon him, passes away, then to al-Hasan; and if al-Hasan passes away, then to al-Husayn; and if al-Husayn passes away, then to the eldest of my children. God bears witness to that, and al-Miqdad b. al-Aswad and al-Zubayr b. al-'Awwam; and 'Ali b. Abi Talib, peace be upon him, wrote it. [30]
188:1: Al-Sayyid Ibn Tawus said in Kashf al-Mahajja, in a discourse of his on the point that the Prophet and the Commander of the Faithful,
188:n26: Naqifa: from naqafa the man's skull — he broke it away from the brain.
188:n27: “And I would show you” — a variant.
189:0: peace be upon them both, were not poor, and that it is not a condition of asceticism that it be accompanied by poverty — in these words: And your grandfather Muhammad, may God bless him and his Family, granted your mother Fatima, peace be upon her, Fadak and al-'Awali among the whole of his grants; and its income, in the report of al-Shaykh 'Abd Allah b. Hammad al-Ansari, was twenty-four thousand dinars every year, and in the report of another, seventy thousand dinars. End of quotation. [31]
189:1: [The length of her stay, peace be upon her, after her father] I say: the sayings differ concerning the length of Fatima's stay, the blessings of God be upon her, after the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and his Family. He who reckons it most says: six months; and he who reckons it least says: forty days. And what I choose is that she stayed after her father, the blessings of God be upon them both and their families, ninety-five days, and was taken on the third of Jumada the Second.
189:2: And Muhammad b. Jarir al-Tabari the Imami related, with a reliable chain, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah, peace be upon him, who said: Fatima, peace be upon her, was taken in Jumada the Second, on Tuesday, three nights having passed of it, in the year eleven of the Hijra. And the cause of her death was that Qunfudh, the freedman of 'Umar, struck her [32] with the hilt of the sword at his command, so that she miscarried Muhsin and fell severely ill from that; and she did not let anyone of those who had harmed her come in upon her — and so on. [33]
189:n32: In the source: lakazaha, which also means he struck her.
